title.zh: 卷三十二 列傳第二十: 崔鑒 崔辯 崔挺
title.en: Volume 32 Biographies 20: Cui Jian, Cui Bian, Cui Ting
title.raw: 卷三十二 列傳第二十: 崔鑒 崔辯 崔挺 Volume 32 Biographies 20: Cui Jian, Cui Bian, Cui Ting

sentences.zh: 崔鑒 崔辯 崔挺

translations.literal: Cui Jian, Cui Bian, Cui Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jian, Cui Bian, and Cui Ting.

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十

translations.literal: Biography number twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 20

sentences.zh: 崔鑒兄孫伯謙崔辯孫士謙士謙子彭士謙弟說說子弘度

translations.literal: Cui Jian's elder brother's grandson Boqian; Cui Bian's grandson Shiqian; Shiqian's son Peng; Shiqian's younger brother Shuo; Shuo's son Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Included in this account are Boqian, grandson of Cui Jian's elder brother; Shiqian, grandson of Cui Bian; Peng, son of Shiqian; Shuo, Shiqian's younger brother; and Hongdu, son of Shuo.

sentences.zh: 崔挺子孝芬孫宣猷曾孫仲方仲方從叔昂挺從子季舒挺族孫暹

translations.literal: Cui Ting's son Xiaofen; grandson Xuanyou; great-grandson Zhongfang; Zhongfang's cousin Ang; Ting's nephew Jishu; Ting's clansman descendant Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Also treated here are Xiaofen, son of Cui Ting; Xuanyou, his grandson; Zhongfang, his great-grandson; Ang, Zhongfang's cousin; Jishu, Ting's nephew; and Xian, a clansman descendant of Ting.

sentences.zh: 崔鑒，字神具，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Cui Jian, styled Shenju, was a native of Anping in Boling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jian, whose style name was Shenju, came from Anping in Boling commandery.

sentences.zh: 六世祖贊，魏尚書僕射。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Zan was Wei Minister of the Works.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back, his ancestor Zan had served as Wei Minister of the Works.

sentences.zh: 五世祖洪，晉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Hong was Jin Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations back, Hong had been Jin Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 曾祖懿，字世茂，仕燕，位秘書監。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yi, styled Shimao, served Yan and held the post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yi, styled Shimao, had served the Yan state as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖遭，字景遇，位钜鹿令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zao, styled Jingyu, held the post of Magistrate of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zao, styled Jingyu, had been magistrate of Julu county.

sentences.zh: 父綽，少孤，學行修明，有名於世。

translations.literal: His father Chuo, orphaned young, was cultivated in learning and conduct and had a name in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chuo lost his parents early, yet through learning and conduct won renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 與范陽盧玄、勃海高允、趙郡李靈等俱被征，尋以母老固辭。

translations.literal: Together with Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, Li Ling of Zhao commandery, and others he was summoned, but soon firmly declined on account of his mother's age.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned along with Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, Li Ling of Zhao commandery, and others, but soon begged off firmly because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 後為郡功曹，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as Commandery Merit Officer and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as commandery merit officer and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 鑒頗有文學，自中書博士轉侍郎，賜爵桐廬縣子。

translations.literal: Jian was fairly accomplished in letters; he went from Erudite of the Secretariat to Attendant, and was granted the enfeoffment of Viscount of Tonglu.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was fairly accomplished in letters. He rose from Erudite of the Secretariat to Attendant and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Tonglu.

sentences.zh: 出為東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out from court as Governor of Eastern Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to serve as governor of Eastern Xu province.

sentences.zh: 鑒欲安新附，人有年老者，表求假以守令，詔從之。

translations.literal: Jian wished to settle the newly attached population; where there were elderly men, he memorialized asking that they be granted acting posts as prefects and magistrates, and an imperial edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to settle the newly attached population, Jian memorialized that elderly men among them be allowed to hold acting prefect and magistrate posts, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 又於州內銅冶為農具，兵人獲利。

translations.literal: He also had copper smelting within the province made into farm tools, which brought profit to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Within the province he also had copper from smelting forged into farm tools, to the profit of the troops.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈青州刺史、安平侯，諡曰康。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Qing province and Marquis of Anping, with the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made governor of Qing province and Marquis of Anping, with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 子合，字貴和，少有時譽，襲爵桐廬子，位終常山太守。

translations.literal: His son He, styled Guihe, had a reputation early in life; he inherited the Tonglu viscounty, and his final office was Administrator of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: His son He, styled Guihe, won early renown, inherited the Tonglu viscounty, and ended his career as administrator of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 長子忻，字伯悅，有世幹。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xin, styled Boyue, had the talent of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xin, styled Boyue, possessed the talent of a whole generation.

sentences.zh: 以鄭儼之甥，累遷兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: As a nephew of Zheng Yan, he was repeatedly promoted until Concurrent Vice Director of the Left of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As Zheng Yan's nephew, he rose repeatedly until he served as concurrent vice director of the left in the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，遇害河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he met his death at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 追贈殿中尚書、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Palace and Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made director of the palace and governor of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 忻弟仲哲，早喪所生，為祖母宋氏所養。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brother Zhongzhe lost his birth mother early and was reared by his grandmother, Lady Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's younger brother Zhongzhe lost his birth mother early and was raised by his grandmother, Lady Song.

sentences.zh: 六歲，宋亡，啼慕不止，見者悲之。

translations.literal: At age six, when Lady Song died, he wept and longed for her without cease; those who saw it were moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he was six and Lady Song died, he wept and mourned her without cease, and all who saw him were moved.

sentences.zh: 性恢達，常以將略自許。

translations.literal: By nature he was broad-minded and often boasted of his military plans.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was open and bold, and often prided himself on his military plans.

sentences.zh: 以軍功賜爵安平縣男。

translations.literal: For military merit he was granted the rank of Baron of Anping county.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was granted the rank of baron of Anping county.

sentences.zh: 及父康于燕被圍，泣訴朝廷，遂除別將，與都督元譚赴援，戰歿。

translations.literal: When his father Kang was besieged in Yan, he wept and appealed to the court; he was thereupon appointed Separate General and went with the Commander Yuan Tan to rescue him, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Kang was besieged in Yan, he wept and appealed to the court, was appointed separate general, and marched with the commander Yuan Tan to the relief, where he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 子長瑜，位至開府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Changyu reached the post of Army Aide in the Secretariat of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changyu rose to army aide in the secretariat of the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 長瑜子子樞，學涉好文詞，經辯有才幹。

translations.literal: Changyu's son Zishu was broadly learned, fond of literary composition, skilled in disputation, and talented in administration.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu's son Zishu was broadly learned, loved literary composition, excelled in debate, and had administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，位考功郎中，參議五禮，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: He served Qi, holding the post of Bureau Chief in the Ministry of Personnel, taking part in deliberations on the Five Rites, and awaiting edicts at the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi service he was bureau chief in the Ministry of Personnel, joined deliberations on the five rites, and awaited edicts at the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 兼散騎常侍，聘周。

translations.literal: Concurrently he was Regular Attendant Cavalier and was sent as envoy to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as regular attendant cavalier and was sent on a mission to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 使還，除通直散騎常侍，兼知度支。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was made Regular Attendant Cavalier in Direct Service and concurrently oversaw the revenue bureau.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made regular attendant cavalier in direct service and concurrently oversaw the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 子樞明解世務，所居稱職。

translations.literal: Zishu understood worldly affairs clearly and was called competent in every post he held.
translations.idiomatic: Zishu understood worldly affairs clearly and was regarded as competent in every post he held.

sentences.zh: 因度支有受納風聞，為御史劾，遇赦免。

translations.literal: Because the revenue bureau was rumored to have accepted bribes, he was impeached by the censorate but was spared when an amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: When the revenue bureau was rumored to have taken bribes, the censorate impeached him, but he was spared by an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 仕周，位至上士。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he reached the rank of Senior Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he rose to senior clerk.

sentences.zh: 預尉遲迥事，被誅。

translations.literal: He took part in Yu Chi Tong's affair and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in Yu Chi Tong's rising and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 子樞次弟子端，亦有才幹，而文藝為優。

translations.literal: Zishu's next younger brother Duan also had talent and ability, but his literary accomplishment was superior.
translations.idiomatic: Zishu's next younger brother Duan was also talented and capable, yet excelled in literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 曆殿中侍御史，卒于通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as Palace Attendant Censor and died while holding the post of Regular Attendant Cavalier in Direct Service.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as palace attendant censor and died while regular attendant cavalier in direct service.

sentences.zh: 子端弟子博，武平末，為河陽道行台郎。

translations.literal: Duan's nephew Bo, at the end of Wuping, was clerk on the Heyang circuit headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: Duan's nephew Bo, at the end of the Wuping era, was clerk on the Heyang circuit headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇末，卒于泗州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang in Sui he died while Administrator of Si province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Sui's Kaihuang era he died as administrator of Si province.

sentences.zh: 子博弟子發，有文才，武平末，秘書郎，修起居注。

translations.literal: Bo's nephew Fa had literary talent; at the end of Wuping he was Secretariat Gentleman and revised the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's nephew Fa had literary talent; at the end of Wuping he was secretariat gentleman and revised the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為秦王文學，卒于國子博士。

translations.literal: Serving Sui as literary aide to the Prince of Qin, he died while Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui service he was literary aide to the Prince of Qin and died as erudite of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 長瑜弟叔瓚，頗有學識，性好直言。

translations.literal: Changyu's younger brother Shuguan was quite learned and by nature loved to speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu's younger brother Shuguan was quite learned and by nature loved blunt speech.

sentences.zh: 其妻即齊昭信皇后姊也，文宣擢為魏尹丞。

translations.literal: His wife was the elder sister of the Qi empress of Zhaoxin, and Emperor Wenxuan promoted him to Vice Director of the Wei metropolitan magistracy.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was elder sister to the Qi empress of Zhaoxin, and Emperor Wenxuan promoted him to vice director of the Wei metropolitan magistracy.

sentences.zh: 屬蝗蟲為災，帝以問叔瓚。

translations.literal: When locusts became a calamity, the emperor questioned Shuguan about it.
translations.idiomatic: When locusts brought disaster, the emperor questioned Shuguan about it.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「案《漢書五行志》：'土功不時，蝗蟲作厲。

translations.literal: He replied: "According to the 'Treatise on the Five Phases' in the Book of Han: 'When earthworks are untimely, locusts arise as a scourge.'"
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "According to the Treatise on the Five Phases in the Book of Han: 'When earthworks are untimely, locusts arise as a scourge.'"

sentences.zh: '當今外築長城，內興三台，故致此災。

translations.literal: "At present, externally they build the Long Wall and internally they raise the Three Platforms—hence this calamity has occurred."
translations.idiomatic: "At present the Long Wall is built outside and the Three Platforms are raised within—hence this disaster."

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，令左右毆之，又擢其發，以溷汁沃其頭，曳以出，由是廢頓久之。

translations.literal: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered his attendants to beat him; they also seized his hair, poured night-soil on his head, and dragged him out; because of this he was prostrated in illness for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, ordered attendants to beat him, seized his hair, poured night-soil over his head, and had him dragged out; he was laid low by illness for a long time thereafter.

sentences.zh: 後卒于陽平太守，贈本州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he died while Administrator of Yangping and was posthumously made Governor of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: He later died as administrator of Yangping and was posthumously made governor of his home province.

sentences.zh: 仲弟叔彥，位撫軍。

translations.literal: His second younger brother Shuyan held the post of Pacification General.
translations.idiomatic: His second younger brother Shuyan served as pacification general.

sentences.zh: 叔彥弟季通，位司農少卿。

translations.literal: Shuyan's younger brother Jitong held the post of Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan's younger brother Jitong was vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 季通子德立，好學，愛屬文，預撰《御覽》，位濟州別駕。

translations.literal: Jitong's son Deli loved learning, delighted in literary composition, took part in compiling the Imperial Overview, and held the post of Assistant Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Jitong's son Deli loved learning, delighted in composition, helped compile the Imperial Overview, and served as assistant governor of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 季通弟季良，風望閒雅，位太學博士，以征討功，賜爵蒲陰縣子，累遷太尉長史。

translations.literal: Jitong's younger brother Jiliang had an easy, elegant reputation; he was Erudite of the Imperial University, and for merit on campaign was granted the enfeoffment of Viscount of Puyin, and was repeatedly promoted until Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Jitong's younger brother Jiliang had an easy, elegant reputation, served as erudite of the imperial university, and for campaign merit was enfeoffed viscount of Puyin and rose to chief clerk of the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 及康東還鄉，季良亦去職歸養。

translations.literal: When Kang returned east to his home district, Jiliang also left office to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang returned east to his home district, Jiliang also left office to go home and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 後位中軍將軍、光祿大夫，先康卒於家，贈尚書右僕射，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Later he held the posts of General of the Central Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; he died at home before Kang and was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Right and given the posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as general of the central army and grand master of splendid happiness, died at home before Kang, and was posthumously made vice minister of the right with the posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 康弟習，字貴禮，有世用，卒于河東太守，贈并州刺史。

translations.literal: Kang's younger brother Xi, styled Guili, was useful to his generation; he died while Administrator of Hedong and was posthumously made Governor of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's younger brother Xi, styled Guili, was useful to his generation; he died as administrator of Hedong and was posthumously made governor of Bing province.

sentences.zh: 鑒兄舣，字洛祖，行博陵太守。

translations.literal: Jian's elder brother Yi, styled Luozu, acted as Administrator of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's elder brother Yi, styled Luozu, served as acting administrator of Boling.

sentences.zh: 舣子文業，中書郎、钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: Yi's son Wenye was Attendant of the Secretariat and Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Wenye was attendant of the secretariat and administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 文業子伯謙。

translations.literal: Wenye's son Boqian.
translations.idiomatic: Wenye's son was Boqian.

sentences.zh: 伯謙字士遜，貧居養母。

translations.literal: Boqian, styled Shixun, lived in poverty while supporting his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Boqian, styled Shixun, lived in poverty while caring for his mother.

sentences.zh: 齊神武召補相府兼功曹，稱之曰：「崔伯謙清直奉公，真良佐也。

translations.literal: Qi Emperor Shenwu summoned him to fill the concurrent merit-officer post in the Chancellor's office and praised him, saying: "Cui Boqian is pure, upright, and devoted to the public good—a true fine assistant."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenwu of Qi summoned him to the chancellor's office as concurrent merit officer and praised him: "Cui Boqian is pure, upright, and devoted to the public good—a true fine assistant."

sentences.zh: 」轉七兵、殿中、左戶三曹郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as Bureau Chief in the Seventh Arms, Palace, and Left Household offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to bureau chief in the seventh arms, palace, and left household offices.

sentences.zh: 弟仲讓為北豫州司馬，與高慎同叛。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhongrang was Northern Yu province's army aide and rebelled together with Gao Shen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhongrang was army aide of Northern Yu province and rebelled with Gao Shen.

sentences.zh: 坐免官。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: On that account he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後曆瀛州別駕、京畿司馬。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Assistant Governor of Ying province and Metropolitan Commandery Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: He later served successively as assistant governor of Ying province and metropolitan commandery army aide.

sentences.zh: 文襄將之晉陽，勞之曰：「卿聘足瀛部，已著康歌。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang was about to go to Jinyang, he encouraged Boqian, saying: "Your service has been enough for the Ying region; you have already won songs of peace."
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang was about to go to Jinyang, he encouraged Boqian: "Your service has been enough for the Ying region—you have already won songs of peace."

sentences.zh: 督府務總，是用相授。

translations.literal: "The headquarters' affairs are now entrusted to you in total—therefore I confer this charge on you."
translations.idiomatic: "The headquarters' affairs are now entrusted to you in full—therefore I confer this charge."

sentences.zh: 」臨別，又馬上執手曰：「執子之手，與子偕老，卿宜深體此情。

translations.literal: At parting he again took his hand on horseback and said: "'I hold your hand and grow old with you'—you should deeply embody this feeling."
translations.idiomatic: At parting he again took his hand from horseback: "'I hold your hand and grow old with you'—you should take that feeling to heart."

sentences.zh: 」族弟暹當時寵要，伯謙與之舊寮同門，非吉凶未嘗造請，以雅道自居。

translations.literal: His clansman Xian was then in favor and power; Boqian had been an old colleague and schoolmate with him, yet except for occasions of fortune or misfortune he never paid a visit, holding himself to the standards of refined conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Xian was then in favor and power; Boqian had been an old colleague and schoolmate, yet except for fortune or misfortune he never called on him, holding himself to refined standards.

sentences.zh: 天保初，除濟北太守，恩信大行，富者禁其奢侈，貧者勸課周給。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was made Administrator of Jibei; his favor and trust spread widely; the rich he restrained from luxury and the poor he urged through instruction and relief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was made administrator of Jibei; favor and trust spread widely—the rich he restrained from luxury, the poor he urged on with instruction and relief.

sentences.zh: 縣公田多沃壤，伯謙咸易之以給人。

translations.literal: The commandery's public fields were mostly fertile soil; Boqian exchanged them all to give to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery's public fields were mostly fertile; Boqian exchanged them all to give to the people.

sentences.zh: 又改鞭，用熟皮為之，不忍見血，示恥而已。

translations.literal: He also changed the whip, making it of softened leather, unwilling to see blood—shame alone was the point.
translations.idiomatic: He also changed the whip to softened leather, unwilling to draw blood—shame alone was the aim.

sentences.zh: 朝貴行過郡境，問人太守政何似？

translations.literal: When court nobles passed through the commandery, they asked people what the administrator's government was like.
translations.idiomatic: When court nobles passed through the commandery they asked what the administrator's government was like.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「府君恩化，古者所無。

translations.literal: They replied: "The prefect's favor and transformation are without precedent in antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: They replied: "The prefect's favor and transformation are without precedent in antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」誦人為歌曰：「崔府君，能臨政。

translations.literal: People sang of him: "Prefect Cui can govern well."
translations.idiomatic: People sang of him: "Prefect Cui can govern well."

sentences.zh: 退田易鞭布威德，人無爭。

translations.literal: "Returning fields, changing the whip, spreading authority and virtue—among the people there is no strife."
translations.idiomatic: "Returning fields, changing the whip, spreading authority and virtue—among the people there is no strife."

sentences.zh: 」客曰：「既稱恩化，何因復威？

translations.literal: The visitor said: "If you call it favor and transformation, why also authority?"
translations.idiomatic: The visitor said: "If you call it favor and transformation, why also authority?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「長吏憚其威嚴，人庶蒙其恩惠，故兼言之。

translations.literal: They replied: "The chief officials fear his stern authority, while the common people receive his favor and kindness—therefore both are mentioned together."
translations.idiomatic: They replied: "Chief officials fear his stern authority while the common people receive his kindness—therefore both are mentioned."

sentences.zh: 」以相府舊寮，例有加授，征赴鄴。

translations.literal: As an old colleague of the chancellor's office, by precedent he received an added appointment and was summoned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: As an old colleague of the chancellor's office, by precedent he received an added appointment and was summoned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 百姓號泣遮道，數日不得前。

translations.literal: The common people wept and blocked the road; for days he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The common people wept and blocked the road; for days he could not advance.

sentences.zh: 以弟仲讓在關中，不復居內任，除南钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: Because his younger brother Zhongrang was in Guanzhong, he no longer held an inner appointment and was made Administrator of Southern Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Because his younger brother Zhongrang was in Guanzhong, he no longer held an inner appointment and was made administrator of southern Julu.

sentences.zh: 下車導以禮讓，豪族皆改心整肅。

translations.literal: On taking office he guided them with ritual and deference, and the powerful clans all changed heart and became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he guided them with ritual and deference, and the powerful clans all reformed and became orderly.

sentences.zh: 事無巨細，必自親覽。

translations.literal: In affairs great and small he always examined them personally.
translations.idiomatic: In affairs great and small he always examined them personally.

sentences.zh: 在縣有貧弱未理者，皆曰「我自告白須公，不慮不決」。

translations.literal: Where in the county there were poor and weak persons whose cases were unsettled, all said, "I will report it myself to the prefect—I do not worry that it will not be decided."
translations.idiomatic: Where poor and weak persons in the county had unsettled cases, all said, "I will report it myself to the prefect—I do not worry it will go undecided."

sentences.zh: 在郡七年，獄無停囚。

translations.literal: In seven years in the commandery there were no prisoners held in jail.
translations.idiomatic: In seven years in the commandery there were no prisoners held in jail.

sentences.zh: 每有大使巡察，恆處上第。

translations.literal: Whenever great envoys came on inspection tours, he was always ranked in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever great envoys came on inspection, he was always ranked in the top grade.

sentences.zh: 徵拜銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Grand Master with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed grand master with silver seal and blue ribbon.

sentences.zh: 伯謙少時讀經、史，晚年好《老》、《莊》，容止儼然無慍色，親賓至，則置酒相娛。

translations.literal: In youth Boqian read the classics and histories; in later years he delighted in the Laozi and Zhuangzi; his bearing was always grave without anger, and when kin and guests came he set out wine for their pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Boqian read the classics and histories; in later years he delighted in the Laozi and Zhuangzi; his bearing was always grave without anger, and when kin and guests came he set out wine for their pleasure.

sentences.zh: 清言不及俗事，士大夫以為儀錶。

translations.literal: In pure talk he did not touch on vulgar affairs, and the scholar-officials took him as a model.
translations.idiomatic: In pure talk he did not touch vulgar affairs, and scholar-officials took him as a model.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈南充州刺史，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Governor of Nanchong and given the posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made governor of Nanchong with the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 伯謙弟仲讓，仕西魏，位至鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: Boqian's younger brother Zhongrang served Western Wei and reached the post of Vice Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Relations.
translations.idiomatic: Boqian's younger brother Zhongrang served Western Wei and rose to vice minister of the court for diplomatic relations.

sentences.zh: 崔辯，字神通，鑒之從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Cui Bian, styled Shentong, was a younger cousin of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bian, styled Shentong, was Jian's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 祖琨，字景龍，行本郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kun, styled Jinglong, acted as Administrator of his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kun, styled Jinglong, had acted as administrator of his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 父經，贈兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jing was posthumously made Governor of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing was posthumously made governor of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 辯學涉經史，風儀整峻，獻文徵拜中書博士、武邑太守。

translations.literal: Bian was broadly learned in the classics and histories, with a stern, lofty bearing; Emperor Xianwen summoned him as Erudite of the Secretariat and Administrator of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was broadly learned in classics and histories, with stern, lofty bearing; Emperor Xianwen summoned him as erudite of the secretariat and administrator of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 政事之餘，專以勸學。

translations.literal: Beyond administrative duties he devoted himself solely to encouraging learning.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond administrative duties he devoted himself solely to encouraging learning.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安南將軍、定州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Ding province, with the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made general who pacifies the south and governor of Ding province, with the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 長子景俊，鯁正有高風，好古博涉，以經明行修，徵拜中書博士。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jingjun was upright and had lofty integrity, loved antiquity and was broadly learned, and for clarity in the classics and cultivation in conduct was summoned as Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jingjun was upright with lofty integrity, loved antiquity and was broadly learned, and for clarity in the classics and cultivated conduct was summoned as erudite of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 曆侍御史、主文中散。

translations.literal: He successively served as Attending Censor and Principal Clerk for Drafting in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as attending censor and principal clerk for drafting in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝文賜名為逸。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen bestowed on him the name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen bestowed on him the name Yi.

sentences.zh: 後為員外散騎侍郎，與著作郎韓興宗參定朝儀。

translations.literal: Later he served as Extra Attendant Cavalier and, with Drafting Gentleman Han Xingzong, took part in fixing the court ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as extra attendant cavalier and, with drafting gentleman Han Xingzong, helped fix the court ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 雅為孝文所知重，遷國子博士。

translations.literal: He was always known and valued by Emperor Xiaowen and was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen always knew and valued him, and promoted him to erudite of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 每有公事，逸常被詔獨進，博士特命自逸始。

translations.literal: Whenever there was public business, Yi was often ordered to enter alone; the special summons of erudites began with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there was public business, Yi was often summoned to enter alone—the special summons of erudites began with him.

sentences.zh: 轉通直散騎常侍、廷尉少卿，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant Cavalier in Direct Service and Vice Minister of Justice, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regular attendant cavalier in direct service and vice minister of justice, then died.

sentences.zh: 子巨倫，字孝宗，幼孤。

translations.literal: His son Julun, styled Xiaozong, was orphaned young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Julun, styled Xiaozong, lost his father while still young.

sentences.zh: 及長，曆涉經史，有文學武藝。

translations.literal: When grown, he ranged through the classics and histories and had both literary and martial accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he ranged through classics and histories and possessed both literary and martial accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 叔楷為殷州，巨倫仍為長史、北道別將。

translations.literal: His uncle Kai was governor of Yin province; Julun served as chief clerk and separate general on the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Kai governed Yin province; Julun served as his chief clerk and separate general on the northern route.

sentences.zh: 在州陷賊，斂恤存亡，為賊所義。

translations.literal: When the province fell to bandits, he gathered and relieved the living and dead, and the bandits honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the province fell to bandits, he gathered and relieved survivors and the dead alike, and the bandits honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 葛榮聞其才名，欲用為黃門郎，巨倫心惡之。

translations.literal: Ge Rong heard of his talent and fame and wished to use him as Attendant of the Yellow Gate; Julun detested this in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong heard of his talent and wished to make him attendant of the yellow gate; Julun detested the idea.

sentences.zh: 至五月五日，會集官寮，令巨倫贈詩。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fifth month he gathered his official staff and ordered Julun to present a poem.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fifth month he gathered his officials and ordered Julun to present a poem.

sentences.zh: 巨倫乃曰：「五月五日時，天氣已大熱，狗便呀欲死，牛復喘吐舌。

translations.literal: Julun then said: "On the fifth day of the fifth month the weather is already very hot; dogs begin to pant as though dying, and oxen also gasp with tongues out."
translations.idiomatic: Julun said: "On the fifth day of the fifth month the weather is already fiercely hot; dogs pant as though dying, and oxen gasp with their tongues out."

sentences.zh: 」以此自晦，獲免。

translations.literal: By this he concealed his talent and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: By this he concealed his talent and escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 結死士，夜中南走，逢賊，俱恐不濟。

translations.literal: He gathered men sworn to die, fled south by night, met bandits, and all feared they would not survive.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered men sworn to die, fled south by night, met bandits, and all feared they would not survive.

sentences.zh: 巨倫曰：「甯南死一寸，豈北生一尺！

translations.literal: Julun said: "Better die an inch to the south than live a foot to the north!"
translations.idiomatic: Julun said: "Better die an inch to the south than live a foot to the north!"

sentences.zh: 」便欺賊曰：「吾受敕而行。

translations.literal: He then deceived the bandits, saying: "I am acting on imperial orders."
translations.idiomatic: He then deceived the bandits: "I am acting on imperial orders."

sentences.zh: 」賊爇火觀敕，火未然。

translations.literal: The bandits lit a fire to view the edict, but the fire had not yet caught.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits lit a fire to view the edict, but the fire had not yet caught.

sentences.zh: 巨倫手刃賊十餘人，賊乃四潰，得馬數匹。

translations.literal: Julun personally killed more than ten bandits; the bandits then broke in four directions and fled, and he obtained several horses.
translations.idiomatic: Julun personally killed more than ten bandits; they broke and fled in all directions, and he obtained several horses.

sentences.zh: 夜陰失道，唯看佛塔戶而行。

translations.literal: In the dark of night they lost the road and could only go by watching the doors of pagodas.
translations.idiomatic: In the dark of night they lost the road and could only go by watching pagoda doors.

sentences.zh: 到洛陽，持節別將北討。

translations.literal: Reaching Luoyang, he held credentials as separate general on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Luoyang, he held credentials as separate general on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 初，楷喪之始，巨倫收殯倉卒，事不周固；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Kai first died, Julun had buried him in haste and the arrangements were not thorough;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Kai first died, Julun had buried him in haste and the arrangements were not thorough;

sentences.zh: 至是遂偷路改殯，並竊家口以歸。

translations.literal: now he secretly changed the burial by another route and also stole away the household to return home.
translations.idiomatic: now he secretly changed the burial by another route and also stole away the household to return home.

sentences.zh: 尋授國子博士。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed erudite of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，除東濮陽太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, Julun was made Administrator of Eastern Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, Julun was made administrator of eastern Puyang.

sentences.zh: 時河北紛梗，人避賊，多入郡界。

translations.literal: At that time Hebei was in turmoil and people fleeing bandits often entered the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hebei was in turmoil and people fleeing bandits often entered the commandery.

sentences.zh: 歲儉饑乏，巨倫傾資贍恤，務相全濟。

translations.literal: In a year of famine and hunger Julun spent his whole fortune on relief, striving to save everyone.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine he spent his whole fortune on relief, striving to save everyone.

sentences.zh: 時類高之。

translations.literal: People at the time greatly admired this.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time greatly admired this.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，據郡不從，莊帝還宮，封漁陽縣男。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang and seized the commandery without submitting, Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace and enfeoffed Julun as Baron of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang and held the commandery without submitting, Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace and enfeoffed Julun as baron of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 後除光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒，子子武襲。

translations.literal: When he died his son Ziwu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his son Ziwu inherited.

sentences.zh: 初，巨倫有姊，明慧有才行。

translations.literal: Earlier Julun had an elder sister, bright and talented in ability and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Julun had an elder sister, bright and talented in ability and conduct.

sentences.zh: 因患眇一目，內外親族，莫有求者。

translations.literal: Because of an illness she lost sight in one eye, and neither kin within nor without sought her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness she lost sight in one eye, and neither kin within nor without sought her in marriage.

sentences.zh: 其家議欲下嫁之。

translations.literal: Her family discussed marrying her beneath her station.
translations.idiomatic: Her family discussed marrying her beneath her station.

sentences.zh: 巨倫姑，趙國李叔胤之妻，聞而悲感曰：「吾兄盛德，不幸早世，豈令此女，屈事卑族！

translations.literal: Julun's aunt, wife of Li Shuyin of Zhao, heard this and said in grief: "My elder brother's great virtue met untimely death—how can we let this girl bow to a mean clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Julun's aunt, wife of Li Shuyin of Zhao, heard and said in grief: "My brother's great virtue met untimely death—how can we let this girl bow to a mean clan!"

sentences.zh: 」乃為子翼納之。

translations.literal: She thereupon had her son Yi take her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: She thereupon had her son Yi take her in marriage.

sentences.zh: 時人歎其義識。

translations.literal: People of the time praised her righteous understanding.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time praised her righteous understanding.

sentences.zh: 逸弟模，字叔軌。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Mo, styled Shugui.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Mo, styled Shugui.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，圍亦如之。

translations.literal: His height was eight chi and his girth was the same.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall and was as broad around as he was tall.

sentences.zh: 出後其叔，雅有志度。

translations.literal: He was adopted out to his uncle and by nature had resolve and measure.
translations.idiomatic: He was adopted out to his uncle and by nature had resolve and measure.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤討關、隴，引為西征別將，屢有戰功，封槐里縣伯。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned against Guan and Long he took Mo as separate general on the western expedition; Mo repeatedly won merit in battle and was enfeoffed as Baron of Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned against Guan and Long he took Mo as separate general on the western expedition; Mo repeatedly won merit and was enfeoffed baron of Huaili.

sentences.zh: 後行岐州事，擊賊，歿於陣。

translations.literal: Later he acted as administrator of Qi province, struck bandits, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later he acted as administrator of Qi province, struck bandits, and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、都督、相州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was posthumously made General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commander, and Governor of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he was posthumously made general of agile cavalry, equal in honor to the three dukes, commander, and governor of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 模弟楷。

translations.literal: Mo's younger brother Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's younger brother was Kai.

sentences.zh: 楷字季則，為廣平王懷文學。

translations.literal: Kai, styled Jize, was literary aide to Prince Huai of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, styled Jize, was literary aide to Prince Huai of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 正始中，以王國官非其人，多被戮，唯楷與楊昱以數諫諍獲免。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era, because princely household officials were not the right men, many were executed; only Kai and Yang Yu were spared through repeated remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era, because princely household officials were unfit, many were executed; only Kai and Yang Yu were spared through repeated remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 後為太子中舍人、左中郎將。

translations.literal: Later he served as Household Aide to the Heir Apparent and Left Central General.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as household aide to the heir apparent and left central general.

sentences.zh: 以党附高肇，為中尉所劾。

translations.literal: For faction with Gao Zhao he was impeached by the chief commandant.
translations.idiomatic: For faction with Gao Zhao he was impeached by the chief commandant.

sentences.zh: 事在《高聰傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is in the biography of Gao Cong.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is told in the biography of Gao Cong.

sentences.zh: 楷性嚴烈，能摧挫豪強，時人語曰：「莫鋋鬱買反彳解孤楷反，付崔楷。

translations.literal: Kai's nature was stern and fierce; he could break the powerful, and people of the time said: "Do not file down Yu and buy the rebel 'Duke Jie' Kai's rebellion—hand it to Cui Kai."
translations.idiomatic: Kai's nature was stern and fierce; he could break the powerful, and people said: "Do not file down Yu and buy Duke Jie's rebellion—hand it to Cui Kai."

sentences.zh: 」時冀、定數州頻遭水害，楷上疏導之便宜，事遂施行。

translations.literal: At that time several provinces including Ji and Ding had suffered repeated flood damage; Kai memorialized on measures that would be expedient, and the matter was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ji, Ding, and other provinces had suffered repeated floods; Kai memorialized on expedient measures and they were carried out.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，置殷州，以楷為刺史，加後將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang Yin province was established and Kai was made its governor with the additional title Rear General.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaochang Yin province was established and Kai was made governor with the additional title rear general.

sentences.zh: 楷將之州，人咸勸單身述職。

translations.literal: When Kai was about to go to the province, people all urged him to take office alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Kai was about to go to the province, people urged him to take office alone.

sentences.zh: 楷曰：「單身赴任，朝廷謂吾有進退之計，將士又誰肯固志？

translations.literal: Kai said: "If I go to my post alone, the court will think I have plans to advance or retreat, and which soldier will then hold firm in resolve?"
translations.idiomatic: Kai said: "If I go alone, the court will think I plan to advance or retreat, and which soldier will hold firm?"

sentences.zh: 」遂闔家赴州。

translations.literal: He thereupon took his whole household to the province.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon took his whole household to the province.

sentences.zh: 賊勢已逼，或勸減小弱以避之，乃遣第四女、第三男夜出。

translations.literal: Bandit power already pressed close; some urged sending away the weak and small to avoid them, and he sent his fourth daughter and third son out by night.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits already pressed close; some urged sending away the weak, and he sent his fourth daughter and third son out by night.

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「一朝送免兒女，將謂吾心不固。

translations.literal: Then he said: "In one morning to send away my children—people will say my heart is not firm."
translations.idiomatic: Then he said: "To send away my children in one morning—people will say my heart is not firm."

sentences.zh: 」遂命追還。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered them brought back.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon ordered them brought back.

sentences.zh: 及賊來攻，楷率力拒抗，莫不爭奪，咸稱崔公尚不惜百口，吾等何愛一身？

translations.literal: When bandits came to attack, Kai led resistance with all his strength; none failed to strive, and all said, "Lord Cui does not spare a hundred mouths—how can we love a single body?"
translations.idiomatic: When bandits attacked, Kai led resistance; all strove, saying, "Lord Cui does not spare a hundred mouths—how can we love one body?"

sentences.zh: 力竭城陷，楷執節不屈，賊遂害之。

translations.literal: Strength exhausted, the city fell; Kai held his credentials and would not bow, and the bandits killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Strength exhausted, the city fell; Kai held his credentials and would not bow, and the bandits killed him.

sentences.zh: 楷兄弟父子並死王事，朝野傷歎焉。

translations.literal: Kai's brothers, sons, and father all died in the king's service; court and countryside mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's brothers, sons, and father all died in the king's service; court and countryside mourned.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、鎮軍將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made attendant, general who pacifies the army, and governor of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，又特贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、都督、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was specially posthumously made General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commander, and Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he was specially posthumously made general of agile cavalry, equal in honor to the three dukes, commander, and governor of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 長子士元，沈雅有學尚。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shiyuan was deep, refined, and devoted to learning.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shiyuan was deep, refined, and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 州陷，戰沒，贈平州刺史。

translations.literal: When the province fell he died in battle and was posthumously made Governor of Ping province.
translations.idiomatic: When the province fell he died in battle and was posthumously made governor of Ping province.

sentences.zh: 子育王，少以器幹稱，仕齊至起部郎。

translations.literal: His son Yuwang, young, was known for capacity and achievement and in Qi service reached Bureau Chief in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuwang, known young for capacity, in Qi reached bureau chief in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 子文豹，字蔚，少有文才，本州大中正。

translations.literal: His son Wenbao, styled Wei, had literary talent young and was chief rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenbao, styled Wei, had literary talent young and was chief rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 士元弟士謙。

translations.literal: Shiyuan's younger brother Shiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan's younger brother was Shiqian.

sentences.zh: 士謙，孝昌初解褐著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Shiqian, at the beginning of Xiaochang, left the cloth and became Assistant Drafting in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian, at the beginning of Xiaochang, left the cloth and became assistant drafting in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後賀拔勝出鎮荊州，以士謙為行台左丞。

translations.literal: Later Heba Sheng went out to garrison Jing province and made Shiqian left aide on the headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: Later Heba Sheng went out to garrison Jing province and made Shiqian left aide on the headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，士謙勸勝倍道兼行，謁帝關右，勝不能用。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Shiqian urged Sheng to march day and night, double his pace, and call on the emperor in Guanzhong; Sheng would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Shiqian urged Sheng to march day and night and call on the emperor in Guanzhong; Sheng would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 州人劉誕引侯景軍奄至，勝與戰，敗績，遂奔梁。

translations.literal: A man of the province, Liu Yan, led Hou Jing's army in a sudden attack; Sheng fought them, was defeated, and fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan of the province led Hou Jing's army in a sudden attack; Sheng fought, was defeated, and fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 士謙與俱行。

translations.literal: Shiqian went with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian went with him.

sentences.zh: 及至梁，每乞師赴援。

translations.literal: When they reached Liang he repeatedly begged troops to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Liang he repeatedly begged for troops to rescue.

sentences.zh: 梁武雖不為出軍，而嘉勝等志節，並許其還國。

translations.literal: Although Emperor Wu of Liang did not send an army, he admired Sheng and the others for their integrity and all permitted their return home.
translations.idiomatic: Although Emperor Wu of Liang did not send troops, he admired their integrity and permitted all to return home.

sentences.zh: 乃令士謙先，且通鄰好。

translations.literal: He then had Shiqian go first to open friendly relations with neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Shiqian go first to open friendly relations with neighbors.

sentences.zh: 周文素聞其名，甚禮之，賜爵千乘縣男。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou had long heard his name and treated him with great courtesy, granting him the rank of Baron of Qiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou had long heard his name and treated him with great courtesy, granting him baron of Qiancheng.

sentences.zh: 及勝至，拜太師長史，以功進爵為子，拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: When Sheng arrived, Shiqian was made chief clerk to the Grand Preceptor; for merit his rank was raised to viscount and he was made Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng arrived, Shiqian was made chief clerk to the grand preceptor; for merit his rank rose to viscount and he was made vice director of the right.

sentences.zh: 從周文解洛陽圍，經河橋戰，加定州大中正、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wen of Zhou in raising the siege of Luoyang, he fought at Heqiao and was made chief rectifier of Ding province and Governor of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Wen in raising the siege of Luoyang, he fought at Heqiao and was made chief rectifier of Ding and governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 又破柳仲禮於隨郡，討李遷哲于魏興，並有功，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、直州刺史。

translations.literal: He also defeated Liu Zhongli at Sui commandery and campaigned against Li Qianzhe at Weixing, all with merit, and was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Marshal with the same honors as the Three Dukes, and Governor of Zhi province.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Liu Zhongli at Sui and campaigned against Li Qianzhe at Weixing with merit, and was promoted to general of agile cavalry, grand marshal with the same honors as the three dukes, and governor of Zhi.

sentences.zh: 賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: He was granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 恭帝初，轉利州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Gongdi reign he was transferred to Governor of Li province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Gongdi reign he was transferred to governor of Li province.

sentences.zh: 士謙性明悟，深曉政術，吏人畏而愛之。

translations.literal: Shiqian's nature was clear and perceptive; he deeply understood the art of government, and clerks and people both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian was clear and perceptive, deeply understood government, and clerks and people both feared and loved him.

sentences.zh: 周保定二年，遷總管、安州刺史，加大將軍，進爵武康郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding of Zhou he was made Commander and Governor of An province with the added title Great General and advanced to Duke of Wukang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou's second year of Baoding he was made commander and governor of An with the added title great general and advanced to duke of Wukang commandery.

sentences.zh: 天和中，授江陵總管、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era he was made Commander of Jiangling and Governor of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianhe era he was made commander of Jiangling and governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 州既統攝遐長，俗兼夷夏，又南接陳境，東鄰齊寇。

translations.literal: The province commanded a long frontier, its customs mixed barbarian and Chinese, and it bordered Chen to the south and Qi raiders to the east.
translations.idiomatic: The province commanded a long frontier, mixed barbarian and Chinese customs, bordered Chen to the south and Qi raiders to the east.

sentences.zh: 士謙外禦強敵，內撫軍人，風化大行，號稱良牧。

translations.literal: Shiqian outwardly resisted strong enemies and inwardly comforted the troops; transformation spread widely and he was called a fine administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian outwardly resisted strong enemies and inwardly comforted troops; transformation spread widely and he was called a fine administrator.

sentences.zh: 每年考績，常為天下之最，屢有詔褒美焉。

translations.literal: Every year in performance review he was always first in the realm, and edicts repeatedly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Every year in performance review he ranked first in the realm, and edicts repeatedly praised him.

sentences.zh: 士謙隨賀拔勝之在荊州也，雖被親遇，而名位未顯；

translations.literal: When Shiqian followed Heba Sheng in Jing province, though treated with intimacy his name and rank were not yet prominent;
translations.idiomatic: When Shiqian followed Heba Sheng in Jing, though treated intimately his name and rank were not yet prominent;

sentences.zh: 及踐其位，朝野以為榮。

translations.literal: when he stepped into Sheng's position, court and countryside took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: when he stepped into Sheng's position, court and countryside took it as glory.

sentences.zh: 卒於州，闔境痛惜之，立祠堂，四時祭饗。

translations.literal: He died in the province; the whole territory mourned him and erected a shrine with sacrifices in the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the province; the whole territory mourned and erected a shrine with sacrifices in the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 子曠嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kuang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 士謙性至孝，與弟說特相友愛，雖復年位並高，資產皆無私焉。

translations.literal: Shiqian's nature was utmost filial; he and his younger brother Shuo were especially close in friendship; though years and rank both rose high, they kept no private property between them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian was utmost filial and especially close to his younger brother Shuo; though years and rank both rose high, they kept no private property between them.

sentences.zh: 居家嚴肅，曠及說子弘度並奉其遺訓云。

translations.literal: At home he was stern; Kuang and Shuo's son Hongdu all followed his legacy teachings.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was stern; Kuang and Shuo's son Hongdu all followed his legacy teachings.

sentences.zh: 曠少溫雅。

translations.literal: Kuang in youth was gentle and refined.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang in youth was gentle and refined.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位開府儀同大將軍、浙州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he held the posts of Grand Marshal with the same honors as the Three Dukes and Governor of Zhe province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he held grand marshal with the same honors as the three dukes and governed Zhe province.

sentences.zh: 曠弟彭。

translations.literal: Kuang's younger brother Peng.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang's younger brother was Peng.

sentences.zh: 彭字子彭，少孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Peng, styled Zipeng, was orphaned young and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Peng, styled Zipeng, was orphaned young and was known for filial service to his mother.

sentences.zh: 性剛毅，有武略，工騎射，善《周官》、《尚書》，並略通大義。

translations.literal: By nature he was firm and resolute, had military plans, was skilled in mounted archery, and was versed in the Rites of Zhou and the Documents, with some grasp of their larger meaning.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was firm and resolute, had military plans, was skilled in mounted archery, and was versed in the Rites of Zhou and the Documents with some grasp of their larger meaning.

sentences.zh: 仕周，累遷門正上士。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he was repeatedly promoted until Senior Clerk in the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Zhou, he rose repeatedly to senior clerk in the gate office.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為相，周陳王純鎮齊州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chancellor, Prince Chun of Zhou Chen garrisoned Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chancellor, Prince Chun of Zhou Chen garrisoned Qi province.

sentences.zh: 帝恐其為變，遣彭以兩騎征純入朝。

translations.literal: The emperor feared he would rebel and sent Peng with two horsemen to summon Chun to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared rebellion and sent Peng with two horsemen to summon Chun to court.

sentences.zh: 彭未至齊州三十里，因詐病止傳舍，遣人召純。

translations.literal: Peng had not yet reached thirty li from Qi province when he feigned illness and stopped at a post station, sending a man to summon Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Before Peng had come within thirty li of Qi province, he feigned illness and stopped at a post station, then sent someone to summon Chun.

sentences.zh: 純疑有變，多將從騎至彭所。

translations.literal: Chun suspected there was trouble and brought many attendant horsemen to Peng's place.
translations.idiomatic: Chun suspected trouble and came to Peng's lodging with many attendant horsemen.

sentences.zh: 彭請間，因顧騎士執而鎖之。

translations.literal: Peng asked for a private audience, then looking back signaled the knights to seize and shackle him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng asked for a private audience, then signaled his knights to seize Chun and put him in shackles.

sentences.zh: 乃大言曰：「陳王有罪，詔征入朝，左右不得輒動。

translations.literal: Then he spoke loudly: "The Prince of Chen has committed a crime; an edict summons him to court—those on his left and right must not move without permission.
translations.idiomatic: Then he declared loudly, "The Prince of Chen has committed a crime. An edict summons him to court. Those at his side must not stir."

sentences.zh: 」左右愕然而去。

translations.literal: " Chun's attendants stood stunned and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's attendants stood stunned and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 至，拜上儀同。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was appointed Senior Inspector with the Same Honors.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he was appointed senior inspector with the same honors.

sentences.zh: 及踐祚，遷監門郎將，兼領右衛長史，賜爵安陽縣男。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, Peng was transferred to Gate Guard Commandant, concurrently Chief Clerk of the Right Guard, and granted the title Viscount of Anyang county.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Peng was made gate guard commandant and chief clerk of the right guard, and was granted the title viscount of Anyang county.

sentences.zh: 再遷驃騎將軍，恆典宿衛。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Flying Cavalry General, always in charge of night guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to flying cavalry general and always held charge of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 性謹密，在省闥二十餘年，當上，在仗危坐終日，未嘗有墮容。

translations.literal: By nature he was cautious and meticulous; for more than twenty years within the palace gates, on duty at court he sat upright in his post all day, never once showing a slack expression.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was cautious and meticulous. For more than twenty years within the palace gates, whenever on duty at court he sat upright at his post all day and never once showed a slack expression.

sentences.zh: 上每謂曰：「卿當上日，我寢處自安。

translations.literal: The emperor often said to him: "On days you are on duty, I rest at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often told him, "On days when you are on duty, I sleep at ease."

sentences.zh: 」又嘗曰：「卿弓馬固以絕人，頗知學不？

translations.literal: " He also once said: "Your bow and horsemanship are already unmatched—do you know something of learning?
translations.idiomatic: He also once asked, "Your bow and horsemanship are already unmatched. Do you know something of learning?"

sentences.zh: 」彭曰：「臣少愛《周禮》、《尚書》，休沐之暇，不敢廢也。

translations.literal: " Peng said: "Your servant from youth has loved the Rites of Zhou and the Documents; in leisure from official leave, I have not dared neglect them.
translations.idiomatic: Peng replied, "Your servant has loved the Rites of Zhou and the Documents since youth, and in leisure from official leave I have not dared neglect them."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「試為我言之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Try expounding them for me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then try expounding them for me."

sentences.zh: 」彭因說君臣戒慎之義，上稱善。

translations.literal: " Peng then discoursed on the meaning of ruler and minister being vigilant and careful; the emperor praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Peng then discoursed on the duty of ruler and minister to be vigilant and careful, and the emperor praised his words.

sentences.zh: 觀者以為知言。

translations.literal: Those present considered his words insightful.
translations.idiomatic: Those present considered his words insightful.

sentences.zh: 後加上開府，遷備身將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was given Senior Opening Office and promoted to Personal Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was given senior opening office and promoted to personal guard general.

sentences.zh: 上嘗宴達頭可汗使者于武德殿，有鴿鳴于梁上。

translations.literal: The emperor once feasted the emissary of Khan Tatou in Wude Hall; a pigeon cried on a beam.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once feasted the emissary of Khan Tatou in Wude Hall when a pigeon cried on a beam overhead.

sentences.zh: 命彭射之，中，上大悅，賜錢一萬。

translations.literal: He ordered Peng to shoot it; Peng hit it, and the emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed ten thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Peng to shoot it. Peng hit the bird, and the emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed ten thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 及使者反，可汗復遣使請崔將軍一與相見。

translations.literal: When the emissary returned, the khan again sent an emissary requesting one meeting with General Cui.
translations.idiomatic: When the emissary returned, the khan again sent an envoy asking to meet General Cui once.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此必善射聞於虜庭。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This must be because his skill in archery is known in the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This must be because his skill in archery is known in the barbarian court."

sentences.zh: 」遂遣之。

translations.literal: " So he sent Peng.
translations.idiomatic: So he sent Peng.

sentences.zh: 及至，可汗召善射者數十人，因擲肉於野，以集飛鳶，遣其善射者射之，多不中。

translations.literal: When Peng arrived, the khan summoned several dozen skilled archers; he threw meat in the open to gather kites, had his skilled archers shoot at them, and most missed.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng arrived, the khan summoned several dozen skilled archers, threw meat in the open to gather kites, and had his archers shoot at them, but most missed.

sentences.zh: 彭連發數矢，皆應弦而落。

translations.literal: Peng loosed several arrows in succession, and each bird fell as the bowstring sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Peng loosed several arrows in succession, and each bird fell as the bowstring sounded.

sentences.zh: 突厥莫不嘆服。

translations.literal: None of the Turks failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: All the Turks sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，進爵安陽縣公。

translations.literal: At the end of the Renshou era, he was advanced to Duke of Anyang county.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Renshou era, he was advanced to duke of Anyang county.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷左領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Peng was transferred to Grand General of the Left Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Peng was made grand general of the left vanguard.

sentences.zh: 時漢王諒初平，令彭鎮遏山東，復領慈州事。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Liang of Han had just been pacified; Peng was ordered to secure and suppress Shandong and again held charge of Cizhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Liang of Han had just been pacified. Peng was ordered to secure Shandong and again took charge of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈大將軍，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously given the title Great General with the posthumous name Su.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made great general with the posthumous name Su.

sentences.zh: 子寶德嗣。

translations.literal: His son Baode succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baode succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 士謙弟說。

translations.literal: Shiqian's younger brother Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian's younger brother was Shuo.

sentences.zh: 說本名士約。

translations.literal: Shuo's original name was Shiyue.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo's original name was Shiyue.

sentences.zh: 少有氣概，膂力過人，尤工騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he had spirit and boldness; his physical strength surpassed others, and he was especially skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had spirit and boldness, his physical strength surpassed others, and he was especially skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝牧荊州，以為假節、冠軍將軍、防城都督。

translations.literal: When Heba Sheng governed Jing province, Shuo was made Acting Commander, Champion General, and Frontier Defense Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Sheng governed Jing province, Shuo was made acting commander, champion general, and frontier defense commander.

sentences.zh: 又隨奔梁。

translations.literal: He again followed in flight to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed in flight to Liang.

sentences.zh: 復自梁歸西魏。

translations.literal: He returned from Liang to Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He returned from Liang to Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 授武衛將軍、都督，封安昌縣子。

translations.literal: He was appointed Martial Guard General and Commander, enfeoffed as Viscount of Anchang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed martial guard general and commander and enfeoffed as viscount of Anchang county.

sentences.zh: 從周文復弘農，戰沙苑，皆有功，進爵為侯，除京兆郡守。

translations.literal: Following Duke Wen of Zhou he recovered Hongnong; at the battle of Shawei he had merit; he was advanced to marquis and made Administrator of Jingzhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Following Duke Wen of Zhou he recovered Hongnong and fought at Shawei, earning merit in both. He was advanced to marquis and made administrator of Jingzhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 累遷都官尚書、定州大中正，改封安固縣侯；

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Justice, Senior Rectifier of Ding province, and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Angu county;
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to minister of justice and senior rectifier of Ding province, and his enfeoffment was changed to marquis of Angu county;

sentences.zh: 賜姓宇文，並賜名說焉。

translations.literal: he was granted the surname Yuwen and the name Shuo as well.
translations.idiomatic: he was granted the surname Yuwen and the name Shuo.

sentences.zh: 進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，進爵萬年縣公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Flying Cavalry Grand General, Grand Master with Opening Office and Same Honors as the Three Dukes, made Attendant-in-Ordinary, and advanced to Duke of Wannian county.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to flying cavalry grand general and grand master with opening office and the same honors as the three dukes, made attendant-in-ordinary, and advanced to duke of Wannian county.

sentences.zh: 再遷總管、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Commander and Governor of Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to commander and governor of Liang province.

sentences.zh: 說蒞政強毅，百姓畏之。

translations.literal: When Shuo took charge of government he was forceful and resolute; the common people feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuo took charge of government he was forceful and resolute, and the common people feared him.

sentences.zh: 後除使持節、能和中三州、崇德等十三防諸軍事，加授大將軍，改封安平縣公。

translations.literal: Later he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, military commander of Neng, Zhong, and He provinces and the thirteen frontier defenses including Chongde; he was further given Great General and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Anping county.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made bearer of the staff of authority and military commander of Neng, Zhong, and He provinces and the thirteen frontier defenses including Chongde. He was further given the title great general and his enfeoffment was changed to duke of Anping county.

sentences.zh: 建德四年，卒，贈廓、延等五州刺史，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiande he died; posthumously he was given the five provincial governorships of Kuo, Yan, and the rest, with posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiande he died. Posthumously he was given the five governorships of Kuo, Yan, and the rest, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子弘度。

translations.literal: His son was Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 弘度字摩訶衍。

translations.literal: Hongdu, styled Moheyan.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu, styled Moheyan.

sentences.zh: 膂力絕人，儀貌魁岸，須面甚偉，性嚴酷。

translations.literal: His physical strength was unmatched; his bearing was towering, his beard and face extremely imposing, and his nature was severe and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: His physical strength was unmatched. He was towering in bearing, imposing in beard and face, and severe by nature.

sentences.zh: 年十七，周大塚宰宇文護引為親信，累轉大都督。

translations.literal: At seventeen, Grand Preceptor Yuwen Hu of Zhou took him as a confidant; he was repeatedly transferred until Great Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, Grand Preceptor Yuwen Hu of Zhou took him as a confidant, and he rose repeatedly until great commander.

sentences.zh: 時護子中山公訓為蒲州刺史，令弘度從焉。

translations.literal: At the time Hu's son, Duke Zhongshan Xun, was Governor of Pu province; Xun had Hongdu follow him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hu's son, Duke Zhongshan Xun, was governor of Pu province, and Xun had Hongdu follow him.

sentences.zh: 嘗與訓登樓，至上層，去地四五丈，俯臨之。

translations.literal: Once he and Xun ascended a tower; they went to the upper story, four or five zhang above the ground, and looked down.
translations.idiomatic: Once he and Xun ascended a tower to the upper story, four or five zhang above the ground, and looked down.

sentences.zh: 訓曰：「可畏也！

translations.literal: Xun said: "How frightening!
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "How frightening!"

sentences.zh: 」弘度曰：「此何足畏？

translations.literal: " Hongdu said: "What is there to fear in this?
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu said, "What is there to fear in this?"

sentences.zh: 」欻擲下，至地無所損，訓大奇之。

translations.literal: " Suddenly he threw himself down; reaching the ground he was unhurt, and Xun was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he threw himself down. He reached the ground unhurt, and Xun was greatly astonished.

sentences.zh: 後以戰功授儀同。

translations.literal: Later for battlefield merit he was given Inspector with the Same Honors.
translations.idiomatic: Later for battlefield merit he was given inspector with the same honors.

sentences.zh: 從平齊，進上開府、鄴縣公。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Qi, he was advanced to Senior Opening Office and Duke of Ye county.
translations.idiomatic: Following the pacification of Qi, he was advanced to senior opening office and duke of Ye county.

sentences.zh: 尋從汝南公宇文神舉破盧昌期於范陽，鄖公韋孝寬經略淮南。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Duke Yuwen of Runan Shenju in defeating Lu Changqi at Fanyang; Duke Yun Wei Xiaokuan planned strategy in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he followed Duke Yuwen of Runan Shenju in defeating Lu Changqi at Fanyang, while Duke Yun Wei Xiaokuan planned strategy in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 以前後勳進位上大將軍。

translations.literal: For merit before and after he was advanced to Senior Great General.
translations.idiomatic: For his earlier and later merit he was advanced to senior great general.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵安平縣公。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's title Duke of Anping county.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's title, duke of Anping county.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥反，弘度以行軍總管從韋孝寬討之，所當無不披靡。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Hongdu served as campaign commander following Wei Xiaokuan to suppress him; wherever he confronted the enemy none failed to be swept aside.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Hongdu served as campaign commander under Wei Xiaokuan to suppress him, and wherever he confronted the enemy none failed to be swept aside.

sentences.zh: 弘度妹先適迥子為妻。

translations.literal: Hongdu's younger sister had earlier been given in marriage to Jiong's son as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu's younger sister had earlier been given in marriage to Jiong's son.

sentences.zh: 及破鄴城，迥窘迫升樓，弘度直上龍尾追之。

translations.literal: When Ye city was taken, Jiong in distress ascended a tower; Hongdu went straight up the Dragon Tail ramp in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye city fell, Jiong in distress ascended a tower, and Hongdu went straight up the Dragon Tail ramp in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 迥將射弘度，弘度脫兜鍪謂曰：「今日各圖國事，不得顧私。

translations.literal: Jiong was about to shoot Hongdu; Hongdu removed his helmet and said: "Today each of us seeks the state's interest—we cannot consider private ties.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was about to shoot Hongdu. Hongdu removed his helmet and said, "Today each of us seeks the state's interest. We cannot consider private ties.

sentences.zh: 事既如此，早為身計，何所待也？

translations.literal: Matters having come to this, make early plans for yourself—what are you waiting for?
translations.idiomatic: Matters having come to this, make early plans for yourself. What are you waiting for?"

sentences.zh: 」迥擲弓於地，罵大丞相極口，自殺。

translations.literal: " Jiong threw his bow to the ground, cursed the Grand Chancellor to the utmost, and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong threw his bow to the ground, cursed the grand chancellor to the utmost, and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 弘度顧弟弘升，使取迥頭。

translations.literal: Hongdu looked to his younger brother Hongsheng and had him take Jiong's head.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu looked to his younger brother Hongsheng and had him take Jiong's head.

sentences.zh: 進位上柱國。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to senior pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 時行軍總管例封國公，以弘度不時殺迥，縱致惡言，由是降爵一等為武鄉郡公。

translations.literal: At the time campaign commanders were customarily enfeoffed as dukes of a state; because Hongdu did not kill Jiong promptly and thus allowed slander to spread, for this reason his rank was lowered one grade to Duke of Wuxiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the time campaign commanders were customarily enfeoffed as state dukes, but because Hongdu did not kill Jiong promptly and thus allowed slander to spread, his rank was lowered one grade to duke of Wuxiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，以行軍總管拒突厥于原州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he served as campaign commander resisting the Turks at Yuan province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang he served as campaign commander resisting the Turks at Yuan province.

sentences.zh: 還，拜華州刺史。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Governor of Hua province.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed governor of Hua province.

sentences.zh: 納妹為秦孝王妃。

translations.literal: He gave his younger sister in marriage as consort to Prince Xiao of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his younger sister in marriage as consort to Prince Xiao of Qin.

sentences.zh: 尋遷襄州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Commander of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to commander of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 弘度素貴，禦下嚴急，所在令行禁止，盜賊屏跡。

translations.literal: Hongdu had long been honored; he was severe and urgent toward subordinates; wherever he was, orders were executed and prohibitions heeded, and bandits vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu had long been honored. He was severe and urgent toward subordinates, and wherever he served orders were executed and prohibitions heeded until bandits vanished.

sentences.zh: 梁主蕭琮來朝被止，以弘度為江陵總管，鎮荊州。

translations.literal: When the Liang ruler Xiao Cong came to court and was detained, Hongdu was made Commander of Jiangling and garrisoned Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang ruler Xiao Cong came to court and was detained, Hongdu was made commander of Jiangling and garrisoned Jing province.

sentences.zh: 陳人憚之，不敢窺境。

translations.literal: The Chen people feared him and did not dare peer across the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen people feared him and did not dare peer across the border.

sentences.zh: 以行軍總管從秦孝王平陳，賜物五千段。

translations.literal: As campaign commander he followed Prince Xiao of Qin in pacifying Chen and was granted five thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: As campaign commander he followed Prince Xiao of Qin in pacifying Chen and was granted five thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 高智慧等作亂，復以行軍總管隸楊素。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhihui and others rose in rebellion, he again served as campaign commander under Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui and others rose in rebellion, he again served as campaign commander under Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 弘度與素品同，而年長於素，素每屈下之，一旦隸素，意甚不平。

translations.literal: Hongdu and Su were of equal rank, but Hongdu was older than Su; Su always yielded to him, and once subordinate to Su his mind was very resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu and Su were of equal rank, but Hongdu was older than Su and Su always yielded to him. Once subordinate to Su, Hongdu was deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 素亦優容之。

translations.literal: Su also treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Su also treated him with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 及還，以行軍總管檢校原州事，以備胡。

translations.literal: When he returned he was made campaign commander to inspect and oversee Yuan province affairs, to guard against the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he was made campaign commander to inspect and oversee Yuan province, to guard against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 無虜而還。

translations.literal: There were no enemies and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Finding no enemy, he returned.

sentences.zh: 上甚禮之，復以其弟弘升女為河南王妃。

translations.literal: The emperor treated him with great courtesy and again took Hongsheng's daughter as consort to the Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated him with great courtesy and again took Hongsheng's daughter as consort to the Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，檢校太府卿。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he was made acting Minister of the Palace Granary.
translations.idiomatic: In the Renshou era he served as acting minister of the palace granary.

sentences.zh: 自以一門二妃，無所降下。

translations.literal: He considered that with two princesses in one family he owed deference to no one.
