translations.idiomatic: He considered that with two princesses in one family he owed deference to no one.

sentences.zh: 每誡其寮吏曰：「人當誠恕，無得欺誑。

translations.literal: He often admonished his staff officers: "A man should be sincere and forgiving and must not deceive.
translations.idiomatic: He often admonished his staff officers, "A man should be sincere and forgiving and must not deceive."

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " They all said: "Yes.
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」後嘗食鱉，侍者八九人。

translations.literal: " Later once while eating turtle he had eight or nine attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Later, once while eating turtle he had eight or nine attendants.

sentences.zh: 弘度問之曰：「鱉美乎？

translations.literal: Hongdu asked them: "Is the turtle delicious?
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu asked them, "Is the turtle delicious?"

sentences.zh: 」人懼之，皆曰：「美。

translations.literal: " Fearing him, they all said: "Delicious.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing him, they all said, "Delicious."

sentences.zh: 」弘度大罵曰：「傭奴！

translations.literal: " Hongdu cursed loudly: "Servile wretches!
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu cursed loudly, "Servile wretches!"

sentences.zh: 」何敢誑我？

translations.literal: " How dare you deceive me?
translations.idiomatic: How dare you deceive me?"

sentences.zh: 汝初未食鱉，安知其美？

translations.literal: You have not yet eaten turtle—how do you know it is delicious?
translations.idiomatic: You have not yet eaten turtle. How do you know it is delicious?"

sentences.zh: 」俱杖之八十。

translations.literal: " He had them all beaten eighty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: He had them all beaten eighty strokes.

sentences.zh: 官屬百工見之，莫不汗流，無敢欺隱。

translations.literal: When officials and craftsmen saw this none failed to sweat; no one dared conceal anything.
translations.idiomatic: When officials and craftsmen saw this, none failed to break into a sweat, and no one dared conceal anything.

sentences.zh: 時有屈突蓋為武候車騎，亦嚴刻。

translations.literal: At the time Qutu Gai was Wuhou Chariot and Cavalry—also severe.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Qutu Gai served as Wuhou chariot and cavalry officer and was also severe.

sentences.zh: 長安為之語曰：「寧飲三斗醋，不見崔弘度；

translations.literal: Chang'an had a saying about it: "Better drink three dou of vinegar than see Cui Hongdu;
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an had a saying: "Better drink three dou of vinegar than see Cui Hongdu;

sentences.zh: 甯炙三斗艾，不逢屈突蓋。

translations.literal: better endure roasting three dou of mugwort than meet Qutu Gai.
translations.idiomatic: better endure roasting three dou of mugwort than meet Qutu Gai."

sentences.zh: 」然弘度居家，子弟班白，動行捶楚，閨門整肅，為當世所稱。

translations.literal: " Yet at home Hongdu's sons and younger relatives, white-haired among them, were often beaten; his household was sternly ordered and was praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at home Hongdu's sons and younger relatives, white-haired among them, were often beaten. His household was sternly ordered and was praised by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 未幾秦王妃以罪誅，河南王妃復被廢，弘度憂恚，謝病於家。

translations.literal: Before long the Princess of Qin was executed for a crime and the Princess of Henan was again deposed; Hongdu grieved and resentful, pleaded illness and stayed home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Princess of Qin was executed for a crime and the Princess of Henan was again deposed. Grieving and resentful, Hongdu pleaded illness and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 諸弟乃與之別居，彌不得志。

translations.literal: His younger brothers then separated from him to live apart; he became even more frustrated.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers then separated from him to live apart, and he became even more frustrated.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，河南王為太子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, the Prince of Henan became crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, the Prince of Henan became crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝將復立崔妃，遣中使就第宣旨。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to restore Lady Cui as consort and sent a palace emissary to his residence to announce the imperial decree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to restore Lady Cui to her status as consort and dispatched a palace emissary to his home to deliver the imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 使者詣弘升家，弘度不之知。

translations.literal: The emissary went to Hongsheng's home; Hong Du did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emissary went to the residence of Hongsheng, but Hong Du was unaware.

sentences.zh: 使者反，帝曰：「弘度有何言？

translations.literal: The emissary returned, and the emperor said: "What did Hong Du say?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emissary returned, the emperor asked, "What did Hong Du say?"

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「弘度稱疾不起。

translations.literal: The emissary said: "Hong Du claimed illness and would not rise."
translations.idiomatic: The emissary replied, "Hong Du pleaded illness and refused to rise."

sentences.zh: 」帝默然，其事竟寢。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent, and the matter ultimately came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing further, and the matter was dropped altogether.

sentences.zh: 弘度憂憤，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Hong Du, aggrieved and indignant, died before long.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Du, consumed by grief and indignation, died not long after.

sentences.zh: 崔挺，字雙根，辯之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Cui Ting, styled Shuanggen, was a younger male cousin of Bian on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ting, courtesy name Shuanggen, was a younger cousin of Cui Bian.

sentences.zh: 父郁，位濮陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Yu held the post of Administrator of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cui Yu served as Administrator of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 挺幼孤，居喪盡禮，少敦學。

translations.literal: Ting lost his father while young, observed mourning rites completely, and in youth was devoted to study.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was orphaned at an early age. He observed mourning rites with full propriety and devoted himself to study from youth.

sentences.zh: 五代同居，後頻年饑，家始分析。

translations.literal: Five generations lived together; later, in years of frequent famine, the family at last divided.
translations.idiomatic: The family had lived together across five generations, but after repeated years of famine they finally divided the household.

sentences.zh: 挺與弟振推讓田宅舊資，惟守墓田而已。

translations.literal: Ting and his younger brother Zhen yielded to each other fields, houses, and old assets, keeping only grave-plot land.
translations.idiomatic: Ting and his younger brother Zhen deferred to each other in dividing fields, houses, and family property, each keeping only the land around the ancestral graves.

sentences.zh: 家徒壁立，兄弟怡然，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: The home was bare as walls standing alone; the brothers were content and never let books leave their hands.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in utter poverty, with nothing but bare walls—yet the brothers were cheerful and never put down their books.

sentences.zh: 鄉人有贍遺，挺辭而後受，仍亦散之。

translations.literal: When fellow villagers sent provisions, Ting declined and then accepted, yet dispensed them again.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors offered gifts of support, Ting would decline at first but eventually accept them—only to distribute what he received among others.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，射策高第。

translations.literal: He was nominated as a xiucai and ranked at the top in the cice examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as a xiucai and placed at the top of the cice examination.

sentences.zh: 拜中書博士，轉侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat and later transferred to Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat and later promoted to Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以工書，受敕于長安書文明太后父燕宣王碑，賜爵秦昌子。

translations.literal: Because he excelled at calligraphy, he received an order to inscribe at Chang'an the stele for Yan the King of Xuannan, father of Empress Dowager Wenming, and was granted the title Viscount of Qinchang.
translations.idiomatic: For his skill in calligraphy, he was ordered to inscribe at Chang'an the stele for Yan, King of Xuannan, father of Empress Dowager Wenming, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Qinchang.

sentences.zh: 轉登聞令，遷典屬國下大夫。

translations.literal: He transferred to be Director of the Appeals Office and was promoted to Grand Master of the Protocol for Dependent States.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Appeals Office and promoted to Grand Master of the Protocol for Dependent States.

sentences.zh: 以參議律令，賜帛、谷、馬、牛等。

translations.literal: For participating in deliberation on statutes and ordinances, he was granted silk, grain, horses, cattle, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: For his participation in drafting statutes and ordinances, he was rewarded with silk, grain, horses, cattle, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 尚書李沖甚重之。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Li Chong greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, Minister of Works, held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 孝文以挺女為嬪。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen took Ting's daughter as a consort.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen took Ting's daughter into the palace as a consort.

sentences.zh: 宋王劉昶南鎮彭城，詔挺為長史，以疾辭免，乃以王肅為長史，其被遇如此。

translations.literal: When Prince of Song Liu Chang garrisoned the south at Pengcheng, an edict appointed Ting as chief administrator, but he declined on grounds of illness and was excused; then Wang Su was made chief administrator—such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chang, Prince of Song, was assigned to the southern garrison at Pengcheng, Ting was ordered to serve as chief administrator, but declined citing illness; Wang Su was appointed in his stead—evidence of how highly he was regarded.

sentences.zh: 後拜昭武將軍、光州刺史，風化大行。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Displays Martiality and Governor of Guangzhou; civilizing influence was greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed General Who Displays Martiality and Governor of Guangzhou, where he achieved broad success in transforming local customs through education.

sentences.zh: 及車駕幸兗州，召挺赴行在所，問以臨邊之略，因及文章。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Yanzhou, Ting was summoned to the temporary palace and questioned about strategy for guarding the frontier, and then about literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Yanzhou, Ting was summoned to the temporary palace, questioned about frontier strategy, and then about literary matters.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅，謂曰：「別卿以來，倏焉二載。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said to him: "Since we parted, two years have swiftly passed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and said, "Since we last met, two years have flown by."

sentences.zh: 吾所綴文，以成一集，今當給卿副本。

translations.literal: The compositions I have strung together have formed a collection; now I shall give you a copy."
translations.idiomatic: "I have assembled my writings into a collection, and I shall now give you a copy."

sentences.zh: 」顧謂侍臣曰：「擁旄者皆如此，何憂哉！

translations.literal: He turned and said to the attendant officials: "If all who bear command banners are like this, what is there to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his attendants, he added, "When every frontier commander is like this, what have we to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」復還州。

translations.literal: Ting then returned to his province.
translations.idiomatic: Ting then returned to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及散騎常侍張彝巡行風俗，謂曰：「彝受使巡方，采察謠訟，入境觀政，實愧清使之名。

translations.literal: When Palace Attendant Zhang Yi toured to inspect local customs, he said: "Yi, having received a commission to tour the regions, gathering and examining popular songs and petitions, and entering a province to observe its governance, is truly ashamed of the name 'inspector of purity.'"
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Attendant Zhang Yi came to inspect local customs, he told Ting, "I was sent to tour the realm, examine popular grievances, and observe governance upon entering each province—and I am embarrassed to call myself an inspector of good government."

sentences.zh: 」州舊掖城西北數里有斧山，峰嶺高峻。

translations.literal: Within the province, several li northwest of the old city of Ye was Mount Fu; its peaks and ridges were high and steep.
translations.idiomatic: A few li northwest of the old city of Ye in the province stood Mount Fu, its peaks towering and sheer.

sentences.zh: 北臨滄海，南望岱嶽。

translations.literal: To the north it overlooked the Cang Sea; to the south it gazed upon Mount Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It faced the Cang Sea to the north and Mount Tai to the south.

sentences.zh: 挺于頂上欲營觀宇，故老曰：「此嶺上，秋夏之際，常有暴雨。

translations.literal: Ting wished to build a hall on the summit; the elders said: "On this ridge, between autumn and summer, violent storms often occur."
translations.idiomatic: Ting planned to erect a pavilion on the summit, but local elders warned, "On this ridge, violent storms often strike between autumn and summer."

sentences.zh: 相傳云是龍道，恐此觀不可久立。

translations.literal: Tradition says it is the dragon's path; I fear this hall cannot long stand."
translations.idiomatic: "Legend holds this is the dragon's path—I fear your hall cannot endure long here."

sentences.zh: 」挺曰：「人龍相去，何遠之有？

translations.literal: Ting said: "How far apart are men and dragons?"
translations.idiomatic: Ting replied, "How far apart can men and dragons truly be?"

sentences.zh: 虯龍倏忽，豈一路乎？

translations.literal: Coiled dragons come and go in an instant—are they confined to a single path?"
translations.idiomatic: "Dragons rise and vanish in an instant—must they keep to one road alone?"

sentences.zh: 」遂營之。

translations.literal: He thereupon built it.
translations.idiomatic: He built it anyway.

sentences.zh: 數年間，果無風雨之異。

translations.literal: For several years, indeed no unusual storms occurred.
translations.idiomatic: For several years, no untoward storms materialized.

sentences.zh: 挺既代，即為風雨所毀，遂莫能立。

translations.literal: Once Ting left office, it was destroyed by wind and rain, and thereafter could not be maintained.
translations.idiomatic: After Ting departed, storms destroyed the pavilion, and it could never be rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 眾以為善化所感。

translations.literal: The people regarded it as a response to his virtuous transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The people took this as a sign of the power of his virtuous governance.

sentences.zh: 時以犯罪配邊者多有逃越，遂立重制，一人犯罪逋亡，闔門充役。

translations.literal: At the time, many convicts sentenced to frontier duty for crimes fled; a severe regulation was therefore established: if one person committed a crime and absconded, the entire household was conscripted for corvée.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, many criminals sentenced to frontier exile fled, so a harsh rule was imposed: when one person committed a crime and fled, the entire household was conscripted for corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 挺上書，以為《周書》父子罪不相及，以一人犯罪，延及闔門，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Ting submitted a memorial, holding that in the Book of Zhou, the crimes of father and son do not extend to each other; to extend punishment to the whole household for one person's crime—how pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Ting submitted a memorial arguing that the Book of Zhou holds that fathers and sons are not punished for each other's crimes; to punish an entire household for one person's offense—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 辭甚雅切，帝納之。

translations.literal: His language was very elegant and earnest, and the emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: His language was eloquent and moving, and the emperor accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 先是，州內少鐵，器用皆求之他境。

translations.literal: Previously, iron was scarce within the province, and tools and utensils all had to be obtained from other regions.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, the province lacked iron, and all tools and utensils had to be imported from elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 挺表復鐵官，公私有賴。

translations.literal: Ting submitted a memorial to restore iron offices; both public and private sectors benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Ting memorialized the throne to restore iron production offices, to the benefit of both public and private interests.

sentences.zh: 孝文將辨天下氏族，仍亦訪定，乃遙授挺本州大中正。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was about to classify the clans throughout the realm and also sought to determine their status; he therefore remotely appointed Ting as Grand Assessor of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen set out to classify the clans of the realm and determine their standing, he appointed Ting from afar as Grand Assessor of his home province.

sentences.zh: 掖縣有人年逾九十，板輿造州。

translations.literal: In Ye county there was a man over ninety who came to the provincial capital in a carry-chair.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Ye county, more than ninety years old, came to the provincial capital in a carry-chair.

sentences.zh: 自稱少曾充使林邑，得一美玉，方尺四寸，甚有光采，藏之海島，垂六十歲，忻逢明政，今願奉之。

translations.literal: He said that in youth he had once served as envoy to Linyi and obtained a fine jade, one foot square and four inches thick, very lustrous; he had hidden it on a sea island for nearly sixty years and, rejoicing to encounter enlightened governance, now wished to present it.
translations.idiomatic: He said that in his youth he had served as an envoy to Linyi and obtained a fine jade tablet, a foot square and four inches thick, of remarkable luster; he had kept it hidden on a sea island for nearly sixty years and, delighted to live under enlightened rule, now wished to present it as a gift.

sentences.zh: 挺曰：「吾雖德謝古人，未能以玉為寶。

translations.literal: Ting said: "Although my virtue falls short of the ancients, I cannot take jade as treasure."
translations.idiomatic: Ting said, "Though my virtue falls short of the ancients, I cannot regard jade as a treasure."

sentences.zh: 」遣船隨取，光潤果然，迄不肯受，乃表送都。

translations.literal: He sent a boat to fetch it; its luster was indeed as described, yet he still refused to accept it and instead submitted a memorial to send it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a boat to retrieve it; the jade proved as lustrous as described, yet he still refused to accept it and instead memorialized the court to have it sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 景明初，見代，老幼泣涕追隨，縑帛送贈，悉不納。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era, when he was replaced, old and young wept and followed him; they sent silk and cloth as parting gifts, but he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingming era, when he was recalled from office, old and young alike wept and followed him, offering silk and cloth as parting gifts—all of which he declined.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍趙修得幸宣武，挺雖同州壤，未嘗詣門。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhao Xiu gained favor with Emperor Xuanwu; although Ting was from the same province, he never visited Zhao's door.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zhao Xiu won the favor of Emperor Xuanwu; though Ting was from the same province, he never once called at Zhao's residence.

sentences.zh: 北海王詳為司徒、錄尚書事，以挺為司馬，固辭不免。

translations.literal: Prince of Beihai Xiang served as Minister of Education and Director of the Department of State Affairs; he appointed Ting as Administrator, but though Ting firmly declined, he could not be excused.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Beihai Xiang served as Minister of Education and Director of the Department of State Affairs, he appointed Ting as Administrator; Ting repeatedly declined but could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 世人皆歎其屈，而挺處之夷然。

translations.literal: People of the world all lamented this as a demotion, yet Ting bore it with complete equanimity.
translations.idiomatic: The world lamented this as a demotion, yet Ting accepted it with perfect composure.

sentences.zh: 詳攝選，眾人競稱考第，以求遷敘，挺終無言。

translations.literal: When Xiang oversaw the selection of officials, everyone competed to claim their examination rank to seek promotion; Ting in the end said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang oversaw official selection, everyone else clamored to claim their merit ratings in hopes of promotion; Ting remained silent throughout.

sentences.zh: 詳曰：「崔光州考級並未加授，宜投一牒，當為申請。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Governor Cui of Guangzhou, your examination grade has not yet been formally conferred; you should submit a petition, and I shall apply on your behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Governor Cui, your merit rating has not yet been formally conferred; you should submit a petition, and I will apply on your behalf."

sentences.zh: 蘧伯玉恥獨為君子，亦何故默然？

translations.literal: Qu Boyu was ashamed to be the only gentleman—why then are you silent?"
translations.idiomatic: "Qu Boyu was ashamed to be the only gentleman—why do you remain silent?"

sentences.zh: 」挺曰：「階級是聖朝大例，考課亦國之恆典，至於自炫求進，竊以羞之。

translations.literal: Ting said: "Rank and grade are great precedents of the sage dynasty; merit examination is also a constant institution of the state; as for boasting and seeking advancement, I privately find it shameful."
translations.idiomatic: Ting replied, "Rank and merit review are established institutions of our dynasty; as for boasting and seeking advancement, I find that shameful."

sentences.zh: 」詳大相稱歎。

translations.literal: Xiang greatly praised and admired this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang praised him greatly.

sentences.zh: 其為司馬，詳未曾呼名，常稱州號，以示優禮。

translations.literal: While he served as Administrator, Xiang never called him by name but always addressed him by his provincial title, to show special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Ting's tenure as Administrator, Xiang never addressed him by name but always by his provincial title, as a mark of special respect.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈輔國將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰景。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted the title General Who Assists the State and Governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death, he was posthumously honored as General Who Assists the State and Governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 光州故吏聞凶問，莫不悲感，共鑄八尺銅象，於城東廣固寺赴八關齋，追奉冥福。

translations.literal: Former subordinates of Guangzhou, hearing news of his death, were all grieved; together they cast an eight-foot bronze statue and, at Guanggu Temple east of the city, attended the Eight Precepts assembly to pray for blessings in the afterlife.
translations.idiomatic: Former subordinates from Guangzhou, upon hearing of his death, were overcome with grief; together they cast an eight-foot bronze statue and, at Guanggu Temple east of the city, observed the Eight Precepts assembly to pray for his blessings in the afterlife.

sentences.zh: 初，崔光貧賤，挺贍遺衣食，常親敬焉。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Cui Guang was poor and lowly, Ting sent him food and clothing and always treated him with personal respect.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier years, when Cui Guang was poor and obscure, Ting supported him with food and clothing and always treated him with personal respect.

sentences.zh: 又識邢巒、宋弁于童幼，世稱其知人。

translations.literal: He also recognized Xing Yan and Song Bian in their childhood; the world praised his discernment of talent.
translations.idiomatic: He also recognized Xing Yan and Song Bian when they were still children; the world praised his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 曆官三十餘年，家資不益，食不重味，室無綺羅，閨門之內，雍雍如也。

translations.literal: Over more than thirty years in office, his household wealth did not increase; he never ate more than one dish at a meal, kept no silk in his home, and within his inner quarters all was harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than thirty years of official service, he never increased his household wealth; he never ate more than one dish at a meal, kept no silk finery at home, and maintained perfect harmony within his family.

sentences.zh: 欲諸子恭敬廉讓，因以孝為字。

translations.literal: Wishing his sons to be respectful, modest, and yielding, he therefore gave them all the courtesy character Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing his sons to be respectful, modest, and yielding, he gave them all the courtesy character Xiao (Filial).

sentences.zh: 及葬，親故多有贈賵，諸子推挺素志，一無所受。

translations.literal: At his burial, many relatives and friends offered funeral gifts; his sons, honoring Ting's lifelong wishes, accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: At his burial, many relatives and friends offered funeral gifts, but his sons, honoring Ting's lifelong wishes, accepted none.

sentences.zh: 有子六人，長子孝芬。

translations.literal: He had six sons; the eldest was Xiaofen.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons; the eldest was Xiaofen.

sentences.zh: 孝芬字恭梓。

translations.literal: Xiaofen, styled Gongzi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen, courtesy name Gongzi.

sentences.zh: 早有才識，博學好文章。

translations.literal: From early on he had talent and insight; he was broadly learned and loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He showed early talent and insight, was broadly learned, and loved literary composition.

sentences.zh: 孝文召見，甚嗟賞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen summoned him for an audience and greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen summoned him for an audience and greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 李彪謂挺曰：「比見賢子謁帝，旨喻殊優，今當為絕群耳。

translations.literal: Li Biao said to Ting: "I recently saw your worthy son audience the emperor; his understanding was exceptionally fine—he will surely surpass all others."
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao told Ting, "I recently saw your worthy son audience the emperor; his understanding was exceptionally fine—he will surely surpass all others."

sentences.zh: 」挺曰：「卿自欲善處人父子之間，然斯言吾不敢聞也。

translations.literal: Ting said: "You yourself wish to conduct yourself well between father and son, yet I dare not hear such words."
translations.idiomatic: Ting replied, "You simply wish to conduct yourself well between father and son—but I dare not hear such words."

sentences.zh: 」後襲父爵，累遷司空屬、定州大中正。

translations.literal: Later he inherited his father's title and was repeatedly promoted to staff member of the Minister of Works and Grand Assessor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited his father's title and rose through the ranks to become a staff member of the Minister of Works and Grand Assessor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 長於剖判，甚有能名，府主任城王澄雅重之。

translations.literal: He excelled at legal adjudication and had a strong reputation for capability; the Prince of Rencheng Wang Cheng of the prefecture greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at legal adjudication and earned a strong reputation for capability; Wang Cheng, Prince of Rencheng and prefectural chief, held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 澄奏地制八條，孝芬所參定也。

translations.literal: Cheng submitted the eight articles on land regulations—Xiaofen participated in drafting them.
translations.idiomatic: The eight articles on land regulations that Cheng submitted were drafted with Xiaofen's participation.

sentences.zh: 遷廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，梁將裴邃等寇淮南，詔行台酈道元、都督河間王榮討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Liang generals Pei Sui and others invaded Huainan; an edict ordered mobile commander Li Daoyuan and Commander Hejian Wang Rong to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaochang era, Liang generals Pei Sui and others invaded Huainan; an edict ordered mobile commander Li Daoyuan and Commander Wang Rong of Hejian to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 敕孝芬持節催令赴接，賊退而還。

translations.literal: Xiaofen was ordered with imperial credentials to hurry the forces to engage; the rebels retreated and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen received imperial credentials to hurry the forces into action; the rebels retreated and he returned.

sentences.zh: 遷荊州刺史，兼尚書、南道行台，領軍司，率諸將以援神俊，因代焉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Jingzhou, concurrently Minister and Commander of the Southern Route mobile headquarters, leading the military office; he led various generals to aid Shen Jun and then replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Jingzhou, concurrently serving as Minister and commander of the Southern Route mobile headquarters and military supervisor; he led various generals to aid Shen Jun and then replaced him.

sentences.zh: 孝芬遂從恆農道南入，敵便奔散，人還安堵。

translations.literal: Xiaofen then entered from the south along the Hengnong route; the enemy at once fled and scattered, and the people returned to peaceful settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen marched south along the Hengnong route; the enemy fled and scattered, and the people returned to peaceful lives.

sentences.zh: 明帝嘉勞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 後以元叉之党，與盧同、李獎等並除名，征還。

translations.literal: Later, as an associate of Yuan Cha's faction, he was dismissed from office along with Lu Tong, Li Jiang, and others and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as an associate of Yuan Cha's faction, he was stripped of office along with Lu Tong, Li Jiang, and others and recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 又除孝芬為廷尉。

translations.literal: Xiaofen was again appointed Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen was again appointed Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 章武王融以贓貨被劾，孝芬案以重法。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhangwu Rong was impeached for accepting bribes; Xiaofen tried the case under the heavy penalty law.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhangwu Rong was impeached for accepting bribes; Xiaofen tried the case under the heavy penalty law.

sentences.zh: 及融為都督，北討鮮于修禮，時孝芬弟孝演率宗從在博陵，為賊攻陷，遇害。

translations.literal: When Rong became commander and marched north against Xianyu Xiuli, at that time Xiaofen's younger brother Xiaoyan leading their clan kinsmen was in Boling; the city was attacked and captured by rebels, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong became commander and marched north against Xianyu Xiuli, Xiaofen's younger brother Xiaoyan was in Boling leading their clan kinsmen; the city was overrun by rebels and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 融密啟雲孝演入賊為逆，遂見收捕。

translations.literal: Rong secretly memorialized that Xiaoyan had joined the rebels in rebellion; Xiaofen was thereupon arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Rong secretly memorialized that Xiaoyan had joined the rebels in rebellion; Xiaofen was thereupon arrested.

sentences.zh: 全家投梁，遇赦乃還。

translations.literal: His entire family fled to Liang; they returned only after an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: His entire family fled to Liang territory and returned only after an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 後梁將成景俊逼彭城，孝芬兼尚書右丞，為徐州行台。

translations.literal: Later, when Liang general Cheng Jingjun pressed Pengcheng, Xiaofen served concurrently as Right Director of the Ministry and commander of the Xuzhou mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Liang general Cheng Jingjun besieged Pengcheng, Xiaofen served concurrently as Right Director of the Ministry and commander of the Xuzhou mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 孝芬將發，入辭。

translations.literal: As Xiaofen was about to depart, he entered to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing, Xiaofen went to take leave of the court.

sentences.zh: 靈太后謂曰：「卿女今事我兒，與卿是親。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling said: "Your daughter now serves my son; you and I are kin."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling said, "Your daughter now serves my son—we are kin."

sentences.zh: 曾何相負，而內頭元叉車內，稱此嫗須了卻！

translations.literal: How have I wronged you, yet inside Yuan Cha's carriage you said this old woman must be eliminated!"
translations.idiomatic: How have I wronged you, yet inside Yuan Cha's carriage you said this old woman must be eliminated!"

sentences.zh: 」孝芬曰：「臣蒙國厚恩，義無斯語；

translations.literal: Xiaofen said: "Your servant has received the state's profound grace; by duty I could never speak such words;"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen replied, "I owe the state a profound debt of gratitude; I could never speak such words;"

sentences.zh: 假有斯語，誰能得聞？

translations.literal: even if such words had been spoken, who could have overheard them?
translations.idiomatic: even if I had spoken such words, who could have overheard them?

sentences.zh: 若有此聞，即此人於元叉親密，過臣遠矣。

translations.literal: If such words were heard, then whoever reported them must have been far closer to Yuan Cha than I.
translations.idiomatic: If such words were indeed heard, whoever reported them must have been far closer to Yuan Cha than I.

sentences.zh: 乞對之，足辨虛實。

translations.literal: I beg to confront the accuser—truth and falsehood can readily be distinguished."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to confront the accuser and settle truth from falsehood."

sentences.zh: 」太后乃有愧色。

translations.literal: The empress dowager then showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 孝芬既至，景俊等力屈退走。

translations.literal: Once Xiaofen arrived, Cheng Jingjun and the others, their strength exhausted, retreated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaofen arrived, Cheng Jingjun and the others, exhausted, retreated.

sentences.zh: 以孝芬兼尚書，為徐、兗二州行台。

translations.literal: Xiaofen was appointed concurrently as Minister and commander of the mobile headquarters for Xu and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen was appointed concurrently as Minister and commander of the mobile headquarters for Xu and Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 建義初，太山太守羊侃據郡反，引南賊圍兗州行台。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, Mount Tai Prefect Yang Kan rebelled and occupied his commandery, drawing southern invaders to besiege the Yanzhou mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyi era, Mount Tai Prefect Yang Kan rebelled and occupied his commandery, drawing southern invaders to besiege the Yanzhou mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 除孝芬散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，仍兼尚書、東道行台，與大都督刁宣往救援。

translations.literal: Xiaofen was appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Guards the East, and Grand Master of the Golden Seal with Purple Cord, continuing concurrently as Minister and commander of the Eastern Route mobile headquarters; he went with Grand Commander Diao Xuan to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen was appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Guards the East, and Grand Master of the Golden Seal with Purple Cord, continuing concurrently as Minister and commander of the Eastern Route mobile headquarters; he joined Grand Commander Diao Xuan in the relief effort.

sentences.zh: 與行台于侃時相接。

translations.literal: His mobile headquarters then made contact with Yu Kan's forces.
translations.idiomatic: His mobile headquarters then made contact with Yu Kan's forces.

sentences.zh: 至便圍之，侃突圍奔梁。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he at once besieged them; Kan broke through the encirclement and fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival he immediately laid siege; Yang Kan broke through the encirclement and fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 永安中，授西兗州刺史；

translations.literal: During the Yong'an era, he was appointed Governor of Western Yanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an era, he was appointed Governor of Western Yanzhou;

sentences.zh: 孝芬倦外役，固辭不行，仍為太常卿。

translations.literal: Xiaofen, weary of service abroad, firmly declined and did not go, remaining instead as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen, weary of field service, firmly declined the appointment and remained as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，兼殿中尚書，後加儀同三司，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he served concurrently as Director of the Palace Secretariat; later he was given the rank of Palace Attendant of the Third Order and concurrently served as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era, he served concurrently as Director of the Palace Secretariat; later he was given the rank of Palace Attendant of the Third Order and concurrently appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝入關，齊神武至洛，與尚書辛雄、劉廞等並被誅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the Pass, Gao Huan of Northern Qi arrived at Luoyang; Xiaofen, along with Ministers Xin Xiong, Liu Yin, and others, was all executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the Pass and Gao Huan of Northern Qi arrived at Luoyang, Xiaofen was executed along with Ministers Xin Xiong, Liu Yin, and others.

sentences.zh: 沒其家口，天平中，乃免之。

translations.literal: His household members were confiscated; during the Tianping era, they were at last released.
translations.idiomatic: His household members were confiscated; during the Tianping era, they were at last released.

sentences.zh: 孝芬博聞口辯，善談論，愛好後進，終日忻然。

translations.literal: Xiaofen was broadly learned and eloquent, skilled at discourse, fond of nurturing younger talent, and cheerful all day long.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen was broadly learned and eloquent, skilled in conversation, fond of nurturing younger talent, and cheerful throughout the day.

sentences.zh: 商榷古今，間以嘲謔，聽者忘疲。

translations.literal: He discussed and compared past and present, interspersing wit and banter; listeners forgot their fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: He discussed past and present, interspersing wit and banter, so that listeners forgot their fatigue.

sentences.zh: 文筆數十篇。

translations.literal: He left several dozen literary compositions.
translations.idiomatic: He left several dozen literary compositions.

sentences.zh: 有子八人。

translations.literal: He had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 長子勉，字宣祖，頗涉史傳。

translations.literal: The eldest son Mian, styled Xuanzu, was fairly versed in historical records and biographies.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Mian, courtesy name Xuanzu, was fairly versed in historical records and biographies.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，兼尚書右丞。

translations.literal: During Putai, he served concurrently as Right Director of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putai era, he served concurrently as Right Director of the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 勉善附會，世論以浮競譏之。

translations.literal: Mian was skilled at attaching himself to the powerful; worldly opinion mocked him for superficial ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was skilled at currying favor; public opinion criticized him for superficial ambition.

sentences.zh: 為尚書令爾硃世隆所親待，而尚書郎魏季景尤為世隆所知，勉與季景內頗不睦。

translations.literal: He was treated with personal favor by Minister of Works Erzhu Shilong, while Gentleman of the Ministry Wei Jijing was especially trusted by Shilong; inwardly Mian and Jijing were quite at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong, Minister of Works, treated him with personal favor, while Gentleman of the Ministry Wei Jijing enjoyed Shilong's special trust; inwardly Mian and Jijing were quite at odds.

sentences.zh: 季景於世隆求右丞，奪勉所兼；

translations.literal: Jijing asked Shilong for the right directorship and took over Mian's concurrent post;
translations.idiomatic: Jijing asked Shilong for the right directorship and took over Mian's concurrent post;

sentences.zh: 世隆啟用季景，勉遂帳怏自失。

translations.literal: Shilong memorialized to appoint Jijing, and Mian thereupon grew resentful and despondent.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong memorialized to appoint Jijing, and Mian grew resentful and despondent.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，除散騎常侍、征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫、定州大中正，敕左右廂出入。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the East, Grand Master of the Golden Seal with Purple Cord, and Grand Assessor of Dingzhou, with orders to enter and leave through the left and right side gates.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era, he was appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the East, Grand Master of the Golden Seal with Purple Cord, and Grand Assessor of Dingzhou, with orders to enter and leave through the side gates.

sentences.zh: 其家被收之際，逃免。

translations.literal: When his family was being confiscated, he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When his family was being confiscated, he escaped.

sentences.zh: 後見齊神武，勞撫之。

translations.literal: Later he met Gao Huan of Northern Qi, who comforted and reassured him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he met Gao Huan of Northern Qi, who comforted and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 天平初，遣勉送勳貴妻子赴定州，因得還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, Mian was dispatched to escort the wives and children of meritorious nobles to Dingzhou, and thereby was able to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianping era, Mian was dispatched to escort the wives and children of meritorious nobles to Dingzhou, and thereby was able to return home.

sentences.zh: 屬母李氏喪亡，勉哀號過性，遇病卒。

translations.literal: Just then his mother Lady Li died; Mian wailed beyond what nature could bear and, falling ill, died.
translations.idiomatic: Just then his mother Lady Li died; Mian grieved beyond all measure and, falling ill, died.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟宣度以子龍子為後。

translations.literal: He had no sons; his younger brother Xuandu made his son Longzi the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons; his younger brother Xuandu adopted his son Longzi as heir.

sentences.zh: 勉弟猷。

translations.literal: Mian's younger brother You.
translations.idiomatic: Mian's younger brother was You.

sentences.zh: 猷字宣猷。

translations.literal: You, styled Xuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: You, courtesy name Xuanyou.

sentences.zh: 少好學，風度閒雅。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; his bearing was leisurely and refined.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning, and his bearing was leisurely and refined.

sentences.zh: 性鯁正，有軍國籌略。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and principled, with strategic talent for military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and principled, with strategic talent for military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，累遷司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Putai era, he rose through the ranks to Attendant of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 既遭家難，遂間行入關。

translations.literal: Having suffered the calamity of his family's destruction, he then traveled by hidden routes to enter the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After his family was destroyed, he traveled by hidden routes to enter the Pass.

sentences.zh: 及謁魏孝武，哀動左右。

translations.literal: When he had an audience with Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, his grief moved those on either side.
translations.idiomatic: When he had an audience with Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, his grief moved all who were present.

sentences.zh: 帝為之改容，目送曰：「忠孝之道，萃此一門。

translations.literal: The emperor changed expression on his account and, watching him depart, said: "The way of loyalty and filial piety is gathered in this one family."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression changed, and as he watched You depart he said, "The way of loyalty and filial piety is gathered in this one family."

sentences.zh: 」即以本官奏門下事。

translations.literal: He was thereupon allowed to submit matters to the Secretariat in his existing office.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon allowed to submit matters to the Secretariat in his existing office.

sentences.zh: 大統初兼給事黃門郎、平原縣伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, he served concurrently as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Baron of Pingyuan county.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era, he served concurrently as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Baron of Pingyuan county.

sentences.zh: 二年，正黃門。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was made regular Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he was made regular Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 行軍禽竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，猷常以本官從軍典文翰。

translations.literal: On campaign they captured Dou Tai, recovered Hongnong, and defeated the enemy at Shayuan; You regularly followed the army in his existing office, managing documents and dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign they captured Dou Tai, recovered Hongnong, and defeated the enemy at Shayuan; You regularly followed the army in his existing office, managing documents and dispatches.

sentences.zh: 五年，除司徒左長史，加驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education and given the additional title General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he was appointed Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education and given the additional title General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時太廟初成，四時祭祀猶設俳優角抵之戲；

translations.literal: At the time the Imperial Ancestral Temple had just been completed, yet the seasonal sacrifices still featured performances by actors and wrestling matches;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Imperial Ancestral Temple had just been completed, yet the seasonal sacrifices still featured performances by actors and wrestling matches;

sentences.zh: 其郊廟祭官，多有假兼。

translations.literal: many of the sacrificial officials for the suburban and temple rites held concurrent appointments on temporary assignment.
translations.idiomatic: many of the sacrificial officials for the suburban and temple rites held concurrent appointments on temporary assignment.

sentences.zh: 猷上疏諫；

translations.literal: You submitted a memorial remonstrating;
translations.idiomatic: You submitted a memorial remonstrating;

sentences.zh: 書奏，並納焉。

translations.literal: when the memorial was submitted, all his proposals were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: when the memorial was submitted, all his proposals were accepted.

sentences.zh: 遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 時婚姻禮嫁聚會之辰，多舉音樂。

translations.literal: At the time, on occasions of marriage rites and wedding gatherings, music was often performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, music was often performed at marriage rites and wedding gatherings.

sentences.zh: 又廛裏富室，衣服奢淫，乃有織成文繡者。

translations.literal: Moreover, among wealthy households in the market wards, clothing was extravagant and licentious, with some even woven into patterned embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among wealthy households in the market wards, clothing was extravagant and licentious, with some even woven into patterned embroidery.

sentences.zh: 猷請禁斷，事並施行。

translations.literal: You requested that these be forbidden and cut off; the measures were all implemented.
translations.idiomatic: You requested that these be forbidden; the measures were all implemented.

sentences.zh: 與盧辯等創修六官。

translations.literal: Together with Lu Bian and others, he helped create and revise the Six Offices system.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Lu Bian and others, he helped create and revise the Six Offices system.

sentences.zh: 十二年，除浙州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was appointed Governor of Zhe province.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, he was appointed Governor of Zhe province.

sentences.zh: 十四年，侯景據河南歸款，遣行台王思政赴之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Hou Jing held Henan and submitted allegiance; mobile commander Wang Sizheng was dispatched to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Hou Jing held Henan and submitted allegiance; mobile commander Wang Sizheng was dispatched to him.

sentences.zh: 周文與思政書曰：「崔宣猷智略明贍，有應變之才。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou wrote to Sizheng: "Cui Xuanyou is intelligent and resourceful, with talent for adapting to changing circumstances."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou wrote to Sizheng, "Cui Xuanyou is intelligent and resourceful, with talent for adapting to changing circumstances."

sentences.zh: 若有所疑，宜與量其可不。

translations.literal: If you have any doubts, you should consult with him and weigh what is feasible."
translations.idiomatic: If you have any doubts, you should consult with him and weigh what is feasible."

sentences.zh: 」思政初頓兵襄城，後於潁川為行台，並致書於猷。

translations.literal: Sizheng first encamped his troops at Xiangcheng, later establishing his mobile headquarters at Yingchuan, and wrote to You on both occasions.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng first encamped his troops at Xiangcheng, later establishing his mobile headquarters at Yingchuan, and wrote to You on both occasions.

sentences.zh: 猷書曰：「襄城控帶京洛，實當今之要地，如有動靜，易相應接。

translations.literal: You wrote: "Xiangcheng commands the approaches to the capital region and Luoyang; it is truly a vital position of the present day. If anything occurs, response and contact are easily made."
translations.idiomatic: You wrote, "Xiangcheng commands the approaches to the capital region and Luoyang; it is truly a vital position of the present day. If anything occurs, response and contact are easily made."

sentences.zh: 潁川既鄰寇境，又無山川之固，賊若潛來，徑至城下。

translations.literal: Yingchuan borders enemy territory and lacks the protection of mountains and rivers; if bandits come secretly, they can reach the city walls directly.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan borders enemy territory and lacks the protection of mountains and rivers; if bandits come secretly, they can reach the city walls directly.

sentences.zh: 莫若頓兵襄城，為行台所。

translations.literal: It would be better to encamp troops at Xiangcheng and make it the seat of the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to encamp troops at Xiangcheng and make it the seat of the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 潁川置州，遣郭賢守。

translations.literal: Establish a province at Yingchuan and send Guo Xian to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Establish a province at Yingchuan and send Guo Xian to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 則表裏膠固，人心易安，縱有不虞，豈能為患。

translations.literal: Then front and rear will be firmly joined, hearts will easily be settled, and even if the unexpected occurs, how could it become a calamity?"
translations.idiomatic: Then front and rear will be firmly joined, hearts will easily be settled, and even if the unexpected occurs, how could it become a calamity?"

sentences.zh: 」使人見周文，其以啟聞。

translations.literal: He sent a messenger to see Emperor Wen of Zhou and had the letter reported.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a messenger to see Emperor Wen of Zhou and had the letter reported.

sentences.zh: 周文令依猷策。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou ordered that You's plan be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou ordered that You's plan be followed.

sentences.zh: 思政重啟，求與朝廷立約，賊若水攻，乞一周為斷；

translations.literal: Sizheng submitted another memorial, requesting to establish an agreement with the court: if the enemy attacks by water, he asked for one week as the limit;
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng submitted another memorial, requesting to establish an agreement with the court: if the enemy attacks by water, he asked for one week as the limit;

sentences.zh: 陸攻，請三歲為期。

translations.literal: for a land attack, he requested three years as the term.
translations.idiomatic: for a land attack, he requested three years as the term.

sentences.zh: 限內有事，不煩赴援。

translations.literal: Within these limits, if trouble arose, he would not trouble the court to send relief.
translations.idiomatic: Within these limits, if trouble arose, he would not trouble the court to send relief.

sentences.zh: 過此以往，惟朝廷所裁。

translations.literal: Beyond this, all would be at the court's discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, all would be at the court's discretion.

sentences.zh: 乃許之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 及潁川沒，周文深追悔焉。

translations.literal: When Yingchuan fell, Emperor Wen of Zhou deeply regretted it afterward.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingchuan fell, Emperor Wen of Zhou deeply regretted not having followed You's advice.

sentences.zh: 以疾去職，屬大軍東征，周文賜以馬，隨軍與之籌略。

translations.literal: He left office due to illness; when the great army marched east, Emperor Wen of Zhou granted him a horse, and he followed the army to discuss strategy with them.
translations.idiomatic: He left office due to illness; when the great army marched east, Emperor Wen of Zhou granted him a horse, and he followed the army to discuss strategy with them.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、本州大中正，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was promoted to Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Palace Attendant of the Third Order with an opening office, and Grand Assessor of his home province, and was granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, he was promoted to Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Palace Attendant of the Third Order with an opening office, and Grand Assessor of his home province, and was granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 及陳將蔡皎來附，晉公護議欲南伐，公卿莫敢言。

translations.literal: When Chen general Cai Jiao came to submit allegiance, Duke of Jin Hu proposed a southern campaign; none of the ministers and nobles dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen general Cai Jiao came to submit allegiance, Duke of Jin Hu proposed a southern campaign; none of the ministers and nobles dared speak.

sentences.zh: 猷獨進曰：「前歲東征，死傷過半，比雖加撫循，而創痍未復。

translations.literal: You alone advanced and said: "Last year's eastern campaign left more than half dead and wounded; though care and relief have since been added, the wounds are not yet healed."
translations.idiomatic: You alone stepped forward and said, "Last year's eastern campaign left more than half dead and wounded; though care and relief have since been added, the wounds are not yet healed."

sentences.zh: 近者長星為災，乃上玄所以垂鑒誡也，豈可窮兵極武，而重其譴負哉？

translations.literal: Recently the broom star appeared as a calamity—this is Heaven's way of bestowing warning and admonition; how can we exhaust troops and push warfare to the extreme and again incur its reproach and burden?"
translations.idiomatic: Recently the broom star appeared as a calamity—this is Heaven's way of bestowing warning and admonition; how can we exhaust troops and push warfare to the extreme and again incur its reproach and burden?"

sentences.zh: 」議不從。

translations.literal: The proposal was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 後水軍果敗，而裨將元定等遂沒江南。

translations.literal: Later the naval force was indeed defeated, and lieutenant generals such as Yuan Ding were lost south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Later the naval force was indeed defeated, and lieutenant generals such as Yuan Ding were lost south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 建德六年，拜少司徒，加上開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande, he was appointed Vice Minister of Education and given the additional title of Grand General with an opening office of the Second Order.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiande, he was appointed Vice Minister of Education and given the additional title of Grand General with an opening office of the Second Order.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，以猷前代舊齒，授大將軍，進爵汲郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the abdication, because You was an elder of the previous dynasty, he was appointed Grand General and advanced to Duke of Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the abdication, because You was an elder of the previous dynasty, he was appointed Grand General and advanced to Duke of Ji commandery.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年，卒，諡曰明。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaihuang, he died; his posthumous name was Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaihuang, he died; his posthumous name was Ming.

sentences.zh: 子仲方嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhongfang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongfang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 仲方字不齊。

translations.literal: Zhongfang, styled Buqi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang, courtesy name Buqi.

sentences.zh: 少好讀書，有文武才略。

translations.literal: From youth he loved reading and possessed both civil and military talent and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved reading and possessed both civil and military talent and strategy.

sentences.zh: 年十五，周文帝見而異之，令與諸子同就學。

translations.literal: At age fifteen, Emperor Wen of Zhou saw him and was struck by his unusual qualities; he ordered him to study together with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: At age fifteen, Emperor Wen of Zhou saw him and was struck by his unusual qualities; he ordered him to study together with his sons.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝亦在其中。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui was also among them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui was also among them.

sentences.zh: 由是與帝少相款密。

translations.literal: From this he and the emperor became close and intimate from youth.
translations.idiomatic: From this he and the future emperor became close and intimate from youth.

sentences.zh: 後以明經為晉公宇文護參軍，轉記室，遷司正大夫，與斛斯征、柳敏等同修禮律。

translations.literal: Later, having passed the classics examination, he became aide to Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, transferred to be recorder, was promoted to Grand Master of Correct Conduct, and together with Husizheng and Liu Min revised the rites and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Later, having passed the classics examination, he became aide to Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, transferred to be recorder, was promoted to Grand Master of Correct Conduct, and together with Husizheng and Liu Min revised the rites and statutes.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功授平東將軍、銀青光祿大夫，賜爵石城縣男。

translations.literal: Later, for military merit, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Cord, and was granted the title Baron of Shicheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for military merit, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Cord, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Shicheng county.

sentences.zh: 時武帝陰有滅齊志，仲方獻二十策，帝大奇之。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wu secretly harbored the intent to destroy Qi; Zhongfang submitted twenty stratagems, and the emperor was greatly impressed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Wu secretly harbored the intent to destroy Qi; Zhongfang submitted twenty stratagems, and the emperor was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 復與少內史赴芬刪定格式。

translations.literal: He again joined Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Fufen in revising and fixing the administrative regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Fufen in revising and fixing the administrative regulations.

sentences.zh: 尋從帝攻下晉州，又令仲方說下翼城等四城，授儀同，進爵范陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed the emperor in capturing Jin province; Zhongfang was also ordered to persuade the surrender of Yicheng and three other cities; he was granted the rank of Palace Attendant of the Fourth Order and advanced to Marquis of Fanyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he followed the emperor in capturing Jin province; Zhongfang was also ordered to persuade the surrender of Yicheng and three other cities; he was granted the rank of Palace Attendant of the Fourth Order and advanced to Marquis of Fanyang county.

sentences.zh: 後以行軍長史從郯國公王軌禽陳將吳明徹于呂梁，仲方策居多。

translations.literal: Later, as campaign chief administrator, he followed Duke of Tan Wang Gui in capturing Chen general Wu Mingche at Lüliang; Zhongfang's stratagems contributed the most.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as campaign chief administrator, he followed Duke of Tan Wang Gui in capturing Chen general Wu Mingche at Lüliang; Zhongfang's stratagems contributed the most.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，為少內史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, he became Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, he became Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，隋文帝為丞相，與仲方相見，握手極歡，仲方亦歸心焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Yang Jian became chief minister; he met with Zhongfang, clasped hands in great joy, and Zhongfang also pledged his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Yang Jian became chief minister; he met with Zhongfang, clasped hands in great joy, and Zhongfang also pledged his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 其夜上便宜十八事，帝並嘉納之。

translations.literal: That same night he submitted eighteen timely proposals; the emperor praised and accepted them all.
translations.idiomatic: That same night he submitted eighteen timely proposals; the emperor praised and accepted them all.

sentences.zh: 又勸帝應天受命，從之。

translations.literal: He also urged the emperor to accept Heaven's mandate; the emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the emperor to accept Heaven's mandate; the emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，上召仲方與高熲議正朔服色事。

translations.literal: When the abdication was accepted, the emperor summoned Zhongfang and Gao Jiong to discuss the calendar and ceremonial colors.
translations.idiomatic: When the abdication was accepted, the emperor summoned Zhongfang and Gao Jiong to discuss the calendar and ceremonial colors.

sentences.zh: 仲方曰：「晉為金行，後魏為水，周為木，皇家以火承木德之統。

translations.literal: Zhongfang said: "Jin belonged to the Metal phase, Later Wei to Water, Zhou to Wood; the imperial house inherits the Wood virtue with Fire."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang said, "Jin belonged to the Metal phase, Later Wei to Water, Zhou to Wood; the imperial house inherits the Wood virtue with Fire."

sentences.zh: 又聖躬載誕之初，有赤光之瑞。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of the sacred person's birth, there was an auspicious sign of red light.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at the beginning of the sacred person's birth, there was an auspicious sign of red light.

sentences.zh: 車服旗牲，並宜用赤。

translations.literal: Chariots, robes, banners, and sacrificial animals should all appropriately use red.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots, robes, banners, and sacrificial animals should all appropriately use red.

sentences.zh: 」又勸上除六官，依漢魏之舊。

translations.literal: He also urged the emperor to abolish the Six Offices and follow the old system of Han and Wei."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the emperor to abolish the Six Offices and follow the old system of Han and Wei."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: All were accepted.

sentences.zh: 進位上開府，授司農少卿，進爵固安縣公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to opening office of the Second Order, appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and advanced to Duke of Gu'an county.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to opening office of the Second Order, appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and advanced to Duke of Gu'an county.

sentences.zh: 令發丁三萬于朔方、靈武築長城，東至黃河，西拒綏州，南至勃出嶺，綿曆七百里。

translations.literal: He was ordered to conscript thirty thousand laborers to build the Great Wall at Shuofang and Lingwu, extending east to the Yellow River, west to Sui province, south to Bochu ridge—a span of seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to conscript thirty thousand laborers to build the Great Wall at Shuofang and Lingwu, extending east to the Yellow River, west to Sui province, south to Bochu ridge—a span of seven hundred li.

sentences.zh: 明年，復令仲方發丁十萬，于朔方已東，緣邊險要，築數十城，以遏胡寇。

translations.literal: The following year, Zhongfang was again ordered to conscript one hundred thousand laborers east of Shuofang to build several dozen fortresses along strategic frontier points and check barbarian raids.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Zhongfang was again ordered to conscript one hundred thousand laborers east of Shuofang to build several dozen fortresses along strategic frontier points and check barbarian raids.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，去職。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his father's death, he left office.

sentences.zh: 未期，起為虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Before the mourning period ended, he was recalled to serve as Governor of Guo province.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mourning period ended, he was recalled to serve as Governor of Guo province.

sentences.zh: 上書論取陳之策曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial discussing the strategy for conquering Chen, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial discussing the strategy for conquering Chen, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣謹案：晉太康元年，歲在庚子，晉武帝平吳。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: In the first year of Taikang of Jin, the year being gengzi, Emperor Wu of Jin pacified Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully observes: In the first year of Taikang of Jin, the year gengzi, Emperor Wu of Jin pacified Wu.

sentences.zh: 至今開皇六年，歲次丙午，合三百七載。

translations.literal: From then until the sixth year of Kaihuang, the year being bingwu, it totals three hundred and seven years.
translations.idiomatic: From that time to the sixth year of Kaihuang, the year bingwu, three hundred and seven years have elapsed.

sentences.zh: 《春秋寶乾圖》云：「王者三百年一蠲法。

translations.literal: The Baogan Tu of the Spring and Autumn Annals says: "Every three hundred years a king remits the laws."
translations.idiomatic: The Baogan Tu of the Spring and Autumn Annals states, "Every three hundred years a king remits the laws."

sentences.zh: 」今三百之期，可謂至矣。

translations.literal: "The period of three hundred years may be said to have arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The period of three hundred years may be said to have arrived.

sentences.zh: 陳氏草竊，起於丙子，至今丙午，又子午為沖，陰陽之忌。

translations.literal: Chen arose by usurpation beginning in bingzi; until the present bingwu year, moreover zi and wu are in mutual opposition—a taboo of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen arose through usurpation in bingzi; by the present bingwu year, zi and wu stand in mutual opposition—a yin-yang taboo.

sentences.zh: 昔史趙有言曰：「陳，顓頊之族，為水，故歲在鶉火以滅。

translations.literal: Formerly Shi Zhao had a saying: "Chen is of the lineage of Zhuanxu and belongs to Water; therefore in the year of the Quail Fire it was destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhao once said, "Chen belongs to the lineage of Zhuanxu and to Water; thus in the year of the Quail Fire it perished."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「周武王克商，封胡公滿于陳。

translations.literal: "He also said: "King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang and enfeoffed Duke Hu Man at Chen."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang and enfeoffed Duke Hu Man at Chen."

sentences.zh: 」至魯昭九年，陳災，裨灶曰：「歲五及鶉火而後陳亡，楚克之。

translations.literal: "In the ninth year of Duke Zhao of Lu, Chen suffered a fire; Pi Zao said: "When the year reaches the Quail Fire five times, then Chen will perish and Chu will conquer it."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Duke Zhao of Lu, Chen suffered a fire; Pi Zao said, "When the year reaches the Quail Fire five times, then Chen will perish and Chu will conquer it."

sentences.zh: 」楚，祝融後也，為火正，故復滅陳。

translations.literal: "Chu was descended from Zhu Rong and was director of Fire; therefore it again destroyed Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Chu was descended from Zhu Rong and was director of Fire; therefore it again destroyed Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳承舜後，舜承顓頊。

translations.literal: Chen inherited from Shun, and Shun inherited from Zhuanxu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen traced its descent from Shun, and Shun from Zhuanxu.

sentences.zh: 太歲左行，歲星右轉；

translations.literal: The Grand Year moves leftward, the Year Star turns rightward;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Year moves leftward while the Year Star turns rightward;

sentences.zh: 鶉火之歲，陳族再亡，戊午之年，媯虞運盡。

translations.literal: In the year of the Quail Fire the Chen clan perished twice; in the year wuwu the fortune of the Gui-Yu line was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of the Quail Fire the Chen clan fell twice; in wuwu the fortune of the Gui-Yu line ran out.

sentences.zh: 語跡雖殊，考事無別。

translations.literal: The wording and traces differ, but examining the matter there is no difference.
translations.idiomatic: The words and traces differ, yet the underlying facts do not.

sentences.zh: 皇朝五運相承感火德。

translations.literal: The imperial dynasty, with the Five Movements succeeding one another, responds to the virtue of Fire.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty, with the Five Movements succeeding one another, responds to the virtue of Fire.

sentences.zh: 而國號為隋，隋與楚同分，楚是火正。

translations.literal: Yet the dynastic name is Sui; Sui shares the same asterism as Chu, and Chu was director of Fire.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the dynastic name is Sui, which shares an asterism with Chu—and Chu was director of Fire.

sentences.zh: 午為鶉火，未為鶉首，申為實沈，酉為大梁。

translations.literal: Wu is the Quail Fire, wei is the Quail Head, shen is the Real Shen, and you is the Great Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Wu is the Quail Fire, wei the Quail Head, shen the Real Shen, and you the Great Bridge.

sentences.zh: 既當周、秦、晉、趙之分，若當此分發兵，將得歲之助。

translations.literal: These correspond to the divisions of Zhou, Qin, Jin, and Zhao; if troops are dispatched in these divisions, they will obtain the aid of the year star.
translations.idiomatic: These fall within the divisions of Zhou, Qin, Jin, and Zhao; troops dispatched in these sectors will gain the year star's aid.

sentences.zh: 以今量古，陳滅不疑。

translations.literal: Measuring the present by the past, the destruction of Chen admits no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the present by the past, Chen's fall cannot be doubted.

sentences.zh: 臣謂午、未、申、酉並其數極。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that wu, wei, shen, and you all reach the limit of their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that wu, wei, shen, and you all reach the extremity of their cycle.

sentences.zh: 蓋聞天時不如地利，地利不如人和。

translations.literal: I have heard that heavenly timing is not as good as earthly advantage, and earthly advantage is not as good as human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly timing is inferior to earthly advantage, and earthly advantage to human harmony—or so it is said.

sentences.zh: 況主聖臣良，兵強國富，陳既主昏於上，人讟於下，險無百二之固，眾非九國之師，獨此島夷，而稽天討！

translations.literal: Moreover, when the ruler is sage and ministers good, the army strong and the state rich, while Chen has a benighted ruler above and murmuring people below, lacks the impregnable strength of a hundredfold advantage, and its forces are not an army of nine states—this lone island barbarian dares delay Heaven's punitive expedition!
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler is sage and ministers capable, the army strong and state rich, while Chen has a benighted ruler and murmuring subjects, lacks a hundredfold fortress, and fields no army of nine states—what is this island people to delay Heaven's judgment?

sentences.zh: 伏度朝廷，自有宏謨，皞蕘所見，冀申螢爝。

translations.literal: I venture to suppose the court already has its grand design; what this humble opinion offers may add a glimmer to the torch.
translations.idiomatic: The court surely has its grand design already; what this humble view offers may yet add a flicker to the flame.

sentences.zh: 今唯須武昌以下，蘄、和、徐、方、吳、海等州，更帖精兵，密營渡計；

translations.literal: Now it is only necessary, from Wuchang downstream through Qi, He, Xu, Fang, Wu, Hai, and other provinces, to post elite troops and secretly plan the crossing;
translations.idiomatic: From Wuchang downstream through Qi, He, Xu, Fang, Wu, Hai, and other provinces, elite troops should be posted and crossing plans laid in secret;

sentences.zh: 益、信、襄、荊、基、郢等州，速造舟楫，多張形勢，為水戰之具。

translations.literal: In Yi, Xin, Xiang, Jing, Ji, Ying, and other provinces, rapidly build boats and warships and display great force as preparations for naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: In Yi, Xin, Xiang, Jing, Ji, Ying, and other provinces, ships should be built swiftly and force displayed as preparation for naval war.

sentences.zh: 蜀、漢二江，是其上流，水路沖要，必爭之所。

translations.literal: The Min and Han rivers are its upper reaches; these water routes are strategic points that both sides must contest.
translations.idiomatic: The Min and Han rivers form the upper reaches—water routes of strategic importance that both sides must fight for.

sentences.zh: 賊雖于流頭、荊門、延洲、公安、巴陵、隱磯、夏口、盆城置船，然終聚漢口、峽口，以水戰火決。

translations.literal: Though the enemy may station ships at Liutou, Jingmen, Yanzhou, Gongan, Baling, Yinji, Xiakou, and Pencheng, in the end they will gather at Hankou and Xiakou and decide the matter by naval battle.
translations.idiomatic: Though the enemy may station fleets at Liutou, Jingmen, Yanzhou, Gongan, Baling, Yinji, Xiakou, and Pencheng, they will ultimately mass at Hankou and Xiakou and settle matters by naval battle.

sentences.zh: 若賊必以上流有軍，令精兵赴援者，下流諸將，即須擇便橫度。

translations.literal: If the enemy surely sends elite troops upstream to reinforce because there are troops above, then the generals downstream must choose a convenient point to cross.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy sends elite reinforcements upstream, downstream commanders must seize a convenient crossing point.

sentences.zh: 如擁眾自衛，上江水軍，鼓行以前。

translations.literal: If they mass troops for self-defense, the upstream naval forces should advance with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: If they mass for self-defense, the upstream fleet should advance to the beat of drums.

sentences.zh: 雖恃九江五湖之險，非德無以為固；

translations.literal: Though they rely on the peril of the Nine Rivers and Five Lakes, without virtue they cannot hold firm;
translations.idiomatic: They may rely on the Nine Rivers and Five Lakes, but without virtue no defense holds;

sentences.zh: 徒有三吳百越之兵，無恩不能自立。

translations.literal: They have only the forces of the Three Wu and the Hundred Yue, but without benevolence they cannot stand alone.
translations.idiomatic: They may field the armies of Three Wu and the Hundred Yue, but without benevolence they cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 上覽，大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 轉基州刺史，征入朝。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Governor of Ji province and summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Ji province and summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 仲方因陳經略，上善之，賜以禦袍褲並羅雜彩五百段，進位開府。

translations.literal: Zhongfang thereupon presented his strategic plan; the emperor approved it and granted him an imperial robe and trousers plus five hundred bolts of mixed silk, advancing him to opening office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang presented his strategic plan; the emperor approved and granted an imperial robe and trousers plus five hundred bolts of mixed silk, promoting him to opening office.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，以仲方為行軍總管，與秦王會。

translations.literal: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Zhongfang was made campaign commander and joined Prince Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Zhongfang served as campaign commander and joined Prince Qin.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，坐事免。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was pacified, he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復位。

translations.literal: Before long, he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 後數載，授會州總管。

translations.literal: Several years later, he was appointed Commander of Hui province.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed Commander of Hui province.

sentences.zh: 時諸羌猶未賓附，詔仲方擊之，與賊三十餘戰，紫祖、四鄰、望方、涉題、幹碉、小鐵圍山、白男、弱水等赭都諸賊悉平。

translations.literal: At the time the various Qiang had not yet submitted; an edict ordered Zhongfang to attack them. After more than thirty battles with the enemy, the Zhe tribes including Zizu, Silin, Wangfang, Sheti, Gandiao, Little Tiewei Mountain, Bainan, and Ruoshui were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang tribes had not yet submitted; ordered to attack, Zhongfang fought more than thirty engagements and pacified the Zhe tribes of Zizu, Silin, Wangfang, Sheti, Gandiao, Little Tiewei Mountain, Bainan, Ruoshui, and others.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢一百二十口、黃金三十斤。

translations.literal: He was granted one hundred and twenty slaves and servants and thirty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He received one hundred and twenty slaves and thirty jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 遷代州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander of Dai province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commander of Dai province.

sentences.zh: 總被征入朝。

translations.literal: The commander was repeatedly summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The commander was called to court repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 會文帝崩，漢王餘黨據呂州不下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the remnant followers of Prince Han held Lü province and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, Prince Han's remnant followers held Lü province and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣周羅碶攻之，中流矢卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang dispatched Zhou Luozi to attack them; he was struck by an arrow in midstream and died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent Zhou Luozi to attack; he was struck by an arrow midstream and died.

sentences.zh: 及令仲方代總其眾，拔之，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Zhongfang to take overall command of the forces, captured the city, and advanced him to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang was ordered to take overall command, captured the city, and was promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 曆戶部、禮部尚書，坐事免。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Revenue and Minister of Rites and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Revenue and Minister of Rites before being dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋為國子祭酒，轉太常卿。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he became Director of the Imperial Academy and was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Director of the Imperial Academy and was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其衰老，出拜上郡太守。

translations.literal: The court, considering him aged, sent him out as Administrator of Shang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Considering his age, the court sent him out as Administrator of Shang commandery.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，歲餘起為信都太守。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he left office; after a year he was recalled to serve as Administrator of Xin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He left office upon his mother's death; a year later he was recalled as Administrator of Xin commandery.

sentences.zh: 後乞骸骨，優詔許之，卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he requested retirement; an edict graciously permitted it, and he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later requested retirement; a gracious edict permitted it, and he died at home.

sentences.zh: 子燾，位定陶令。

translations.literal: His son Tao held the post of magistrate of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao served as magistrate of Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 宣猷弟宣度，位齊王開府司馬、恆農太守。

translations.literal: Xuanyou's younger brother Xuandu held the post of Administrator of the Prince of Qi's opening office and Administrator of Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyou's younger brother Xuandu served as Administrator of the Prince of Qi's opening office and Administrator of Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 宣度弟宣軌，頗有才學，位尚書考功郎中，與弟宣質、宣靜、宣略並早卒。
