translations.literal: Xuandu's younger brother Xuangui was quite talented and learned, holding the post of Gentleman in the Ministry's Merit Examination Bureau; together with his younger brothers Xuanzhi, Xuanjing, and Xuanlue he all died early.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandu's younger brother Xuangui was talented and learned, serving as Gentleman in the Ministry's Merit Examination Bureau; his younger brothers Xuanzhi, Xuanjing, and Xuanlue all died young.

sentences.zh: 孝芬弟孝偉，趙郡太守。

translations.literal: Xiaofen's younger brother Xiaowei was Administrator of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowei, younger brother of Xiaofen, governed Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡經葛榮離亂後，人皆賣鬻兒女。

translations.literal: After the commandery had suffered the chaos of Ge Rong's depredations, people all sold their sons and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Rong's chaos, people throughout the commandery sold their children.

sentences.zh: 夏椹大熟，孝偉勸戶人多收之，郡內乃安。

translations.literal: When mulberries ripened in summer, Xiaowei urged the households to gather more of them, and peace was restored within the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When summer mulberries ripened, Xiaowei urged households to gather more; peace returned to the commandery.

sentences.zh: 教其人種殖，招撫遺散，先恩後威，一周之後，流戶大至。

translations.literal: He taught the people to plant crops, recruited and reassured the scattered refugees, applying kindness before severity; within a week, displaced households arrived in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He taught farming, recruited scattered refugees, and applied kindness before severity; within a week displaced households poured in.

sentences.zh: 興立學校，親加勸厲，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: He established schools and personally encouraged learning; the people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He founded schools and personally encouraged learning; the people came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 卒郡，贈瀛州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously he was granted Governor of Ying province with the posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously granted Governor of Ying province with the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 朝議謂為未申，復贈安北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held this insufficient; he was again granted General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: The court found this insufficient and additionally granted him General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 一子昂。

translations.literal: He had one son, Ang.
translations.idiomatic: One son, Ang.

sentences.zh: 昂字懷遠，七歲而孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Ang, styled Huaiyuan, was orphaned at seven and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, courtesy name Huaiyuan, was orphaned at seven and was known for filial service to his mother.

sentences.zh: 伯父吏部尚書孝芬嘗謂親友曰：「此兒終當遠至，是吾家千里駒也。」

translations.literal: His uncle, Minister of Personnel Xiaofen, once told relatives and friends: "This boy will surely go far; he is our family's thousand-li colt."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle, Minister of Personnel Xiaofen, once told relatives and friends, "This boy will surely go far; he is our family's thousand-li colt."

sentences.zh: 昂性端直，頗綜文詞。

translations.literal: Ang was upright by nature and fairly versed in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Ang was upright by nature and well versed in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 天平二年，文襄引為記室參軍，季以腹心之任。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianping, Wen Xiang recruited him as recorder-aide and soon entrusted him with matters of the innermost confidence.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianping, Wen Xiang recruited him as recorder-aide and soon entrusted him with his innermost confidence.

sentences.zh: 及輔國政，召為開府長史，並攝京畿長史事。

translations.literal: When he assisted in governing the state, he was summoned to be chief administrator of the opening office and concurrently oversaw the chief administrator affairs of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Xiang took charge of state affairs, Ang was summoned as chief administrator of the opening office and concurrently oversaw capital-region administration.

sentences.zh: 時勳將親族賓客，多行不軌，孫騰、司馬子如之門尤劇。

translations.literal: At the time meritorious generals, kin, and retainers often acted lawlessly; the households of Sun Teng and Sima Ziru were especially egregious.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious generals, kin, and retainers often broke the law; the households of Sun Teng and Sima Ziru were worst of all.

sentences.zh: 昂受文襄密旨，以法繩之，未幾間，內外齊肅。

translations.literal: Ang received Wen Xiang's secret instructions and restrained them by law; before long, both inside and outside were orderly and disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on Wen Xiang's secret orders, Ang restrained them by law; before long order prevailed inside and out.

sentences.zh: 尋遷司徒右長史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Right Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Chief Administrator under the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 時左府有陽平人吳賓為妄認繼嗣事，披訴經久。

translations.literal: At the time in the left office there was a man of Yangping named Wu Bin involved in a false claim to succession; he had been petitioning for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: In the left office a man of Yangping, Wu Bin, had long petitioned over a false claim to succession.

sentences.zh: 長史王昕、郎中鄭憑、掾盧斐、屬王敬寶等窮其獄，始末積年，鞫掠不獲實。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Wang Xin, Gentleman Zheng Ping, aide Lu Fei, and clerk Wang Jingbao investigated the case; for years at beginning and end they interrogated and tortured without obtaining the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Wang Xin, Gentleman Zheng Ping, aide Lu Fei, and clerk Wang Jingbao investigated for years, torturing without finding the truth.

sentences.zh: 司徒婁昭付昂推問，即日詰根緒，獲其真狀。

translations.literal: Minister Lou Zhao handed the case to Ang for investigation; on the same day he traced the root and obtained the true facts.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lou Zhao handed the case to Ang, who traced the root cause the same day and found the facts.

sentences.zh: 昭歎曰：「左府都官數人，不如右府一長史。

translations.literal: Zhao sighed and said: "Several men of the left office's judiciary are not equal to one chief administrator of the right office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao sighed and said, "Several men of the left office's judiciary are not equal to one chief administrator of the right office.

sentences.zh: 」昕、憑甚以為愧。

translations.literal: "Xin and Ping were deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Ping were deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 武定中，文襄普令內外極言得失。

translations.literal: During Wuding, Wen Xiang broadly ordered those inside and outside to speak freely of gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuding, Wen Xiang ordered everyone inside and outside to speak freely of strengths and weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 昂上書曰：「屯田之設，其來尚矣。

translations.literal: Ang submitted a memorial saying: "The establishment of military colonies has a long history.
translations.idiomatic: Ang submitted a memorial saying, "The establishment of military colonies has a long history.

sentences.zh: 曹魏破蜀，業以興師。

translations.literal: When Cao Wei destroyed Shu, the enterprise prospered through the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei's conquest of Shu prospered through its armies.

sentences.zh: 馬晉平吳，兵因取給。

translations.literal: When Jin of the Ma clan pacified Wu, the troops drew their supplies from it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's pacification of Wu drew its troops' supplies from the colonies.

sentences.zh: 朝廷頃以懷、洛兩邑，鄰接邊境，薄屯豐稔，糧儲已贍。

translations.literal: Recently the court, because the two districts of Huai and Luo border the frontier, with thin colonies and abundant harvests, has already filled the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The court has recently filled granaries from thin colonies and rich harvests in the Huai and Luo districts bordering the frontier.

sentences.zh: 准此而論，龜鏡非遠。

translations.literal: Judging by this example, the mirror is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: By this precedent the lesson is close at hand.

sentences.zh: 其幽、安二州，控帶奚賊、蠕蠕；

translations.literal: The You and An provinces control the Xi bandits and the Rouran;
translations.idiomatic: You and An provinces guard against the Xi bandits and Rouran;

sentences.zh: 徐、揚、兗、豫，連接吳越強鄰。

translations.literal: Xu, Yang, Yan, and Yu connect with the powerful neighbor of Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, Yang, Yan, and Yu border the powerful neighbor Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 實藉轉輸之資，常勞私糴之費。

translations.literal: They truly rely on transport resources and are constantly troubled by the expense of private grain purchases.
translations.idiomatic: They depend on transport and are constantly burdened by the cost of buying grain privately.

sentences.zh: 諸道別遣使營之，每考其勤惰，則人加勸勵，倉廩充實，供軍濟國，實謂在茲。

translations.literal: If each route separately dispatches envoys to manage this and each year examines diligence and idleness, then people will be further encouraged, granaries filled, and armies and state supplied—this truly lies here.
translations.idiomatic: If each route sends envoys to manage colonies and yearly examines diligence, people will be encouraged, granaries filled, and armies and state supplied—here lies the key.

sentences.zh: 其次，法獄之重，人命所懸。

translations.literal: Second, the weight of the law courts hangs on human lives.
translations.idiomatic: Second: the law courts weigh on human lives.

sentences.zh: 頃者官司糾察，多不審練，乃聞緣淺入深，未有雪大為小，咸以畏避嫌疑，共相殘刻。

translations.literal: Recently when offices investigate and examine, they often lack thoroughness; one hears of going from shallow to deep without clearing the great and reducing it to the small—all alike fear and avoid suspicion and mutually inflict harshness.
translations.idiomatic: Recent investigations often lack thoroughness; officials go from shallow to deep without distinguishing great from small, all fearing suspicion and mutually inflicting cruelty.

sentences.zh: 至如錢絹粟麥，其狀難分，徑指為贓，罪從此定。

translations.literal: As for money, silk, grain, and wheat, their forms are hard to distinguish; they are directly pointed to as bribes, and guilt is fixed thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Money, silk, grain, and wheat are hard to tell apart; they are simply labeled bribes and guilt fixed.

sentences.zh: 乞勒群司，務存獲實。

translations.literal: I beg that all offices be charged to strive to obtain the truth.
translations.idiomatic: I beg all offices to strive for the truth.

sentences.zh: 如此則有息將來，必無枉濫。

translations.literal: Thus there will be relief in the future and surely no wrongful condemnation.
translations.idiomatic: Then wrongful condemnation will cease and relief will come.

sentences.zh: 」文襄納之。

translations.literal: "Wen Xiang accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang accepted it.

sentences.zh: 後除尚書左丞，其年兼度支尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Left Director of the Ministry; that same year he concurrently served as Director of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Director of the Ministry and that same year concurrently Director of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 左丞之兼尚書，近代未有，朝野榮之。

translations.literal: For a left director to concurrently hold a ministry post was unprecedented in recent times; court and countryside honored it.
translations.idiomatic: A left director holding a concurrent ministry post was unprecedented in recent times; court and country honored the appointment.

sentences.zh: 度支水漕陸運，昂設轉輸相入之差，付給新陳之法，有利於人，遂為常式。

translations.literal: For revenue transport by water and land, Ang established the differential of mutual transfer and the method of issuing new and old supplies—a benefit to the people that became a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: For water and land revenue transport, Ang devised mutual transfer differentials and methods for issuing new and old supplies—benefiting the people and becoming permanent law.

sentences.zh: 右僕射崔暹奏請海沂煮鹽，有利軍國。

translations.literal: Right Vice Minister Cui Xian memorialized requesting salt boiling at Hai and Yi, beneficial to army and state.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Minister Cui Xian proposed boiling salt at Hai and Yi to benefit army and state.

sentences.zh: 文襄以問昂。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang asked Ang about it.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang consulted Ang.

sentences.zh: 昂曰：「亦既官煮，須斷人灶，官力雖多，不及人廣。

translations.literal: Ang said: "Once it is officially boiled, private kilns must be cut off; though official labor is great, it cannot match the breadth of private effort.
translations.idiomatic: Ang said, "Once it is officially boiled, private kilns must be cut off; though official labor is great, it cannot match the breadth of private effort.

sentences.zh: 請准關市，薄為灶稅，私館官給，彼此有宜。

translations.literal: I request following the model of frontier markets, levying a light kiln tax, with private workshops supplied by the state—beneficial to both sides.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed following frontier-market practice with a light kiln tax and state-supplied private workshops—beneficial to both.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之。

translations.literal: "The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed this.

sentences.zh: 武定六年，甘露降宮闕，文武同賀。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wuding, sweet dew fell upon the palace gates; civil and military officials rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wuding, sweet dew fell on the palace gates; civil and military officials rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 魏帝問右僕射崔暹、尚書楊愔、崔甗、邢邵、散騎常侍魏收、御史中丞陸操、國子祭酒李澤曰：「可各言德績感致所由。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor asked Right Vice Minister Cui Xian, Ministers Yang Yin, Cui Yan, Xing Shao, Palace Attendant Wei Shou, Imperial Censor Lu Cao, and Director of the Imperial Academy Li Ze: "Each may speak of the virtue and achievements by which such a response was sensed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor asked Right Vice Minister Cui Xian, Ministers Yang Yin, Cui Yan, Xing Shao, Palace Attendant Wei Shou, Imperial Censor Lu Cao, and Director of the Imperial Academy Li Ze, "Each may speak of the virtue and achievements by which such a response was sensed.

sentences.zh: 」次至昂，昂曰：「吉凶兩門，不由符瑞，故桑雉之戒，實啟中興；

translations.literal: "When it came to Ang, Ang said: "The two gates of fortune and calamity do not depend on talismans and omens; therefore the warning of the mulberry pheasant truly inaugurated restoration;
translations.idiomatic: When it came to Ang, Ang said, "The two gates of fortune and calamity do not depend on talismans and omens; therefore the warning of the mulberry pheasant truly inaugurated restoration;

sentences.zh: 小鳥孕大，未聞福感。

translations.literal: Small birds gestate large ones—one has never heard of fortune responding thus.
translations.idiomatic: Small birds do not gestate large ones—fortune has never been known to respond in such a way.

sentences.zh: 所願陛下，雖休勿休，允答天意。

translations.literal: What I wish for Your Majesty is that though you rest, you do not cease resting, truly answering Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: What I wish for Your Majesty is that even in repose you never cease striving, truly answering Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 」帝為斂容。

translations.literal: The emperor composed his expression.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler composed his expression.

sentences.zh: 後攝都官尚書，上勸田事七條。

translations.literal: Later he oversaw the Directorate of Justice and submitted seven articles urging agricultural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he oversaw the Directorate of Justice and submitted seven articles on agricultural policy.

sentences.zh: 尋兼太府卿。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he concurrently served as Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, he concurrently served as Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，改散騎常侍，兼大司農卿。

translations.literal: When Qi accepted the abdication, he was changed to Palace Attendant and concurrently served as Director of the Grand Granary.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi accepted the abdication, he became Palace Attendant and concurrently Director of the Grand Granary.

sentences.zh: 二寺所掌，世號繁劇，昂校理有術，下無奸偽。

translations.literal: The two offices he managed were known in the world as complex and arduous; Ang regulated them with method, and below him there was no fraud.
translations.idiomatic: The two offices he managed were notoriously complex; Ang regulated them skillfully, and fraud disappeared below him.

sentences.zh: 又奏上橫市妄費事三十四條。

translations.literal: He also memorialized thirty-four items concerning wasteful spending at the cross-market.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized thirty-four items concerning wasteful spending at the cross-market, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 其年，與太子少師邢邵議定國初禮式，仍封華陽縣男。

translations.literal: That year, together with Junior Tutor Xing Shao he deliberated on the rites and forms of the founding of the state, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: That year, with Junior Tutor Xing Shao he fixed the rites and forms of the founding of the state, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 又詔刪定律令，損益禮樂，令尚書右僕射琡等四十三人在領軍府議定。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered revision of statutes and ordinances and augmentation and reduction of rites and music; forty-three men including Right Vice Minister Yu and others were ordered to deliberate at the Commandant's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered revision of statutes and ordinances and changes to rites and music; forty-three men including Right Vice Minister Yu were ordered to deliberate at the Commandant's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 帝尋幸晉陽。

translations.literal: The emperor soon visited Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler soon visited Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 將發，敕遞相遵率；

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he ordered that compliance be passed along in relay;
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to depart, he ordered that compliance be passed along in relay;

sentences.zh: 不者，命昂以聞。

translations.literal: if not, he ordered Ang to report it.
translations.idiomatic: any who failed were to report to Ang.

sentences.zh: 昂部分科條，校正今古，手所增損，十有七八。

translations.literal: Ang arranged the sections and articles, corrected present and past, and with his own hand added or reduced seven or eight tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Ang arranged the sections and articles, corrected present against past, and personally revised seven or eight tenths.

sentences.zh: 轉廷尉卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He became transferred to Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 昂號深文，世論不以平恕相許。

translations.literal: Ang was known for severity in law; public opinion did not regard him as fair and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ang was known for severity in law; public opinion did not regard him as fair and forgiving.

sentences.zh: 又與尚書盧斐，別典京畿詔獄，並有殘刻之聲。

translations.literal: Together with Minister Lu Fei, he separately oversaw capital-region edict cases, and both had a reputation for cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Along with Minister Lu Fei, he separately oversaw capital-region edict cases, and both had a reputation for cruelty.

sentences.zh: 至於推繩大事，理可明言是非，不至冤酷。

translations.literal: Yet in major cases where right and wrong could be clearly stated, there was no wrongful severity.
translations.idiomatic: Still, in major cases where right and wrong could be clearly stated, there was no wrongful severity.

sentences.zh: 有濮陽子沈子遐，齎侯景鐵券，告徐州都督府長史畢義緒期舉兵應景；

translations.literal: There was a man of Puyang named Shen Zixia who carried Hou Jing's iron certificate and reported that Chief Administrator Bi Yixu of the Xuzhou Commandant's headquarters planned to raise troops in response to Hou Jing;
translations.idiomatic: A man of Puyang, Shen Zixia, carrying Hou Jing's iron certificate, reported that Chief Administrator Bi Yixu of the Xuzhou Commandant's headquarters planned to raise troops for Hou Jing;

sentences.zh: 又衛尉卿杜弼門生郝子寬，告弼誹謗，並與元子雄謀逆。

translations.literal: Also, the disciple of Chamberlain Du Bi, Hao Zikuan, reported that Bi had slandered the court and together with Yuan Zixiong plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Also, Chamberlain Du Bi's disciple Hao Zikuan reported that Bi had slandered the court and plotted rebellion with Yuan Zixiong.

sentences.zh: 帝盛怒，付昂窮鞫。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and handed the cases to Ang for exhaustive interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler was greatly enraged and handed the cases to Ang for exhaustive interrogation.

sentences.zh: 昂皆執正雪免，告者引妄獲罪。

translations.literal: Ang in each case upheld justice and cleared the accused; the accusers were punished for false reports.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ang in each case upheld justice and cleared the accused; the accusers were punished for false reports.

sentences.zh: 天保三年，除度支尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, he was appointed Director of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the third year of Tianbao, he was appointed Director of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時有肴藏小吏，因內臣投書告事，又別有飛書告事者，並付昂窮檢。

translations.literal: At the time there was a petty clerk in the provisions store who, through an inner court eunuch, submitted a letter of accusation; there were also anonymous letters of accusation—both were handed to Ang for exhaustive investigation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a provisions-store clerk submitted accusations through an inner-court eunuch, and anonymous letters also appeared—both were handed to Ang for exhaustive investigation.

sentences.zh: 昂言笑間，咸得情，告者辭窮，並引嫌狀。

translations.literal: Between words and laughter Ang obtained the truth in each case; the accusers were reduced to silence and all were implicated by suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Between words and laughter Ang obtained the truth in each case; the accusers were reduced to silence and implicated by their own suspicion.

sentences.zh: 於是飛書遂絕。

translations.literal: Anonymous letters of accusation thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Anonymous accusations thereupon ceased.

sentences.zh: 轉都官尚書，仍兼都官事，食濟州北郡幹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of Justice, still concurrently overseeing justice affairs, with income from the Gan district of Ji province's northern commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He became transferred to Director of Justice, still concurrently overseeing justice affairs, with income from the Gan district of Ji province's northern commandery.

sentences.zh: 文宣幸東山，謂曰：「舊人多出為州，當用卿為令僕，勿望刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan visited Dongshan and said to him: "Old men are mostly sent out as governors; I shall use you as Minister and Vice Minister—do not hope for a governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan visited Dongshan and told him, "Old men are mostly sent out as governors; I shall use you as Minister and Vice Minister—do not hope for a governorship.

sentences.zh: 卿六十外，當與卿本州。

translations.literal: After you pass sixty, I shall give you your home province.
translations.idiomatic: After you pass sixty, I shall give you your home province, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 中間，州不可得也。

translations.literal: In the meantime, a governorship cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: During the meantime, a governorship cannot be obtained.

sentences.zh: 」後九卿以上陪集東宮，帝指昂及尉瑾、司馬子瑞謂皇太子曰：「此是國家名臣，汝宜記之。

translations.literal: "Later, when officials of the Nine Ministers and above accompanied the gathering at the Eastern Palace, the emperor pointed to Ang, Wei Jin, and Sima Zirui and told the crown prince: "These are famous ministers of the state; you should remember them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when officials of the Nine Ministers and above accompanied the gathering at the Eastern Palace, the emperor pointed to Ang, Wei Jin, and Sima Zirui and told the crown prince, "These are famous ministers of the state; you should remember them.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，復侍宴金鳳台，歷數諸人，咸有罪負，至昂，曰：「崔昂直臣，魏收才士，婦兄妹夫，俱省罪過。

translations.literal: "Before long, he again attended a banquet at Golden Phoenix Terrace; going through the men one by one, all had faults and burdens—when he came to Ang, he said: "Cui Ang is a straight minister, Wei Shou a talented writer; as brother-in-law and sister's husband, both are forgiven their faults.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, at a banquet at Golden Phoenix Terrace, the emperor went through the men one by one, noting each one's faults—when he came to Ang, he said, "Cui Ang is a straight minister, Wei Shou a talented writer; as brother-in-law and sister's husband, both are forgiven their faults.

sentences.zh: 」十年，除兼右僕射，數日，即拜為真，未幾，還為兼。

translations.literal: "In the tenth year, he was appointed concurrent Right Vice Minister; after several days he was formally appointed, and before long was again made concurrent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, he was appointed concurrent Right Vice Minister; after several days he was formally appointed, and before long was again made concurrent.

sentences.zh: 楊愔少時與昂不平，文宣崩後，遂免昂右僕射，除儀同三司、光祿勳。

translations.literal: Yang Yin had been at odds with Ang from youth; after Emperor Wenxuan died, he removed Ang from Right Vice Minister and appointed him Palace Attendant of the Third Order and Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin had been at odds with Ang from youth; after Emperor Wenxuan died, he removed Ang from Right Vice Minister and appointed him Palace Attendant of the Third Order and Director of the Imperial Household, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 皇建元年，轉太常卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangjian, he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: During the first year of Huangjian, he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 河清元年，兼御史中丞，太常如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Heqing, he concurrently served as Imperial Censor and remained Minister of Ceremonies as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Heqing, he concurrently served as Imperial Censor while remaining Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 昂從甥李公統坐高歸彥事誅。

translations.literal: Ang's nephew by marriage Li Gongtong was executed for the Gao Guiyan affair.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's nephew by marriage Li Gongtong was executed for the Gao Guiyan affair, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 依律，婦人年六十以上免配宮。

translations.literal: By law, women sixty and above were exempt from assignment to palace service.
translations.idiomatic: Under the law, women sixty and above were exempt from assignment to palace service.

sentences.zh: 時公統母年始五十餘而稱六十，公統舅宣寶求吏以免其姊。

translations.literal: At the time Gongtong's mother was just over fifty yet claimed to be sixty; Gongtong's uncle Xuanbao sought an official to exempt his sister.
translations.idiomatic: During the time Gongtong's mother was just over fifty yet claimed to be sixty; Gongtong's uncle Xuanbao sought an official to exempt his sister.

sentences.zh: 昂弗知，錄尚書、彭城王浟發其事，竟坐除名。

translations.literal: Ang did not know of it; Director of the Department of State Affairs Prince Pengcheng You exposed the matter, and Ang was ultimately stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ang did not know of it; Director of the Department of State Affairs Prince Pengcheng You exposed the matter, and Ang was ultimately stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 三年，復為五兵尚書，遷祠部。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was again appointed Minister of the Five Armies and transferred to Director of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: During the third year, he was again appointed Minister of the Five Armies and transferred to Director of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天統元年，卒，贈趙州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiantong, he died and was posthumously granted Governor of Zhao province.
translations.idiomatic: During the first year of Tiantong, he died and was posthumously granted Governor of Zhao province.

sentences.zh: 昂有風調才識，奮立堅正剛直之名。

translations.literal: Ang had bearing, judgment, and talent, and established a reputation for standing firm in uprightness and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ang had bearing, judgment, and talent, and established a reputation for standing firm in uprightness and integrity.

sentences.zh: 然好揣上情，感激時主，或陳便宜蠲省，或列陰私罪失。

translations.literal: Yet he liked to gauge the ruler's mood and respond to the times, sometimes presenting timely reductions and savings, sometimes listing secret faults and failures.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he liked to gauge the ruler's mood and respond to the times, sometimes presenting timely reductions and savings, sometimes listing secret faults and failures, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 深為文宣所知賞，朝之大事，多以委之。

translations.literal: He was deeply known and rewarded by Emperor Wenxuan; major affairs of court were often entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He became deeply known and rewarded by Emperor Wenxuan; major affairs of court were often entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 情尚嚴猛，每行鞭撻，雖苦楚萬端，對之自若。

translations.literal: His disposition favored severity; whenever he applied the whip, though suffering was extreme, he remained composed.
translations.idiomatic: His disposition favored severity; whenever he applied the whip, though suffering was extreme, he remained composed, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 前則崔暹、季舒為之親援，後乃高德正是其中表，常有挾恃，意色矜高。

translations.literal: Earlier Cui Xian and Ji Shu were his close supporters; later Gao Dezheng was his kinsman by marriage—they constantly gave him backing, and his bearing was proud and lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cui Xian and Ji Shu were his close supporters; later Gao Dezheng was his kinsman by marriage—they constantly gave him backing, and his bearing was proud and lofty, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 以此不為名流歸服。

translations.literal: For this the leading figures did not defer to him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, the leading figures did not defer to him.

sentences.zh: 有五子。

translations.literal: He had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: He fathered five sons.

sentences.zh: 第三子液，字君洽，頗習文藻，有學涉，風儀器局為時論所許。

translations.literal: The third son Ye, styled Junqia, was fairly versed in literary composition, had learning and breadth, and his bearing and capacity were approved by contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The third son Ye, courtesy name Junqia, was fairly versed in literary composition, had learning and breadth, and his bearing and capacity were approved by contemporary opinion.

sentences.zh: 以奉朝請待詔文林館。

translations.literal: As a palace attendant he awaited edicts at the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: As a palace attendant he awaited edicts at the Forest of Literature, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang of Sui, he was Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang of Sui, he was Vice Director of the Secretariat, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 孝偉弟孝演，字則伯，出繼伯父。

translations.literal: Xiaowei's younger brother Xiaoyan, styled Zebai, was adopted to succeed his father's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowei's younger brother Xiaoyan, courtesy name Zebai, was adopted to succeed his father's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 性通率，美須髯，姿貌魁傑，少無宦情，沈浮鄉里。

translations.literal: By nature he was frank and open; he had a fine beard and moustache and a towering, heroic appearance; from youth he had no taste for office and drifted in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was frank and open; he had a fine beard and moustache and a towering, heroic appearance; from youth he had no taste for office and drifted in his home district, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 位瀛州安西府外兵參軍，因罷歸。

translations.literal: He held the post of external military aide in the Anxi office of Ying province, then resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of external military aide in the Anxi office of Ying province, then resigned and returned home, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 及鮮于修禮起逆，遇害。

translations.literal: When Xianyu Xiuli rose in rebellion, he met with disaster and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianyu Xiuli rose in rebellion, he met with disaster and was killed.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟孝直以子士遊為後。

translations.literal: He had no sons; his younger brother Xiaozhi made his son Shiyou the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He fathered no sons; his younger brother Xiaozhi made his son Shiyou the heir.

sentences.zh: 孝直字叔廣，身長八尺，眉目疏朗，早有志尚。

translations.literal: Xiaozhi, styled Shuguang, was eight feet tall with sparse, clear brows and eyes; from early on he had lofty aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhi, courtesy name Shuguang, was eight feet tall with sparse, clear brows and eyes; from early on he had lofty aspirations.

sentences.zh: 稍遷直閣將軍、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General of the Direct Gate and Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became gradually promoted to General of the Direct Gate and Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 爾硃兆入洛，孝直以天下未寧，去職歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Xiaozhi, seeing the realm still unsettled, left office and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Xiaozhi, seeing the realm still unsettled, left office and returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 太昌中，除衛將軍、右光祿大夫，辭不赴。

translations.literal: During Taichang, he was appointed General of the Guard and Grand Master with the Right Seal; he declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: During Taichang, he was appointed General of the Guard and Grand Master with the Right Seal; he declined and did not go, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，誡諸子曰：「吾才疏效薄，于國無功。

translations.literal: He died at home, admonishing his sons: "My talent is meager and my achievements slight; I have been of no use to the state.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home, admonishing his sons, "My talent is meager and my achievements slight; I have been of no use to the state.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷復加贈諡，宜循吾意，不得祗受。

translations.literal: If the court again adds posthumous honors, you should follow my wish and not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: If the court again adds posthumous honors, you should follow my wish and not accept them, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 若致幹求，則非吾意。

translations.literal: If you importune for them, that is not my intent.
translations.idiomatic: If you importune for them, that is not my intent, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 」子士順，位太府卿。

translations.literal: "His son Shishun held the post of Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shishun held the post of Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 孝直弟孝政，字季讓。

translations.literal: Xiaozhi's younger brother Xiaozheng, styled Jirang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhi's younger brother Xiaozheng, courtesy name Jirang.

sentences.zh: 十歲挺亡，號哭不絕，見者為之悲慘。

translations.literal: When Ting died, Xiaozheng was ten; he wailed without cease, and those who saw him were moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: After Ting died, Xiaozheng was ten; he wailed without cease, and those who saw him were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 志尚貞立，博學經史，雅好辭賦。

translations.literal: His aspirations were upright; he was broadly learned in the classics and histories and fond of rhapsodies and fu.
translations.idiomatic: His aspirations were upright; he was broadly learned in the classics and histories and fond of rhapsodies and fu, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 喪紀特所留情，衣服制度，手能執造。

translations.literal: Mourning rites were what he especially attended to; as for clothing and regulations, his hand could execute and make them.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites were what he especially attended to; as for clothing and regulations, he could execute and make them himself.

sentences.zh: 位太尉汝南王悅行參軍。

translations.literal: He held the post of traveling aide to Prince Yu of Runan, Grand Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of traveling aide to Prince Yu of Runan, Grand Minister of War, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 孝芬兄弟孝義慈厚，弟孝演、孝政先亡，孝芬等哭泣哀慟，絕肉蔬食，容貌毀瘠，見者傷之。

translations.literal: The Xiaofen brothers were filial, righteous, kind, and generous; their younger brothers Xiaoyan and Xiaozheng died first, and Xiaofen and the others wept and mourned, abstaining from meat and eating vegetables, their appearance wasted and emaciated—those who saw them were grieved.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaofen brothers were filial, righteous, kind, and generous; their younger brothers Xiaoyan and Xiaozheng died first, and Xiaofen and the others wept and mourned, abstaining from meat and eating vegetables, their appearance wasted and emaciated—those who saw them were grieved, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 孝偉等奉孝芬盡恭順之禮，坐食進退，孝芬不命則不敢也。

translations.literal: Xiaowei and the others served Xiaofen with full respectful obedience; in sitting, eating, advancing, and withdrawing, they dared not act without Xiaofen's command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowei and the others served Xiaofen with full respectful obedience; in sitting, eating, advancing, and withdrawing, they dared not act without Xiaofen's command, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 雞鳴而起，且溫顏色，一錢尺帛，不入私房，吉凶有須，聚對分給。

translations.literal: They rose at cockcrow and always with gentle countenance; not a coin or foot of silk entered their private rooms—whatever was needed for fortune or calamity they gathered and divided among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They rose at cockcrow and always with gentle countenance; not a coin or foot of silk entered their private rooms—whatever was needed for fortune or calamity they gathered and divided among themselves, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 諸婦亦相親愛，有無共之。

translations.literal: The wives also loved one another and shared whatever they had.
translations.idiomatic: The wives also loved one another and shared whatever they had, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 始挺兄弟同居，孝芬叔振既亡後，孝芬等承奉叔母李氏，若事所生。

translations.literal: Originally Ting's brothers lived together; after Ting's younger brother Zhen died, Xiaofen and the others served their aunt Lady Li as if she were their own mother.
translations.idiomatic: At first, Ting's brothers lived together; after Ting's younger brother Zhen died, Xiaofen and the others served their aunt Lady Li as if she were their own mother.

sentences.zh: 旦夕溫清，出入啟覲，家事巨細，一以諮決。

translations.literal: Morning and evening they attended to her comfort; entering and leaving they reported and paid respects; great and small household matters were all referred to her for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning and evening they attended to her comfort; entering and leaving they reported and paid respects; great and small household matters were all referred to her for decision.

sentences.zh: 每兄弟出行，有獲財物，尺寸以上，皆入李之庫；

translations.literal: Whenever the brothers went out and obtained property, anything above an inch in size all went into Lady Li's storehouse;
translations.idiomatic: In sum: whenever the brothers went out and obtained property, anything above an inch in size all went into Lady Li's storehouse;

sentences.zh: 四時分齎，李氏自裁之，如此二十餘歲。

translations.literal: At the four seasons they distributed shares, and Lady Li herself decided the allotments—thus for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: During the four seasons they distributed shares, and Lady Li herself decided the allotments—thus for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 撫從弟宣伯、子朗，如同氣焉。

translations.literal: They reared their younger cousin Xuanbo and Zilang as if they were full brothers.
translations.idiomatic: They reared their younger cousins Xuanbo and Zilang as if they were full brothers.

sentences.zh: 挺弟振。

translations.literal: Ting's younger brother Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's younger brother was Zhen.

sentences.zh: 振字延根。

translations.literal: Zhen, styled Yangen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, courtesy name Yangen.

sentences.zh: 少有學行，居家孝，為宗族所稱。

translations.literal: From youth he had learning and conduct; at home he was filial and was praised by the clan.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had learning and conduct; at home he was filial and was praised by the clan, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 為秘書中散，在內謹敕，為孝文所知。

translations.literal: He was Attendant Scribe in the Secretariat; within the palace he was careful and disciplined and was known to Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: He became Attendant Scribe in the Secretariat; within the palace he was careful and disciplined and was known to Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 孝文南討，自高陽內史征兼尚書左丞，留京。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, he was summoned from Administrator of Gaoyang to serve concurrently as Left Director of the Ministry and remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, he was summoned from Administrator of Gaoyang to serve concurrently as Left Director of the Ministry and remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 振既才幹被擢，當世以為榮。

translations.literal: Since Zhen's talent and ability had been promoted, the age regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhen's talent and ability had been promoted, the age regarded it as an honor, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 遷太子庶子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He became transferred to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 景明初，除長兼廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, he was appointed long-term concurrent Vice Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: During the beginning of Jingming, he was appointed long-term concurrent Vice Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 振有公斷，以明察稱。

translations.literal: Zhen had public judgment and was known for clear-sightedness.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhen had public judgment and was known for clear-sightedness.

sentences.zh: 河內太守陸琇與咸陽王禧同謀為逆，禧敗事發，振窮案之。

translations.literal: Administrator of Henei Lu Xiu plotted rebellion together with Prince Xianyang of Wei; when Xi's plot failed and was exposed, Zhen exhaustively investigated the case.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Henei Lu Xiu plotted rebellion together with Prince Xianyang of Wei; when Xi's plot failed and was exposed, Zhen exhaustively investigated the case, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 時琇內外親黨及當朝貴要咸為言之，振研核切至，終無縱緩，遂斃之於獄。

translations.literal: At the time inner and outer kin of Xiu and the powerful and important of the court all spoke for him, but Zhen's investigation was thorough to the end and he never relaxed; Xiu was thereupon executed in prison.
translations.idiomatic: During the time inner and outer kin of Xiu and the powerful and important of the court all spoke for him, but Zhen's investigation was thorough to the end and he never relaxed; Xiu was thereupon executed in prison.

sentences.zh: 其奉法如此。

translations.literal: Such was his adherence to law.
translations.idiomatic: This was his adherence to law.

sentences.zh: 除肆州刺史，在任有政績。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Si province and had achievements in office.
translations.idiomatic: He became appointed Governor of Si province and had achievements in office.

sentences.zh: 卒于河東太守，贈南兗州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died as Administrator of Hedong; posthumously he was granted Governor of Southern Yan province with the posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Administrator of Hedong; posthumously he was granted Governor of Southern Yan province with the posthumous name Ding, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 振曆官四十餘載，考課恆為稱職，議者善之。

translations.literal: Zhen served in office for more than forty years; his merit examinations were constantly rated competent—commentators approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhen served in office for more than forty years; his merit examinations were constantly rated competent—commentators approved of this.

sentences.zh: 子子朗，美容貌，涉獵經史，少溫厚，有風尚。

translations.literal: His son Zilang had a handsome appearance, ranged through the classics and histories, was gentle and mild from youth, and had bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Zilang had a handsome appearance, ranged through the classics and histories, was gentle and mild from youth, and had bearing.

sentences.zh: 位侍御史，加平東將軍，卒。

translations.literal: He held the post of Attending Censor and was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Attending Censor and was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East; he died, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 挺從父子瑜，字仲璉，少孤，有學業，位鴻臚少卿，封高邑男，贈瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Ting's younger male cousin's son Ziyu, styled Zhonglian, was orphaned early, had learning and achievement, held the post of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyi, and was posthumously granted Governor of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's younger male cousin's son Ziyu, courtesy name Zhonglian, was orphaned early, had learning and achievement, held the post of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyi, and was posthumously granted Governor of Ying province.

sentences.zh: 子孟舒，字長才，襲父爵，位廣平太守。

translations.literal: His son Mengshu, styled Changcai, inherited his father's title and held the post of Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mengshu, courtesy name Changcai, inherited his father's title and held the post of Administrator of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈殷州刺史、鎮東將軍，諡曰康。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted Governor of Yin province and General Who Guards the East with the posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: After he died, he was posthumously granted Governor of Yin province and General Who Guards the East with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 孟舒弟仲舒，位鄴縣令。

translations.literal: Mengshu's younger brother Zhongshu held the post of magistrate of Ye county.
translations.idiomatic: Mengshu's younger brother Zhongshu held the post of magistrate of Ye county, as the record states.

sentences.zh: 仲舒弟季舒，最知名。

translations.literal: Zhongshu's younger brother Jishu was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Among Zhongshu's brothers, Jishu was the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 季舒字叔正。

translations.literal: Jishu, styled Shuzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu, courtesy name Shuzheng.

sentences.zh: 少孤，性明敏，涉獵經史，長於尺牘，有當世才具。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he was bright and keen by nature, ranged through classics and histories, excelled at official correspondence, and had the talent and capacity of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he was bright and keen, versed in classics and histories, excelled at official correspondence, and possessed the talent the age demanded.

sentences.zh: 年十七，為州主簿。

translations.literal: At seventeen he was chief clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he served as chief clerk of the province.

sentences.zh: 為大將軍、趙郡公琛所器重，言之齊神武。

translations.literal: He was valued by Grand General Duke of Zhao Chen and was recommended to Gao Huan of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Duke of Zhao Chen valued him and recommended him to Gao Huan of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 神武親簡丞郎，補季舒大行台都官郎中。

translations.literal: Gao Huan personally selected assistant directors and gentlemen and appointed Jishu as Gentleman in the Justice Bureau of the Great Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan personally selected assistant directors and appointed Jishu Gentleman in the Justice Bureau of the Great Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 文襄輔政，轉大將軍中兵參軍，甚見親寵。

translations.literal: When Wen Xiang assisted in government, Jishu was transferred to military aide under the Grand General and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Xiang assisted in government, Jishu became military aide under the Grand General and was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 以魏帝左右，須置腹心，擢拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Because the Wei emperor needed trusted men at his side, Jishu was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, because the Wei emperor needed trusted men at his side, Jishu was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文襄為中書監，移門下機事，總歸中書。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang served as Director of the Secretariat; affairs of the Secretariat Gate were transferred to the Secretariat in total.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang served as Director of the Secretariat; all Secretariat Gate affairs were transferred to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又季舒善音樂，故內伎亦回隸焉。

translations.literal: Moreover Jishu was skilled in music, so inner-court performers also came under his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu was also skilled in music, so inner-court performers came under his jurisdiction as well.

sentences.zh: 內伎屬中書，自季舒始也。

translations.literal: Inner-court performers belonging to the Secretariat began with Jishu.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-court performers under the Secretariat began with Jishu.

sentences.zh: 文襄每進書魏帝，有所諫請，或文詞繁雜，季舒輒修飾通之，得申勸戒而已。

translations.literal: Whenever Wen Xiang submitted memorials to the Wei emperor with remonstrances or requests, if the wording was complex, Jishu would revise and clarify them so that admonition and warning could be conveyed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wen Xiang submitted memorials to the Wei emperor, if the wording grew complex, Jishu would revise and clarify them so admonition could get through.

sentences.zh: 靜帝報答霸朝，恆與季舒論之，雲崔中書是我妳母。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing in replying to the hegemonic court always discussed matters with Jishu, saying Cui Vice Director is my wet nurse.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, in replying to the hegemonic court, always discussed matters with Jishu, calling Vice Director Cui his wet nurse.

sentences.zh: 轉給事黃門侍郎，領主衣都統。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and overseer of the Directorate of Imperial Robes.
translations.idiomatic: He also was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and overseer of the Directorate of Imperial Robes.

sentences.zh: 雖跡在魏朝，而歸心霸府，密謀大計，皆得預聞。

translations.literal: Though his traces were in the Wei court, his heart belonged to the hegemonic headquarters; in secret planning of great affairs he was always allowed to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served the Wei court, his heart belonged to the hegemonic headquarters; he was always privy to secret planning of great affairs.

sentences.zh: 於是賓客輻湊，傾身接禮，甚得名譽，勢傾崔暹。

translations.literal: Thereupon guests gathered like wheel spokes; he bent himself to receive and honor them and gained great reputation; his power rivaled Cui Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Guests then gathered in crowds; he received them with full courtesy and gained great reputation; his power rivaled Cui Xian.

sentences.zh: 暹嘗於朝堂屏人拜之曰：「暹若得僕射，皆叔父之恩。

translations.literal: Xian once bowed to him in the hall with others dismissed, saying: "If Xian obtains the post of Vice Minister, it is all thanks to my uncle's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Xian once bowed to him in the hall with others dismissed, saying, "If I obtain the post of Vice Minister, it is all thanks to my uncle's grace.

sentences.zh: 」其權重如此。

translations.literal: "Such was the weight of his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the weight of his authority.

sentences.zh: 時勳貴多不法，文襄無所縱舍，外議以季舒及崔暹等所為，甚被怨嫉。

translations.literal: At the time meritorious nobles often acted unlawfully; Wen Xiang showed no leniency, and outside opinion blamed Jishu, Cui Xian, and others for this and greatly resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious nobles often acted unlawfully; Wen Xiang showed no leniency, and outside opinion blamed Jishu, Cui Xian, and others and greatly resented them.

sentences.zh: 及文襄遇難，文宣將赴晉陽，黃門郎陽休之勸季舒從，曰：「一日不朝，其間容刀。

translations.literal: When Wen Xiang met disaster, Wen Xuan was about to go to Jinyang; Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yang Xiuzhi urged Jishu to follow, saying: "One day absent from court, and a knife may fit between.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Xiang met disaster, Wen Xuan was about to go to Jinyang; Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yang Xiuzhi urged Jishu to follow, saying, "One day absent from court, and a knife may fit between.

sentences.zh: 」季舒性愛聲色，心在閑放，遂不請行，欲恣其行樂。

translations.literal: "Jishu by nature loved music and women; his heart was set on leisure, so he did not request to go, wishing to indulge his pleasures.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu by nature loved music and women; his heart was set on leisure, so he did not go, wishing to indulge his pleasures.

sentences.zh: 司馬子如緣宿憾，及尚食典禦陳山提等列其過狀。

translations.literal: Sima Ziru, owing to old resentment, together with Director of Imperial Food Chen Shanti and others listed his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, sima Ziru, owing to old resentment, together with Director of Imperial Food Chen Shanti and others listed his faults.

sentences.zh: 由是季舒及暹各鞭二百，徙北邊。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jishu and Xian were each flogged two hundred strokes and exiled to the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu and Xian were each flogged two hundred strokes and exiled to the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 天保初，文宣知其無罪，追為將作大匠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Wen Xuan knew they were innocent and recalled Jishu as Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, at the beginning of Tianbao, Wen Xuan knew they were innocent and recalled Jishu as Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍中，俄兼尚書左僕射、儀同三司，大被恩遇。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Palace Attendant and soon concurrently served as Left Vice Minister and Palace Attendant of the Third Order, greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: He also was again promoted to Palace Attendant and soon concurrently served as Left Vice Minister and Palace Attendant of the Third Order, greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 乾明初，楊愔以文宣遺旨，停其僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ganming, Yang Yin, following Emperor Wenxuan's final instructions, removed him from Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, at the beginning of Ganming, Yang Yin, following Emperor Wenxuan's final instructions, removed him from Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪解任。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he left office.

sentences.zh: 起服，除光祿勳，兼中兵尚書。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Director of the Imperial Household and concurrently Minister of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, he was appointed Director of the Imperial Household and concurrently Minister of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 出為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: He also was sent out as Governor of Qi province.

sentences.zh: 坐遣人度淮平市，亦有贓賄事，為御史所劾，會赦不問。

translations.literal: For sending men across the Huai to trade in the market and for accepting bribes, he was impeached by the censor; an amnesty intervened and he was not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: For sending men across the Huai to trade and for accepting bribes, he was impeached by the censor; an amnesty intervened and he was not questioned.

sentences.zh: 武成居籓，曾病，文宣令季舒療病，備盡心力。

translations.literal: When Wucheng was in the princely residence he once fell ill; Wen Xuan ordered Jishu to treat the illness and he exhausted his mind and strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng was in the princely residence he once fell ill; Wen Xuan ordered Jishu to treat the illness, and he gave all his mind and strength.

sentences.zh: 大寧初，追還，引入慰勉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daning he was recalled and summoned in and comforted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daning he was recalled, summoned in, and comforted.

sentences.zh: 累遷度支尚書、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Revenue Bureau and Palace Attendant of the Third Order with an opening office.
translations.idiomatic: He also was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Revenue Bureau and Palace Attendant of the Third Order with an opening office.

sentences.zh: 營昭陽殿，敕令監造，以判事式。

translations.literal: When constructing Zhaoyang Palace, an edict ordered him to supervise construction and set the pattern for judging affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After constructing Zhaoyang Palace, an edict ordered him to supervise construction and set the pattern for judging affairs.

sentences.zh: 為胡長仁密言其短，出為西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Hu Changren secretly spoke of his faults, and he was sent out as Governor of Western Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, hu Changren secretly spoke of his faults, and he was sent out as Governor of Western Yan province.

sentences.zh: 為進典簽於吏部，被責免官。

translations.literal: For advancing a chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel he was rebuked and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, for advancing a chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel he was rebuked and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 又以詣廣甯王宅，決韋鞭數十。

translations.literal: Also for going to Prince of Guangning's residence, he was sentenced to several dozen strokes of the leather whip.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, also for going to Prince of Guangning's residence, he was sentenced to several dozen strokes of the leather whip.

sentences.zh: 及武成崩，不得預於哭泣。

translations.literal: When Wucheng died, he was not allowed to join in the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After Wucheng died, he was not allowed to join in the mourning.

sentences.zh: 久之，除膠州刺史，遷侍中、開府，食新安、河陰二郡幹。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Governor of Jiao province, promoted to Palace Attendant and opening office, with income from the Gan districts of Xin'an and Heyin commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, after a long time he was appointed Governor of Jiao province, promoted to Palace Attendant and opening office, with income from the Gan districts of Xin'an and Heyin commanderies.

sentences.zh: 加左光祿大夫，待詔文林館，監撰《御覽》。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Grand Master with the Left Seal, awaited edicts at the Forest of Literature, and supervised compilation of the Imperial Overview.
translations.idiomatic: He also was given the additional title Grand Master with the Left Seal, awaited edicts at the Forest of Literature, and supervised compilation of the Imperial Overview.

sentences.zh: 加特進，監國史。

translations.literal: He was given special advancement and supervised the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He also was given special advancement and supervised the national history.

sentences.zh: 季舒素好圖籍，暮年轉更精勤，兼推薦人士，獎勸文學，議聲翕然，遠近稱美。

translations.literal: Jishu had always loved books; in his later years he became even more diligent and also recommended men of talent, encouraging literature—opinion united in praise, and he was acclaimed near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu had always loved books; in his later years he grew even more diligent, recommended men of talent, and encouraged literature—opinion united in praise near and far.

sentences.zh: 祖珽受委，奏季舒總監內作。

translations.literal: Zu Ting received appointment and memorialized that Jishu should overall supervise inner construction.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, zu Ting received appointment and memorialized that Jishu should overall supervise inner construction.

sentences.zh: 珽被出，韓長鸞以為珽黨，亦欲出之。

translations.literal: When Ting was sent out, Han Changluan regarded Jishu as Ting's faction and also wished to send him out.
translations.idiomatic: After Ting was sent out, Han Changluan regarded Jishu as Ting's faction and also wished to send him out.

sentences.zh: 屬車駕將適晉陽，季舒與張雕議，以為壽春被圍，大軍出拒，言使往還，須稟節度。

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to go to Jinyang, Jishu and Zhang Diao deliberated that since Shou-chun was besieged and the great army went out to resist, messengers going back and forth required orders from headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial carriage was about to go to Jinyang, Jishu and Zhang Diao argued that since Shou-chun was besieged and the great army had gone out to resist, messengers required orders from headquarters.

sentences.zh: 兼道路小人，或相驚恐，雲大駕向并州，畏避南寇，若不啟諫，必動人情。

translations.literal: Moreover petty men on the road might spread alarm, saying the great carriage was going to Bing province to flee southern invaders; if they did not remonstrate, human hearts would surely be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover petty men on the road might spread alarm, saying the great carriage was going to Bing province to flee southern invaders; if they did not remonstrate, hearts would surely be shaken.

sentences.zh: 遂與從駕文官，連名進諫。

translations.literal: They thereupon joined the civil officials accompanying the carriage and submitted a joint memorial of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: They joined the civil officials accompanying the carriage and submitted a joint memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 時貴臣趙彥深、唐邕、段孝言等初亦同心，臨時疑貳，季舒與爭，未決。

translations.literal: At the time eminent ministers Zhao Yanshen, Tang Yong, and Duan Xiaoyan were at first of one mind; at the moment they wavered, and Jishu argued with them without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Eminent ministers Zhao Yanshen, Tang Yong, and Duan Xiaoyan were at first of one mind; at the moment they wavered, and Jishu argued with them without resolution.

sentences.zh: 長鸞遂奏云：「漢兒文官，連名總署，聲雲諫止向并州，其實未必不反，宜加誅戮。

translations.literal: Changluan thereupon memorialized: "Han civil officials jointly signed a memorial, claiming to remonstrate against going to Bing province; in fact they may not have been unwilling to rebel—they should be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Changluan memorialized, "Han civil officials jointly signed a memorial, claiming to remonstrate against going to Bing province; in fact they may have intended rebellion—they should be put to death.

sentences.zh: 」帝即召已署表官人集含章殿，以季舒、張雕、劉逖、封孝琰、裴澤、郭遵等為首，並斬之殿庭。

translations.literal: "The emperor immediately summoned the officials who had signed the memorial to gather in Hanzhang Hall; taking Jishu, Zhang Diao, Liu Ti, Feng Xiaoyan, Pei Ze, Guo Zun, and others as ringleaders, they were all beheaded in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the officials who had signed to Hanzhang Hall; Jishu, Zhang Diao, Liu Ti, Feng Xiaoyan, Pei Ze, Guo Zun, and others were taken as ringleaders and beheaded in the hall.

sentences.zh: 長鸞令棄其屍于漳水。

translations.literal: Changluan ordered their corpses thrown into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: Han Changluan ordered their corpses thrown into the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 自外同署，將加鞭撻，趙彥深執諫獲免。

translations.literal: Of the others who signed jointly, whipping was to be added; Zhao Yanshen remonstrated firmly and they were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, of the others who signed jointly, whipping was to be added; Zhao Yanshen remonstrated firmly and they were spared.

sentences.zh: 季舒等家屬男女徙北邊，妻女及子婦配奚官，小男下蠶室，沒入貲產。

translations.literal: The families of Jishu and the others—men and women—were exiled to the northern frontier; wives, daughters, and daughters-in-law were assigned to the washerwomen's office; young sons were sent to the silkworm chamber; property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The families of Jishu and the others were exiled to the northern frontier; wives, daughters, and daughters-in-law were assigned to the washerwomen's office; young sons were sent to the silkworm chamber; property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 季舒本好醫術，天保中於徙所無事，更銳意研精，遂為名手，多所全濟。

translations.literal: Jishu had originally loved medicine; during Tianbao at the place of exile with nothing to do, he applied himself even more keenly and became a master, saving many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu had originally loved medicine; during Tianbao at the place of exile he applied himself even more keenly and became a master, saving many lives.

sentences.zh: 雖位望轉高，未曾懈怠；

translations.literal: Though rank and standing grew ever higher, he never slackened;
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, though rank and standing grew ever higher, he never slackened;

sentences.zh: 縱貧賤廝養，亦為之療護。

translations.literal: even for poor and lowly servants he also treated and cared for them.
translations.idiomatic: even for poor and lowly servants he treated and cared for them.

sentences.zh: 庶子長君，尚書右外兵郎中。

translations.literal: His son Changjun held the post of Gentleman in the Right Bureau of Military Affairs of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, his son Changjun held the post of Gentleman in the Right Bureau of Military Affairs of the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 次鏡玄，著作佐郎。

translations.literal: The second, Jingxuan, was Assistant Director of the History Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, the second, Jingxuan, was Assistant Director of the History Bureau.

sentences.zh: 並流于長城。

translations.literal: Both were exiled to the Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: The two were were exiled to the Great Wall.

sentences.zh: 未幾，季舒等六人妻，以年老放出。

translations.literal: Before long, the wives of the six men including Jishu were released because of age.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, before long, the wives of the six men including Jishu were released because of age.

sentences.zh: 後南安王思好更稱朝廷罪惡，以季舒等見害為詞，悉召六人兄弟子侄隨軍趣晉陽。

translations.literal: Later Prince of Nanan Sihai again proclaimed the court's crimes and evils, using the killing of Jishu and the others as a pretext; he summoned all six men's brothers, sons, and nephews to follow the army toward Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince of Nanan Sihai proclaimed the court's crimes, using the killing of Jishu and the others as a pretext; he summoned all six men's brothers, sons, and nephews to follow the army toward Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 事敗，長君等並從戮。

translations.literal: When the affair failed, Changjun and the others were all executed with the army.
translations.idiomatic: After the affair failed, Changjun and the others were all executed with the army.

sentences.zh: 六人之妻，又追入官。

translations.literal: The wives of the six men were again seized into official service.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, the wives of the six men were again seized into official service.

sentences.zh: 周武帝滅齊，詔斛律光與季舒等六人同被優贈，季舒贈開府儀同大將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou destroyed Qi, an edict together with Hulu Guang and the other six men including Jishu granted them posthumous honors; Jishu was granted Grand General with an opening office of the Second Order and Governor of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou destroyed Qi, an edict together with Hulu Guang and the other six granted them posthumous honors; Jishu was granted Grand General with an opening office of the Second Order and Governor of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 挺從祖弟敬邕，性長者，為左中郎將，以軍功賜爵臨淄男，位營州刺史。

translations.literal: Ting's younger male cousin Jingyong was by nature a man of integrity, served as Left Palace Gentleman, was granted the title Baron of Linzi for military merit, and held the post of Governor of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's younger male cousin Jingyong was by nature a man of integrity, served as Left Palace Gentleman, was enfeoffed as Baron of Linzi for military merit, and governed Ying province.

sentences.zh: 庫莫奚國有馬數百疋，因風入境，敬邕悉令送還，於是夷人感附。

translations.literal: The Kumo Xi state had several hundred horses that entered the border on the wind; Jingyong ordered them all sent back, and the barbarians were moved to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Kumo Xi had several hundred horses that entered the border on the wind; Jingyong ordered them all sent back, and the barbarians were moved to submit.

sentences.zh: 卒于太中大夫，贈濟州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died as Grand Master of the Palace and was posthumously granted Governor of Ji province with the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He also died as Grand Master of the Palace and was posthumously granted Governor of Ji province with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 敬邕從弟接，字願賓。

translations.literal: Jingyong's younger male cousin Jie, styled Yuanbin.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyong's younger male cousin Jie, courtesy name Yuanbin.

sentences.zh: 容貌魁偉，放邁自高，不拘檢。

translations.literal: His appearance was towering and heroic; he was unrestrained and self-exalted, not bound by restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, his appearance was towering and heroic; he was unrestrained and self-exalted, not bound by restraint.

sentences.zh: 為中書博士、樂陵內史。

translations.literal: He was Doctor of the Secretariat and Internal Administrator of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: He also was Doctor of the Secretariat and Internal Administrator of Leling.

sentences.zh: 雅為任城王澄所禮待，及澄為本部，接了無人王敬，王忻然容下之。

translations.literal: He was always treated with courtesy by Prince of Rencheng Wang Cheng; when Cheng was in his home commandery, Jie showed none of a subject's respect, yet the prince gladly accommodated him.
translations.idiomatic: He was always treated with courtesy by Wang Cheng, Prince of Rencheng; when Cheng was in his home commandery, Jie showed none of a subject's respect, yet the prince gladly accommodated him.

sentences.zh: 後為樂陵太守，還鄉卒。

translations.literal: Later he was Administrator of Leling, returned to his home district, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, later he was Administrator of Leling, returned to his home district, and died.

sentences.zh: 挺族子纂，字叔則。

translations.literal: Ting's clansman Zuan, styled Shize.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's clansman Zuan, courtesy name Shize.

sentences.zh: 博學有文才，既不為時知，乃著《無談子論》。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with literary talent, since he was not recognized by the age he wrote the Wutanzi Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, broadly learned with literary talent, since he was not recognized by the age he wrote the Wutanzi Lun.

sentences.zh: 尋為廷尉正，每有大獄，多所據明，有當官之譽。

translations.literal: Soon he was Director of Justice; in major cases he often clarified the basis and had a reputation for upholding office.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, soon he was Director of Justice; in major cases he often clarified the basis and had a reputation for upholding office.

sentences.zh: 時太原王靜自廷尉監遷少卿，纂恥居其下，乃與靜書，辭氣抑揚，無上下禮。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jing of Taiyuan was transferred from prison supervisor to Vice Director; Zuan was ashamed to rank below him and wrote to Jing with language of praise and blame, without the etiquette of superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Jing of Taiyuan was transferred from prison supervisor to Vice Director; Zuan was ashamed to rank below him and wrote to Jing without the etiquette of superior and inferior.

sentences.zh: 入啟求解位。

translations.literal: He entered and memorialized requesting release from his post.
translations.idiomatic: He also entered and memorialized requesting release from his post.

sentences.zh: 後為洛陽令，卒，贈司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Later he was magistrate of Luoyang, died, and was posthumously granted Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, later he was magistrate of Luoyang, died, and was posthumously granted Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 纂兄穆，字子和，雅有度量，州辟主簿，卒。

translations.literal: Zuan's elder brother Mu, styled Zihe, had elegant measure; the province recruited him as chief clerk and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's elder brother Mu, courtesy name Zihe, had elegant measure; the province recruited him as chief clerk and he died.

sentences.zh: 穆子暹。

translations.literal: Mu's son Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's son was Xian.

sentences.zh: 暹字季倫。

translations.literal: Xian, styled Jilun.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, courtesy name Jilun.

sentences.zh: 少為書生，避地勃海，依高乾，以妹妻其弟慎。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student; fleeing to Bohai he relied on Gao Gan and married his sister to Gan's younger brother Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, in youth he was a student; fleeing to Bohai he relied on Gao Gan and married his sister to Gan's younger brother Shen.

sentences.zh: 慎後臨滄、光二州，啟暹為工史，委以職事。

translations.literal: When Shen later governed Cang and Guang provinces, he recommended Xian as works clerk and entrusted him with duties.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen later governed Cang and Guang provinces, he recommended Xian as works clerk and entrusted him with duties.

sentences.zh: 趙郡公琛鎮定州，辟為開府諮議，隨琛往晉陽。

translations.literal: Duke of Zhao Chen garrisoned Ding province and recruited Xian as opening-office adviser; he followed Chen to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, duke of Zhao Chen garrisoned Ding province and recruited Xian as opening-office adviser; he followed Chen to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 神武與語悅之，以兼丞相長史。

translations.literal: Gao Huan spoke with him and was pleased, appointing him concurrent chief administrator under the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, gao Huan spoke with him and was pleased, appointing him concurrent chief administrator under the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 神武舉兵將入洛，留暹佐琛，凡百後事，一以屬暹，握手殷勤，至於三四。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan raised troops to enter Luoyang, he left Xian to assist Chen; all later affairs were entirely entrusted to Xian, with earnest handclasp three or four times.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised troops to enter Luoyang, he left Xian to assist Chen; all later affairs were entrusted to Xian, with earnest handclasp three or four times.

sentences.zh: 琛後以罪被責，暹亦黜免。

translations.literal: Chen was later punished for a crime; Xian was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, chen was later punished for a crime; Xian was also dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尉景為并州，起暹為別駕。

translations.literal: Wei Jing was commander of Bing province and appointed Xian as vice administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, wei Jing was commander of Bing province and appointed Xian as vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 文襄代景，轉暹為開府諮議，仍行別駕事。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang replaced Jing and transferred Xian to opening-office adviser, still acting as vice administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, wen Xiang replaced Jing and transferred Xian to opening-office adviser, still acting as vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 從文襄鎮撫鄴都，加散騎常侍，遷左丞、吏部郎，領定州大中正，主議《麟趾格》。

translations.literal: Following Wen Xiang in pacifying and settling Ye capital, he was given the additional title Palace Attendant, promoted to Left Director and Gentleman of the Ministry, overseer of Grand Assessor of Ding province, and presided over deliberation of the Linzhi regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Following Wen Xiang in pacifying Ye capital, he was given the additional title Palace Attendant, promoted to Left Director and Gentleman of the Ministry, overseer of Grand Assessor of Ding province, and presided over deliberation of the Linzhi regulations.

sentences.zh: 暹親遇日隆，好薦人士，言邢邵宜親重。

translations.literal: Xian's personal favor grew daily; he liked recommending men of talent and said Xing Shao should be treated with special respect.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, xian's personal favor grew daily; he liked recommending men of talent and said Xing Shao should be treated with special respect.

sentences.zh: 言論之際，邵遂毀暹。

translations.literal: In the course of discussion Shao thereupon slandered Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, in the course of discussion Shao thereupon slandered Xian.

sentences.zh: 文襄不悅，謂暹曰：「卿說子才長，子才專言卿短，此癡人也。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang was displeased and said to Xian: "You say Zicai is long in merit; Zicai exclusively speaks of your faults—this is a foolish man.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang was displeased and said to Xian, "You say Zicai has great merit; Zicai exclusively speaks of your faults—this is a foolish man.

sentences.zh: 」暹曰：「子才言暹短，暹說子才長，皆是實事，不為癡也。

translations.literal: "Xian said: "Zicai speaks of Xian's faults; Xian speaks of Zicai's merits—both are true matters, not foolishness.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "Zicai speaks of my faults; I speak of Zicai's merits—both are true matters, not foolishness.

sentences.zh: 」高慎之叛，偽與暹隙，神武后知之，欲發其事而殺暹，文襄苦救得止。

translations.literal: "When Gao Shen rebelled he falsely claimed enmity with Xian; Gao Huan later learned of it and wished to expose the matter and kill Xian; Wen Xiang strenuously saved him and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Shen rebelled he falsely claimed enmity with Xian; Gao Huan later learned of it and wished to expose the matter and kill Xian; Wen Xiang strenuously saved him and it stopped.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中尉，選畢義雲、盧潛、宋欽道、李愔、崔贍、杜蕤、嵇曄、酈伯偉、崔子武、李廣皆為御史，世稱其知人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Imperial Censor; Bi Yiyun, Lu Qian, Song Qindao, Li Yin, Cui Zhan, Du Rui, Ji Ye, Li Bowei, Cui Ziwu, and Li Guang were all selected as censors—the age praised his discernment of men.
translations.idiomatic: He also was promoted to Imperial Censor; Bi Yiyun, Lu Qian, Song Qindao, Li Yin, Cui Zhan, Du Rui, Ji Ye, Li Bowei, Cui Ziwu, and Li Guang were all selected as censors—the age praised his discernment of men.

sentences.zh: 文襄欲假暹威勢，諸公在坐朝，令暹後通名，因待以殊禮。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang wished to borrow Xian's authority; when the lords were seated at court audience, he ordered Xian to announce his name afterward and treated him with special ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, wen Xiang wished to borrow Xian's authority; when the lords were seated at court audience, he ordered Xian to announce his name afterward and treated him with special ceremony.

sentences.zh: 暹乃高視徐步，兩人擎裾而入，文襄分庭對揖。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon looked high and walked slowly; two men held his robe skirts as he entered, and Wen Xiang bowed facing him across the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xian looked high and walked slowly; two men held his robe skirts as he entered, and Wen Xiang bowed facing him across the hall.

sentences.zh: 暹不讓席而坐，觴再行，便辭退。

translations.literal: Xian did not yield the seat but sat down; after two rounds of wine he at once took leave.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, xian did not yield the seat but sat down; after two rounds of wine he at once took leave.

sentences.zh: 文襄曰：「下官薄有蔬食，公少留。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang said: "This humble office has a modest vegetarian meal; please stay a little.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang said, "This humble office has a modest vegetarian meal; please stay a little.

sentences.zh: 」暹曰：「適受敕，在台檢校。

translations.literal: Xian said: "I have just received orders to inspect at the headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "I have just received orders to inspect at the headquarters."

sentences.zh: 」遂不待食而去，文襄降送之。

translations.literal: He thereupon left without waiting for the meal; Wen Xiang descended to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: He left without waiting for the meal; Wen Xiang descended to see him off.

sentences.zh: 旬日後，文襄與諸公出之東山，遇暹在道，前驅為赤棒所擊，文襄回馬避之。

translations.literal: Ten days later Wen Xiang went out to Dongshan with the lords and met Xian on the road; the vanguard was struck by red clubs and Wen Xiang turned his horse to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Wen Xiang went to Dongshan with the lords and met Xian on the road; the vanguard was struck by red clubs and Wen Xiang turned his horse aside.
