sentences.zh: 暹前後表彈尚書令司馬子如，及尚書元羨、殷州刺史慕容獻，又彈太師司州牧咸陽王恆、并州刺史可硃渾道元、冀州刺史韓軌，罪與鄴下諸貴，極言褒美，且誡屬之。

translations.literal: Xian before and after memorialized and impeached Minister of Works Sima Ziru, Minister Yuan Xian, Administrator of Yin province Murong Xian, Grand Preceptor and Governor of Si province Prince Xianyang of Wei, Governor of Bing province Kezhuhun Daoyuan, and Governor of Ji province Han Gui—crimes and the nobles of Ye capital, speaking extreme praise and also admonishing his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Xian repeatedly memorialized against Minister of Works Sima Ziru, Minister Yuan Xian, Administrator of Yin Murong Xian, Grand Preceptor Prince Xianyang of Wei, Governor of Bing Kezhuhun Daoyuan, and Governor of Ji Han Gui—exposing crimes among the Ye nobles, praising some and admonishing others.

sentences.zh: 先是僧尼猥濫，暹奏設科條篇，沙門法上為昭玄都以檢約之。

translations.literal: Previously monks and nuns had been excessive in number; Xian memorialized to establish articles and sections; the monk Fashang was made Director of the Bureau of Buddhism to inspect and restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously monks and nuns had proliferated excessively; Xian memorialized to establish regulations, and the monk Fashang was made Director of the Bureau of Buddhism to inspect and restrain them.

sentences.zh: 神武如鄴，群官迎於紫陌。

translations.literal: Gao Huan went to Ye; officials welcomed him at Zimo Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, gao Huan went to Ye; officials welcomed him at Zimo Lane.

sentences.zh: 神武握暹手勞之曰：「小兒任重才輕，非中尉何有今日？

translations.literal: Gao Huan grasped Xian's hand and comforted him, saying: "The boy's burden is heavy and his talent slight; without the Imperial Censor, how could there be today?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan grasped Xian's hand and comforted him, saying, "The boy's burden is heavy and his talent slight; without the Imperial Censor, how could there be today?

sentences.zh: 榮華富貴，直是中尉自取，高歡父子無以相報。

translations.literal: Glory, wealth, and honor—you yourself obtained them, Imperial Censor; Gao Huan father and son have nothing with which to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, glory, wealth, and honor—you yourself obtained them, Imperial Censor; Gao Huan father and son have nothing with which to repay.

sentences.zh: 」賜暹馬，使騎之以從，且行且語。

translations.literal: "He granted Xian a horse and ordered him to ride and follow, talking as they went.
translations.idiomatic: He granted Xian a horse and ordered him to ride and follow, talking as they went.

sentences.zh: 暹下拜，馬驚走，神武親為擁之而授轡。

translations.literal: Xian bowed; the horse startled and ran; Gao Huan personally steadied it and handed him the reins.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, xian bowed; the horse startled and ran; Gao Huan personally steadied it and handed him the reins.

sentences.zh: 魏帝宴華林園，謂神武曰：「自頃所在百司，多有貪暴。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor banqueted at Hualin Garden and said to Gao Huan: "Recently in every place the hundred offices have often been greedy and violent.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor banqueted at Hualin Garden and said to Gao Huan, "Recently officials everywhere have often been greedy and violent.

sentences.zh: 朝廷中有用心公平，直言彈劾，不避親戚者，王可勸酒。

translations.literal: In the court there are those who use their hearts fairly, speak straight and impeach, and do not avoid kin—You may urge them to drink.
translations.idiomatic: In the court there are those who use their hearts fairly, speak straight and impeach, and do not avoid kin—you may urge them to drink.

sentences.zh: 」神武降階跪言：「唯御史中尉崔暹一人，謹奉明旨，敢以酒勸，並臣所射賜物千段，乞以回賜。

translations.literal: "Gao Huan descended the steps and knelt, saying: "Only Imperial Censor Cui Xian alone—your servant respectfully follows the clear edict and dares to urge wine, and also the thousand bolts of goods from my archery grant—your servant begs they be returned as gift.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan descended the steps and knelt, saying, "Only Imperial Censor Cui Xian alone—your servant respectfully follows the clear edict and dares to urge wine, and also the thousand bolts of goods from my archery grant—your servant begs they be returned as gift.

sentences.zh: 」帝又褒美之。

translations.literal: The emperor again praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, the emperor again praised him.

sentences.zh: 於是文襄亦催暹酒，神武親為之抃。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wen Xiang also urged Xian to drink; Gao Huan personally clapped for him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang also urged Xian to drink; Gao Huan personally clapped for him.

sentences.zh: 文襄退，謂暹曰：「我尚畏羨，何況餘人！

translations.literal: Wen Xiang withdrew and said to Xian: "I still fear Xian—how much more others!
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang withdrew and said to Xian, "I still fear Xian—how much more others!

sentences.zh: 」神武將還晉陽，又以所乘馬加彩物賜暹。

translations.literal: "When Gao Huan was about to return to Jinyang, he again granted the horse he rode plus colored goods to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan was about to return to Jinyang, he again granted the horse he rode plus colored goods to Xian.

sentences.zh: 由是威名日盛，內外莫不畏服。

translations.literal: From this his awesome name grew daily; inside and outside none did not fear and submit.
translations.idiomatic: From this his awesome name grew daily; none inside or outside failed to fear and submit.

sentences.zh: 神武崩，未發喪，文襄以暹為度支尚書，監國史，兼右僕射，委以心腹之寄，仍為魏帝侍讀。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan died, mourning was not yet announced; Wen Xiang appointed Xian Director of the Revenue Bureau, supervisor of the national history, concurrent Right Vice Minister, and entrusted him with matters of innermost confidence; he still served as the Wei emperor's reader.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, when Gao Huan died, mourning was not yet announced; Wen Xiang appointed Xian Director of the Revenue Bureau, supervisor of the national history, concurrent Right Vice Minister, and entrusted him with matters of innermost confidence; he still served as the Wei emperor's reader.

sentences.zh: 暹憂國如家，以天下為己任。

translations.literal: Xian grieved for the state as for his home and took the realm as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, xian grieved for the state as for his home and took the realm as his own responsibility.

sentences.zh: 文襄盛寵王昭儀，欲立為正室。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang greatly favored Lady Wang Zhaoyi and wished to establish her as principal consort.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, wen Xiang greatly favored Lady Wang Zhaoyi and wished to establish her as principal consort.

sentences.zh: 暹諫曰：「天命未改，魏室尚存，公主無罪，不容棄辱。

translations.literal: Xian remonstrated: "Heaven's mandate has not changed; the house of Wei still exists; the princess is without guilt and cannot be cast aside in disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Xian remonstrated, "Heaven's mandate has not changed; the house of Wei still exists; the princess is without guilt and cannot be cast aside in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 」文襄意不悅，苦請乃從之。

translations.literal: "Wen Xiang was displeased in mind but after strenuous pleading at last followed.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang was displeased but after strenuous pleading at last followed.

sentences.zh: 文襄車服過度，誅戮變常，言談進止，或有虧失。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang's carriages and robes exceeded measure; executions and killings were irregular; in speech and conduct in advancing and withdrawing there were sometimes faults.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang's carriages and robes exceeded measure; executions and killings were irregular; in speech and conduct there were sometimes faults.

sentences.zh: 暹每厲色極言，文襄亦為之止。

translations.literal: Xian each time spoke with stern countenance to the utmost; Wen Xiang also stopped on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, xian each time spoke with stern countenance to the utmost; Wen Xiang also stopped on his account.

sentences.zh: 臨淮王孝友被文襄狎愛，數歌舞戲謔于前，顧見暹，輒斂容而止。

translations.literal: Prince of Huaiyang Xiaoyou was treated with familiarity by Wen Xiang and often sang, danced, and jested before him; when he saw Xian he at once composed himself and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, prince of Huaiyang Xiaoyou was treated with familiarity by Wen Xiang and often sang, danced, and jested before him; when he saw Xian he at once composed himself and stopped.

sentences.zh: 有獄囚數百，文襄盡欲誅之，每催文帳，暹故緩之，不以時進，文襄意釋，竟免。

translations.literal: There were several hundred prisoners; Wen Xiang wished to execute them all; each time he urged the documents Xian deliberately delayed and did not submit in time; Wen Xiang's intent was released and they were ultimately spared.
translations.idiomatic: There were several hundred prisoners; Wen Xiang wished to execute them all; each time he urged the documents Xian deliberately delayed; Wen Xiang's intent was released and they were ultimately spared.

sentences.zh: 司州別駕司馬仲粲、中從事陸士佩並被文襄毆擊，付獄將餓殺，暹送食藥，為致言而釋之。

translations.literal: Vice Administrator of Si province Sima Zhongcan and attendant official Lu Shipi were both beaten by Wen Xiang, handed to prison to be starved to death; Xian sent food and medicine, spoke on their behalf, and they were released.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Administrator of Si province Sima Zhongcan and attendant official Lu Shipi were both beaten by Wen Xiang and handed to prison to be starved; Xian sent food and medicine, spoke on their behalf, and they were released.

sentences.zh: 自出身從官，常日晏乃歸。

translations.literal: From first entering office and serving, he regularly returned only at sunset.
translations.idiomatic: From first entering office, he regularly returned only at sunset.

sentences.zh: 侵曉則與兄弟跪問母之起居，暮則嘗食視寢，然後至外齋，對親賓論事，或與沙門辯玄理，夜久乃還寢。

translations.literal: At dawn he knelt with his brothers to inquire after their mother's comfort; at dusk he tasted food and observed her sleep, then went to the outer study, discussed affairs with kin and guests, or debated Buddhist principles with monks, returning to sleep only late at night.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, at dawn he knelt with his brothers to inquire after their mother's comfort; at dusk he tasted food and observed her sleep, then went to the outer study, discussed affairs with kin and guests, or debated Buddhist principles with monks, returning to sleep only late at night.

sentences.zh: 一生不問家產，魏、梁通和，要貴皆遣人隨聘使交易，暹唯寄求佛經。

translations.literal: All his life he never inquired about household property; when Wei and Liang made peace, the powerful and important all sent men to trade with the envoys—Xian only requested Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: All his life he never inquired about household property; when Wei and Liang made peace, the powerful all sent men to trade with the envoys—Xian only requested Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝聞之，繕寫，以幡花寶蓋贊唄送至館焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang heard of this, had them copied, and sent them to the embassy with banners, flowers, and precious canopies with praise and chanting.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, emperor Wu of Liang heard of this, had them copied, and sent them to the embassy with banners, flowers, and precious canopies with praise and chanting.

sentences.zh: 然好大言，調戲無節。

translations.literal: Yet he liked grand talk and jesting without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, yet he liked grand talk and jesting without restraint.

sentences.zh: 嘗密令沙門明藏著《佛論》而署己名，傳諸江表。

translations.literal: He once secretly ordered the monk Mingzang to compose a Foulun and affixed his own name, transmitting it to the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, he once secretly ordered the monk Mingzang to compose a Foulun and affixed his own name, transmitting it to the lands south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 子達拏，年十三，令儒者權會教其解《周易》兩字，乃集朝貴名流，命達拏高坐開講。

translations.literal: His son Dana, age thirteen, was ordered by Confucian Quan Hui to teach him to explain two words of the Book of Changes; he then gathered eminent court figures and ordered Dana to sit high and open lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, his son Dana, age thirteen, was ordered by Confucian Quan Hui to teach him to explain two words of the Book of Changes; he then gathered eminent court figures and ordered Dana to sit high and open lecture.

sentences.zh: 同郡眭仲讓陽屈服之，暹用仲讓為司徒中郎。

translations.literal: Suizhongrang of the same commandery pretended submission; Xian employed Zhongrang as Attendant of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, suizhongrang of the same commandery pretended submission; Xian employed Zhongrang as Attendant of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 鄴下為之語曰：「講義兩行得中郎。

translations.literal: In Ye capital they said of it: "Two lines of lecture win an Attendant post.
translations.idiomatic: In Ye capital they said, "Two lines of lecture win an Attendant post.

sentences.zh: 」仲讓官至右丞。

translations.literal: "Zhongrang reached the post of Right Director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrang reached the post of Right Director.

sentences.zh: 此皆暹之短也。

translations.literal: These were all Xian's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, these were all Xian's faults.

sentences.zh: 文宣初嗣霸業，司馬子如、韓軌等挾舊怨，言暹罪重。

translations.literal: At the beginning Wen Xuan succeeded to the hegemonic enterprise, Sima Ziru, Han Gui, and others, holding old resentments, said Xian's crimes were heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, at the beginning Wen Xuan succeeded to the hegemonic enterprise, Sima Ziru, Han Gui, and others, holding old resentments, said Xian's crimes were heavy.

sentences.zh: 高隆之亦言宜寬政網，去糾察法官，黜崔暹，則得遠近人意，文宣從之。

translations.literal: Gao Longzhi also said the legal net should be broadened, investigative judges removed, and Cui Xian dismissed—then near and far would be pleased; Wen Xuan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, gao Longzhi also said the legal net should be broadened, investigative judges removed, and Cui Xian dismissed—then near and far would be pleased; Wen Xuan followed this.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，譖毀者猶不息，帝令都督陳山提、舍人獨孤永業搜暹家。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, slander still did not cease; the emperor ordered Commander Chen Shanti and Attendant Dugu Yongye to search Xian's home.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, when he ascended the throne, slander still did not cease; the emperor ordered Commander Chen Shanti and Attendant Dugu Yongye to search Xian's home.

sentences.zh: 甚貧匱，得神武、文襄與暹書千餘紙，多論軍國大事。

translations.literal: It was very poor and destitute; they obtained more than a thousand sheets of letters from Gao Huan and Wen Xiang to Xian, mostly discussing military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: It was very poor; they obtained more than a thousand sheets of letters from Gao Huan and Wen Xiang to Xian, mostly discussing military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝嗟賞之。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, the emperor sighed and praised this.

sentences.zh: 仍不免眾口，流暹于馬城，晝則負土供役，夜則置諸地牢。

translations.literal: Still he could not escape public censure; Xian was exiled to Macheng, carrying earth by day for corvée and placed in a dungeon at night.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, still he could not escape public censure; Xian was exiled to Macheng, carrying earth by day for corvée and placed in a dungeon at night.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，奴告暹謀反，鎖赴晉陽，窮驗無實。

translations.literal: After more than a year a slave reported Xian plotted rebellion; he was chained and sent to Jinyang; exhaustive investigation found no truth.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, after more than a year a slave reported Xian plotted rebellion; he was chained and sent to Jinyang; exhaustive investigation found no truth.

sentences.zh: 先是，文襄疑文宣佯愚，慮其有後變，將陰圖之，以問暹。

translations.literal: Previously Wen Xiang suspected Wen Xuan feigned stupidity and feared he might later change; he planned to plot against him secretly and asked Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, previously Wen Xiang suspected Wen Xuan feigned stupidity and feared he might later change; he planned to plot against him secretly and asked Xian.

sentences.zh: 暹曰：「嘗與二郎俱在行位，試以手板拍其背而不瞋，乃將犀手板換暹竹者，自揩拭而玩視之，以是知其實癡。

translations.literal: Xian said: "I once stood in the same rank with the Second Lord; I tried slapping his back with a hand board and he did not grow angry; he then exchanged my bamboo board for a rhinoceros board, wiped it himself and examined it—thereby I knew he was truly simple.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "I once stood in the same rank with the Second Lord; I tried slapping his back with a hand board and he did not grow angry; he then exchanged my bamboo board for a rhinoceros board, wiped it himself and examined it—thereby I knew he was truly simple.

sentences.zh: 不足慮也。

translations.literal: Not worth worrying about.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, not worth worrying about.

sentences.zh: 」帝既鎖暹，責其往昔打背。

translations.literal: "When the emperor had chained Xian, he blamed him for the past blow to the back.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had chained Xian, he blamed him for the past blow to the back.

sentences.zh: 暹自陳所對文襄之言，明己功以贖死。

translations.literal: Xian himself stated what he had answered Wen Xiang, clarifying his merit to redeem death.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, xian himself stated what he had answered Wen Xiang, clarifying his merit to redeem death.

sentences.zh: 帝悟曰：「我免禍，乃暹之力。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and said: "I escaped calamity—it was Xian's power.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and said, "I escaped calamity—it was Xian's power.

sentences.zh: 」釋而勞之，使行太原郡事，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: "He released and comforted him, ordered him to conduct Taiyuan commandery affairs, and transferred him to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He released and comforted him, ordered him to conduct Taiyuan commandery affairs, and transferred him to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 謂群臣曰：「崔暹清正，天下無雙，卿等不及也。

translations.literal: He told the ministers: "Cui Xian is upright and pure—unmatched under Heaven; you cannot equal him.
translations.idiomatic: He told the ministers, "Cui Xian is upright and pure—unmatched under Heaven; you cannot equal him.

sentences.zh: 」初，文襄欲以最小妹嫁與暹子達拏，會崩，遂寢。

translations.literal: Initially Wen Xiang wished to marry his youngest sister to Xian's son Dana; when he died the matter was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, initially Wen Xiang wished to marry his youngest sister to Xian's son Dana; when he died the matter was suspended.

sentences.zh: 至是，宴于宣光殿，群臣多在焉，文宣謂暹曰：「賢子達拏甚有才學，亡兄長女樂安公主，魏帝外甥，勝朕諸妹，思成大兄宿志，故欲作婚姻。

translations.literal: At this time, banqueting at Xuanguang Hall with many ministers present, Wen Xuan said to Xian: "Your worthy son Dana has great talent and learning; the late brother's eldest daughter Princess Le'an, the Wei emperor's niece, surpasses my sisters; I think to fulfill the elder brother's longstanding wish, and therefore wish to make the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, banqueting at Xuanguang Hall with many ministers present, Wen Xuan said to Xian, "Your worthy son Dana has great talent; the late brother's eldest daughter Princess Le'an, the Wei emperor's niece, surpasses my sisters; I wish to fulfill the elder brother's longstanding wish and make the marriage.

sentences.zh: 」乃以主降達拏。

translations.literal: "He thereupon gave the princess in marriage to Dana.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the princess in marriage to Dana.

sentences.zh: 暹尋遷中書監，兼併省右僕射。

translations.literal: Xian was soon transferred to Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Right Vice Minister of the combined secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, xian was soon transferred to Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Right Vice Minister of the combined secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時法網已嚴，官司難於剖決，系獄者千餘人。

translations.literal: At the time the legal net was already strict and offices found it hard to decide; more than a thousand were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, at the time the legal net was already strict and offices found it hard to decide; more than a thousand were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 暹初上省，便大錄囚，旬月間，斷雪略盡。

translations.literal: When Xian first entered the ministry he at once greatly recorded prisoners; within ten days judgments were cleared almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, when Xian first entered the ministry he at once greatly recorded prisoners; within ten days judgments were cleared almost entirely.

sentences.zh: 文襄時欲封暹，神武亦欲封之，暹並固辭。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang at the time wished to enfeoff Xian; Gao Huan also wished to enfeoff him—Xian firmly declined both.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang wished to enfeoff Xian; Gao Huan also wished to enfeoff him—Xian firmly declined both.

sentences.zh: 文宣數出遊，多至暹宅，以暹女為皇太子妃，李後不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Wen Xuan often went out touring, often reaching Xian's residence; he wished to make Xian's daughter the crown prince's consort, but Empress Li would not allow it, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xuan often toured and often reached Xian's residence; he wished to make Xian's daughter the crown prince's consort, but Empress Li would not allow it, and it stopped.

sentences.zh: 天保八年，遷尚書右僕射、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao he was transferred to Right Vice Minister and Palace Attendant of the Third Order.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, in the eighth year of Tianbao he was transferred to Right Vice Minister and Palace Attendant of the Third Order.

sentences.zh: 時調絹以七丈為匹，暹言之，乃依舊焉。

translations.literal: At the time silk for tax was measured at seven zhang per bolt; Xian spoke of this and it returned to the old standard.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, at the time silk for tax was measured at seven zhang per bolt; Xian spoke of this and it returned to the old standard.

sentences.zh: 帝謂左右曰：「崔暹諫我餘酒過多，然我飲酒何所廢？

translations.literal: The emperor told those at his side: "Cui Xian remonstrates that I drink too much leftover wine—but what does my drinking harm?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told those at his side, "Cui Xian remonstrates that I drink too much—but what does my drinking harm?

sentences.zh: 」常山王私謂暹曰：「至尊威嚴多醉，太后尚不能致言，吾兄弟杜口。

translations.literal: "Prince of Changshan privately said to Xian: "His Majesty is often drunk and awesome; even the empress dowager cannot speak; we brothers keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changshan privately said to Xian, "His Majesty is often drunk and awesome; even the empress dowager cannot speak; we brothers keep silent.

sentences.zh: 僕射獨犯顏，內外深相感愧。

translations.literal: You alone, Vice Minister, offend his countenance—inside and outside we deeply feel gratitude and shame.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, you alone, Vice Minister, offend his countenance—inside and outside we deeply feel gratitude and shame.

sentences.zh: 」十年，卒，帝撫靈哭之，贈開府儀同三司、尚書左僕射、定州刺史，諡曰貞節。

translations.literal: "In the tenth year he died; the emperor stroked the bier and wept for him, posthumously granting him Grand General with an opening office of the Second Order, Left Vice Minister, and Governor of Ding province with the posthumous name Zhenjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died; the emperor stroked the bier and wept, posthumously granting him Grand General with an opening office of the Second Order, Left Vice Minister, and Governor of Ding province with the posthumous name Zhenjie.

sentences.zh: 達拏溫良廉謹，有識學。

translations.literal: Dana was gentle, good, modest, and careful, with discernment and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, dana was gentle, good, modest, and careful, with discernment and learning.

sentences.zh: 位儀同三司、司農卿，周禦府大夫。

translations.literal: He held the rank of Palace Attendant of the Third Order and Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and in Zhou was Grand Master of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, he held the rank of Palace Attendant of the Third Order and Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and in Zhou was Grand Master of the Imperial Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 大象中使鄴，屬尉遲迥起兵，以為總管司馬。

translations.literal: In the Elephant era he was sent to Ye; when Yu Chi Yong rose in arms he was made campaign chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, in the Elephant era he was sent to Ye; when Yu Chi Yong rose in arms he was made campaign chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 迥平，伏誅。

translations.literal: When Yong was pacified, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, when Yong was pacified, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 初，文宣嘗問樂安公主：「達拏于汝何似？

translations.literal: Initially Wen Xuan once asked Princess Le'an: "How does Dana compare to you?
translations.idiomatic: Initially Wen Xuan once asked Princess Le'an, "How does Dana compare to you?

sentences.zh: 」答云：「甚相敬，唯阿家憎兒。

translations.literal: "She answered: "He treats me with great respect—only his mother-in-law hates me.
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "He treats me with great respect—only his mother-in-law hates me.

sentences.zh: 」文宣令宮人召達拏母入而殺之，投漳水。

translations.literal: "Wen Xuan ordered palace women to summon Dana's mother in and kill her, throwing her into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xuan ordered palace women to summon Dana's mother in and kill her, throwing her into the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，達拏殺主以復仇。

translations.literal: When Qi was destroyed, Dana killed the princess to avenge his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, when Qi was destroyed, Dana killed the princess to avenge his mother.

sentences.zh: 暹兄謀開。

translations.literal: Xian's elder brother Moukai.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's elder brother was Moukai.

sentences.zh: 纂從祖弟游，字延叔，少有風概。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger male cousin You, styled Yanshu, had bearing and spirit from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger male cousin You, courtesy name Yanshu, had bearing and spirit from youth.

sentences.zh: 為東郡太守。

translations.literal: He was Administrator of Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, he was Administrator of Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡有鹽戶，常供州郡為兵，子孫見丁從役。

translations.literal: In the commandery were salt households who regularly supplied the province and commandery with corvée labor; descendants when registered for service followed conscription.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, in the commandery were salt households who regularly supplied the province and commandery with corvée labor; descendants when registered for service followed conscription.

sentences.zh: 矜其勞苦，乃為表聞，請聽更代，郡內感之。

translations.literal: Pitying their toil, he memorialized the court requesting rotation of service; within the commandery they were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, pitying their toil, he memorialized the court requesting rotation of service; within the commandery they were moved.

sentences.zh: 太學舊在城內，遊移置城南閑敞處，親自說經，當時學者莫不勸勉，號為良守。

translations.literal: The Imperial Academy had originally been within the city; You moved it to an open place south of the city, personally lectured on the classics, and scholars of the time were all encouraged—he was called a good administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy had originally been within the city; You moved it south to open ground, personally lectured on the classics, and scholars were all encouraged—he was called a good administrator.

sentences.zh: 正光中，除南秦州刺史。

translations.literal: During Zhengguang he was appointed Governor of Southern Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, during Zhengguang he was appointed Governor of Southern Qin province.

sentences.zh: 先是，州人楊松柏、洛德兄弟數為反叛，遊深加招慰，兄弟俱至。

translations.literal: Previously in the province Yang Songbai and Luo De and their brothers had repeatedly rebelled; You deeply recruited and reassured them and the brothers both came.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, previously in the province Yang Songbai and Luo De and their brothers had repeatedly rebelled; You deeply recruited and reassured them and the brothers both came.

sentences.zh: 松柏既郡之豪帥，感恩獎喻，郡賊咸來歸款，且以過在前政，不復自疑，遊乃因宴會，一時俱斬。

translations.literal: Since Songbai was the commandery's powerful chief, moved by gratitude and reward and instruction, commandery bandits all came to submit; moreover because the fault lay with the previous administration they no longer doubted themselves; You thereupon at a banquet killed them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Since Songbai was the commandery's powerful chief, moved by gratitude, commandery bandits all came to submit; because the fault lay with the previous administration they no longer doubted; You at a banquet killed them all at once.

sentences.zh: 於是外人以其不信，合境皆反。

translations.literal: Thereupon outsiders, because he was untrustworthy, rebelled throughout the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders, because he was untrustworthy, rebelled throughout the territory.

sentences.zh: 正光五年，秦州城人殺刺史李彥為逆。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengguang, Qin province city people killed Governor Li Yan in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, in the fifth year of Zhengguang, Qin province city people killed Governor Li Yan in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 數日後，遊知必不安，謀欲出外，尋為城人韓祖香等所攻。

translations.literal: Several days later You knew he could not remain secure and planned to go outside; soon he was attacked by city men Han Zuxiang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, several days later You knew he could not remain secure and planned to go outside; soon he was attacked by city men Han Zuxiang and others.

sentences.zh: 游事窘登樓，慷慨悲歎，乃推下小女而殺之，義不為群小所辱，為祖香等害。

translations.literal: You, pressed, ascended a tower and sighed with generous grief; he pushed down his young daughter and killed her—he would not be shamed by the mob—and was killed by Zuxiang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, you, pressed, ascended a tower and sighed with generous grief; he pushed down his young daughter and killed her—he would not be shamed by the mob—and was killed by Zuxiang and the others.

sentences.zh: 永安中，贈散騎常侍、鎮北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: During Yongan he was posthumously granted Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, during Yongan he was posthumously granted Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 子伏護。

translations.literal: His son Fuhu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Fuhu.

sentences.zh: 論曰：崔鑒以文業應利用之秋，世家有業，余慶不已，人位繼軌，亦為盛哉！

translations.literal: Commentary says: Cui Jian, with literary achievement responding to the season of opportunity, a family with established enterprise and blessings not exhausted, men and offices succeeding in succession—how flourishing!
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, commentary says: Cui Jian, with literary achievement responding to the season of opportunity, a family with established enterprise and blessings not exhausted, men and offices succeeding in succession—how flourishing!

sentences.zh: 辯器業著聞，位不遠到；

translations.literal: Bian's talent and achievement were renowned; his rank did not reach far;
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, bian's talent and achievement were renowned; his rank did not reach far;

sentences.zh: 逸德優官薄，仍世恨之。

translations.literal: Yi's virtue was excellent but his office thin—generations resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, yi's virtue was excellent but his office thin—generations resented it.

sentences.zh: 模雄壯之烈，楷忠貞之操，殺身成義，臨難如歸，非大丈夫亦何能若此矣！

translations.literal: Mo's heroic and strong valor, Kai's loyal and steadfast integrity—achieving righteousness by giving their lives, facing hardship as if returning home—if not great men, how could they be like this!
translations.idiomatic: Mo's heroic valor, Kai's loyal steadfast integrity—achieving righteousness by giving their lives, facing hardship as if returning home—if not great men, how could they be like this!

sentences.zh: 士謙昆弟非唯武毅見重，忠公之稱，亦足嘉云。

translations.literal: Shiqian and his brothers were valued not only for martial resolve; the title of loyal public servant is also worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, shiqian and his brothers were valued not only for martial resolve; the title of loyal public servant is also worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 挺兄弟風操高亮，懷文抱質，曆事著聞，見重朝野，繼世承家，門族並著，市朝可變，人焉不絕。

translations.literal: The Ting brothers' bearing and integrity were lofty; they embraced culture and possessed substance; serving through successive reigns they were renowned, valued by court and countryside; continuing the family across generations, the clan was illustrious—the marketplace may change, yet the men do not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, the Ting brothers' bearing and integrity were lofty; they embraced culture and possessed substance; serving through successive reigns they were renowned, valued by court and countryside; continuing the family across generations, the clan was illustrious—the marketplace may change, yet the men do not cease.

sentences.zh: 至若宣猷之立入朝贊務，則嘉謀屢陳，出撫宣條，則威恩具舉。

translations.literal: As for Xuanyou's establishing himself in court to assist in affairs, excellent plans were repeatedly offered; going out to govern, authority and kindness were both displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, as for Xuanyou's establishing himself in court to assist in affairs, excellent plans were repeatedly offered; going out to govern, authority and kindness were both displayed.

sentences.zh: 仲方之兼資文武，雅長謀算，伐陳之策，信為深遠。

translations.literal: Zhongfang's combined civil and military capacity, his elegant mastery of strategy—the plan for conquering Chen was truly far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, zhongfang's combined civil and military capacity, his elegant mastery of strategy—the plan for conquering Chen was truly far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 弈世載德，夫豈徒然？

translations.literal: Virtue carried across generations—could it be in vain?
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, virtue carried across generations—could it be in vain?

sentences.zh: 昂智足立功，能足幹事，霸朝委遇，良有以焉。

translations.literal: Ang's intelligence was sufficient to establish merit, his ability sufficient to manage affairs; the hegemonic court's entrustment and favor had good reason.
translations.idiomatic: Ang had the intelligence to establish merit and the ability to manage affairs; the hegemonic court's trust in him was well founded.

sentences.zh: 而謝彼仁心，安茲苛政，晚途遭躓，理其宜也。

translations.literal: Yet he abandoned that humane heart and accommodated this harsh governance; stumbling in his later course—this was according to reason.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he abandoned his humane heart and accommodated harsh governance; to stumble in his later course was only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 季舒蹈龍逢之節，季倫受分庭之遇，雖遭逢異日，得喪不同，考其遺跡，而榮名一也，蓋所謂彼有人焉。

translations.literal: Jishu tread the integrity of Long Feng; Jilun received the courtesy of facing each other across the hall—though they met different times and their gains and losses differed, examining their traces, their honored names are one; this is what is called 'there were men there.'
translations.idiomatic: Jishu upheld the integrity of Long Feng; Xian received the courtesy of facing his lord across the hall—though they lived in different times and met different fates, examining their traces, their honored names are one; this is what is meant by saying there were true men among them.
